[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[application](../index.html)::[crawler](index.html)



# Enum FetchRouter

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/crawler/fetch_router.rs.html#32-45" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum FetchRouter {
    Static(Arc<WreqDownloader>),
    Hybrid(Arc<HybridRouter<WreqDownloader, ObscuraDownloader, ChromiumoxideDownloader>>),
    Full(Arc<ChromiumoxideDownloader>, Arc<ResourceGovernor>),
}
```

Expand description



Type-erased fetch router that dispatches to the appropriate downloader based on the configured [`JsStrategy`](../../domain/js_strategy/enum.JsStrategy.html "enum webfang_core::domain::js_strategy::JsStrategy").

Implements [`Downloader`](../../infrastructure/downloader/trait.Downloader.html "trait webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::Downloader") so it can be passed as `&dyn Downloader` for runtime dispatch and test mocking. Inner types are `Arc`-wrapped so the router can be cheaply cloned into spawned tasks.



## Variants<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="#variant.Static" class="anchor">§</a>

### Static(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::sync::Arc">Arc</a>\<<a href="../../infrastructure/downloader/wreq_downloader/struct.WreqDownloader.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::wreq_downloader::WreqDownloader">WreqDownloader</a>\>)





Static HTTP only (wreq). Default.





<a href="#variant.Hybrid" class="anchor">§</a>

### Hybrid(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::sync::Arc">Arc</a>\<<a href="../../infrastructure/downloader/hybrid_router/struct.HybridRouter.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::hybrid_router::HybridRouter">HybridRouter</a>\<<a href="../../infrastructure/downloader/wreq_downloader/struct.WreqDownloader.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::wreq_downloader::WreqDownloader">WreqDownloader</a>, <a href="../../infrastructure/downloader/obscura_downloader/struct.ObscuraDownloader.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::obscura_downloader::ObscuraDownloader">ObscuraDownloader</a>, <a href="../../infrastructure/downloader/chromiumoxide_downloader/struct.ChromiumoxideDownloader.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::chromiumoxide_downloader::ChromiumoxideDownloader">ChromiumoxideDownloader</a>\>\>)





Hybrid 3-layer: wreq → Obscura → Chromiumoxide.





<a href="#variant.Full" class="anchor">§</a>

### Full(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::sync::Arc">Arc</a>\<<a href="../../infrastructure/downloader/chromiumoxide_downloader/struct.ChromiumoxideDownloader.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::chromiumoxide_downloader::ChromiumoxideDownloader">ChromiumoxideDownloader</a>\>, <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::sync::Arc">Arc</a>\<<a href="../../infrastructure/downloader/resource_governor/struct.ResourceGovernor.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::resource_governor::ResourceGovernor">ResourceGovernor</a>\>)





Chrome-direct rendering with RAM-aware concurrency gating.

Bypasses the wreq → Obscura escalation and renders every page in Chromiumoxide. A dedicated [`ResourceGovernor`](../../infrastructure/downloader/resource_governor/struct.ResourceGovernor.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::resource_governor::ResourceGovernor") checks system memory before each fetch and holds a semaphore permit for its duration, preventing OOM on large crawls. Both fields are `Arc`-wrapped so the router stays cheaply cloneable into spawned tasks.

# Function build_fetch_router

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/crawler/fetch_router.rs.html#65-99" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn build_fetch_router(
    strategy: &JsStrategy,
    timeout_secs: u64,
    tls_emulation: Profile,
    cookie_bridge: Arc<RwLock<CookieBridge>>,
    ignore_waf: bool,
    user_agent: Option<String>,
    cancel_token: CancellationToken,
) -> Result<FetchRouter, DownloadError>
```

Expand description



Build the [`FetchRouter`](enum.FetchRouter.html "enum webfang_core::application::crawler::FetchRouter") for a given JavaScript rendering strategy.

Single source of truth for the strategy → router mapping, shared by the crawl [`Engine`](engine/struct.Engine.html "struct webfang_core::application::crawler::engine::Engine") and the CLI scrape path. `timeout_secs` drives the wreq request timeout (connect timeout is clamped to 10s); `tls_emulation` is the TLS/HTTP2 fingerprint profile applied to the wreq layer; `cookie_bridge` is shared with the Chromiumoxide layer for cookie injection; `ignore_waf` bypasses WAF classification on the hybrid spa-detection path (REQ-WAF-07); `user_agent` pins the User-Agent on the wreq layer (Static and Hybrid L1) so `--user-agent` reaches the wire — `None` keeps the emulation-default + 403-rotation behavior (#503); `cancel_token` is injected into the Full strategy’s [`ResourceGovernor`](../../infrastructure/downloader/resource_governor/struct.ResourceGovernor.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::resource_governor::ResourceGovernor") so permit waits abort on shutdown (#509) — pass an inert token where no cancellation policy exists.

## <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`DownloadError::Internal`](../../infrastructure/downloader/enum.DownloadError.html#variant.Internal "variant webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::DownloadError::Internal") if the wreq client cannot be built.

Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left` is `true`. where F: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html" class="trait" title="trait core::ops::function::FnOnce">FnOnce</a>(&Self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>,







Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left(&self)` returns `true`. Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right "variant either::Either::Right") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") otherwise. [webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[application](../../index.html)::[crawler](../index.html)::[sitemap_discovery](index.html)



# Function crawl_with_sitemap

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/application/crawler/sitemap_discovery.rs.html#57-63" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub async fn crawl_with_sitemap(
    base_url: &str,
    sitemap_url: Option<&str>,
    config: &CrawlerConfig,
) -> Result<Vec<DiscoveredUrl>, CrawlError>
```

Expand description



Crawl site using sitemap (preferred method - FASE 3)

Following **own-borrow-over-clone**: Accepts `&str` not `&String`. Following **api-builder-pattern**: Uses SitemapConfig builder.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `base_url` - Base URL of the website
- `sitemap_url` - Optional explicit sitemap URL (auto-discovers if None)
- `config` - Crawler configuration

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

- `Ok(Vec<DiscoveredUrl>)` - URLs discovered from sitemap
- `Err(CrawlError)` - Error during sitemap fetch or parse

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::application::crawl_with_sitemap;
use webfang_core::domain::CrawlerConfig;
use url::Url;

let seed = Url::parse("https://example.com")?;
let config = CrawlerConfig::new(seed);

let urls = crawl_with_sitemap("https://example.com", None, &config).await?;
println!("Found {} URLs from sitemap", urls.len());
```
















[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[application](../index.html)::[deduplicator](index.html)



# Struct UrlDeduplicator

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/deduplicator.rs.html#53-56" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct UrlDeduplicator { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Lock-free URL deduplicator.

Stores a `u64` hash (8 bytes) per seen URL rather than the full string. Dedup is atomic: `try_insert` performs a single `DashSet::insert` (check-and-insert in one step), so concurrent callers cannot race past each other.

The hash seed is randomized per process startup (`RandomState::new()`, satisfying FR-3) yet stable for the deduplicator’s lifetime, so the same URL always maps to the same `u64` within one process (FR-5).

URLs are normalized to a canonical form before hashing (#517), so equivalent spellings of the same document deduplicate as one key.

## <a href="#example" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Example



``` rust
use webfang_core::application::deduplicator::UrlDeduplicator;

let dedup = UrlDeduplicator::new();
assert!(dedup.try_insert("https://example.com"));   // newly inserted
assert!(!dedup.try_insert("https://example.com"));  // already seen
assert_eq!(dedup.len(), 1);
```

#### pub fn <a href="#method.new" class="fn">new</a>() -\> Self





Create a new deduplicator with a fresh per-process randomized seed.

Pre-allocates capacity for ~100 URLs (mem-with-capacity).





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/deduplicator.rs.html#82-85" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.try_insert" class="fn">try_insert</a>(&self, url: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>





Atomically check-and-insert a URL.

Returns `true` if the URL was newly inserted, `false` if it was already present. This is a single lock-free `DashSet::insert` — no `Mutex`, no `.await` — so it is safe to call from many Tokio tasks concurrently (FR-8) without data races or lost updates.

The URL is normalized via the canonical domain normalizer before hashing (#517), so `https://www.example.com/page` and `https://example.com/page#top` collide on one key.

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[application](../index.html)::[elastic_ingestion](index.html)



# Struct BatchResult

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/elastic_ingestion.rs.html#369-376" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct BatchResult {
    pub success: usize,
    pub errors: Vec<ScraperError>,
    pub panics: usize,
}
```

Expand description



Aggregate result of a batch ingestion run via [`ElasticIngestion::ingest_batch`](struct.ElasticIngestion.html#method.ingest_batch "method webfang_core::application::elastic_ingestion::ElasticIngestion::ingest_batch").

Collects successes, errors, and panics from concurrent URL processing. Uses a collect-all strategy (not fail-fast): every URL is attempted regardless of individual failures.



## Fields<a href="#fields" class="anchor">§</a>

<a href="#structfield.success" class="anchor field">§</a>`success: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.usize.html" class="primitive"><code>usize</code></a>

<a href="#structfield.errors" class="anchor field">§</a>`errors: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec"><code>Vec</code></a>`<`<a href="../../error/enum.ScraperError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError"><code>ScraperError</code></a>`>`

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[application](../index.html)::[elastic_ingestion](index.html)



# Struct ElasticIngestion

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/elastic_ingestion.rs.html#55-72" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct ElasticIngestion<R: VectorRepository + Send + Sync> { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Elastic ingestion pipeline orchestrator (frozen Decision 1).

Generic over the [`VectorRepository`](../../domain/repository/trait.VectorRepository.html "trait webfang_core::domain::repository::VectorRepository") trait and monomorphized at compile time, so the repo’s native `async fn` methods are awaited inline without `Box<dyn Future>` or `dyn` dispatch.

Construct with [`ElasticIngestion::new`](struct.ElasticIngestion.html#method.new "associated function webfang_core::application::elastic_ingestion::ElasticIngestion::new"); optionally inject an ONNX [`SemanticCleaner`](../../domain/semantic_cleaner/trait.SemanticCleaner.html "trait webfang_core::domain::semantic_cleaner::SemanticCleaner") under the `ai` feature via [`ElasticIngestion::with_cleaner`](struct.ElasticIngestion.html#method.with_cleaner "method webfang_core::application::elastic_ingestion::ElasticIngestion::with_cleaner") (frozen Decision 5).



## Implementations<a href="#implementations" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/elastic_ingestion.rs.html#74-360" class="src rightside">Source</a><a href="#impl-ElasticIngestion%3CR%3E" class="anchor">§</a>

### impl\<R: <a href="../../domain/repository/trait.VectorRepository.html" class="trait" title="trait webfang_core::domain::repository::VectorRepository">VectorRepository</a> + <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Send.html" class="trait" title="trait core::marker::Send">Send</a> + <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Sync.html" class="trait" title="trait core::marker::Sync">Sync</a>\> <a href="struct.ElasticIngestion.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::application::elastic_ingestion::ElasticIngestion">ElasticIngestion</a>\<R\>







<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/elastic_ingestion.rs.html#82-96" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.new" class="fn">new</a>( downloader: <a href="../../infrastructure/crawler/resource_downloader/struct.ResourceDownloader.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::crawler::resource_downloader::ResourceDownloader">ResourceDownloader</a>, bridge: <a href="../../infrastructure/bridge/struct.CpuBridge.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::bridge::CpuBridge">CpuBridge</a>, repository: R, config: <a href="../../infrastructure/config/struct.AutotuningConfig.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::config::AutotuningConfig">AutotuningConfig</a>, ) -\> Self





Wire the four pipeline components (frozen Decision 1: monomorphization).

The repository is generic and monomorphized at compile time. Since [`ingest_batch`](struct.ElasticIngestion.html#method.ingest_batch "method webfang_core::application::elastic_ingestion::ElasticIngestion::ingest_batch") uses `buffer_unordered` (cooperative concurrency on the current task), the repository is borrowed by `&self` across all futures — no `Arc` sharing is needed.





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/elastic_ingestion.rs.html#108-114" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.with_cleaner" class="fn">with_cleaner</a>(self, cleaner: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::sync::Arc">Arc</a>\<dyn <a href="../../domain/semantic_cleaner/trait.SemanticCleaner.html" class="trait" title="trait webfang_core::domain::semantic_cleaner::SemanticCleaner">SemanticCleaner</a>\>) -\> Self





Inject an ONNX [`SemanticCleaner`](../../domain/semantic_cleaner/trait.SemanticCleaner.html "trait webfang_core::domain::semantic_cleaner::SemanticCleaner") for embedding generation (Decision 5).

When set, [`run`](struct.ElasticIngestion.html#method.run "method webfang_core::application::elastic_ingestion::ElasticIngestion::run") routes HTML through the cleaner’s async `clean()` (HTML chunking + 384-dim embeddings) instead of the bridge’s sync `lol_html` text extraction. `SemanticCleaner::clean()` is async, so it cannot run in the sync Rayon bridge closure and must live here.





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/elastic_ingestion.rs.html#126-159" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub async fn <a href="#method.run" class="fn">run</a>(&self, url: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.unit.html" class="primitive">()</a>, <a href="../../error/enum.ScraperError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError">ScraperError</a>\>





Run the full 7-layer pipeline for a single URL (frozen Decision 2).

Fail-fast (Decision 3): no internal retries/sleep. Network and CPU errors propagate immediately after logging; `PermitGuard` RAII (inside the downloader) releases byte-weighted permits on every path.

##### <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`ScraperError`](../../error/enum.ScraperError.html "enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError") on network failure, CPU panic, or persistence failure.





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/elastic_ingestion.rs.html#255-286" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub async fn <a href="#method.ingest_batch" class="fn">ingest_batch</a>( &self, urls: &\[<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>\], ) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="struct.BatchResult.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::application::elastic_ingestion::BatchResult">BatchResult</a>, <a href="../../error/enum.ScraperError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError">ScraperError</a>\>





Process multiple URLs concurrently using `buffer_unordered` (Issue \#124).

Concurrency is bounded by `self.config.cpu_cores` — at most that many futures are polled simultaneously, which IS the backpressure mechanism (no unbounded queue growth). Uses a collect-all error strategy: every URL is attempted regardless of individual failures.

Panics from individual futures are caught per-future via `catch_unwind` + `AssertUnwindSafe` and counted separately in [`BatchResult::panics`](struct.BatchResult.html#structfield.panics "field webfang_core::application::elastic_ingestion::BatchResult::panics").

##### <a href="#results" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Results

Returns `Ok(BatchResult)` aggregating successes, errors, and panics. Individual URL failures are captured in [`BatchResult::errors`](struct.BatchResult.html#structfield.errors "field webfang_core::application::elastic_ingestion::BatchResult::errors"); systemic failures (e.g. infrastructure collapse) return `Err(ScraperError)`. Inspect the fields to decide whether the batch met your quality bar.

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[application](../index.html)::[extraction](index.html)



# Function extract_content

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/extraction.rs.html#227-336" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub async fn extract_content(
    html: &str,
    url: &Url,
    config: &ScraperConfig,
    asset_downloader: Option<&dyn AssetDownloaderPort>,
    engine: Option<&AdaptiveSelectorEngine>,
    correlation_id: &CorrelationId,
) -> Result<ScrapedContent>
```

Expand description



Pipeline de extracción de contenido: clean → selector → adaptive → readability/fallback.

Recibe HTML ya fetchado y validado (post-WAF). No conoce el transporte.

Correlation identity (#501): the per-page identity is a REQUIRED input — callers own it (e.g. `scrape_single_url_for_tui` declares it on its trace span) and inject it here so the exported content shares the same identity as the page’s `span_fields` in the `--trace-file` JSONL. Standalone callers mint their own root at entry. Identity enters through the type system or not at all — there is no ad-hoc fallback.

## <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`ScraperError::ExtractionFailed`](../../error/enum.ScraperError.html#variant.ExtractionFailed "variant webfang_core::error::ScraperError::ExtractionFailed") when fallback content is below `MIN_FALLBACK_CONTENT` bytes.

# Function extract_with_selector

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/extraction.rs.html#38-101" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn extract_with_selector(
    html: &str,
    selector: &str,
    inspector: Option<&dyn DomInspectorPort>,
) -> ExtractResult
```

Expand description



Extract HTML content using a CSS selector.

When `selector` is not “body”, parses the HTML and extracts all elements matching the selector. Returns the outer HTML of matched elements wrapped in a `` for Readability processing. If no elements match or the selector is invalid, returns [`ExtractResult::Fallback`](../../domain/dom_inspector/enum.ExtractResult.html#variant.Fallback "variant webfang_core::domain::dom_inspector::ExtractResult::Fallback") with the full HTML and an optional diagnostic (when an inspector is provided).

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `html` - The HTML document to extract from
- `selector` - CSS selector string (use `"body"` to skip extraction)
- `inspector` - Optional DOM inspector for diagnostics on failure paths

# Function scrape_with_readability

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/extraction.rs.html#139-157" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub async fn scrape_with_readability(
    client: &dyn HttpClientPort,
    url: &Url,
) -> Result<Vec<ScrapedContent>>
```

Expand description



Scrape a URL using Readability algorithm for clean content extraction

This is the 2026 best practice approach — uses the same algorithm as Firefox Reader View to extract only meaningful content.

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::application::{create_http_client, scrape_with_readability};

let client = create_http_client()?;
let url = url::Url::parse("https://example.com")?;
let results = scrape_with_readability(&client, &url).await?;
```

# Function create_http_client

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/http_client/factory.rs.html#142-144" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn create_http_client() -> Result<Client, ScraperError>
```

Expand description



Create configured HTTP client

Equivalent to `create_http_client_with_config(&HttpClientConfig::default())`: a Chrome145 client with a random pooled user agent, a 30s request timeout, and a 10s connect timeout, plus the Chrome Client Hints default headers. For more control, use `HttpClient::new()` with `HttpClientConfig`.














[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[application](../index.html)::[http_client](index.html)



# Function create_http_client_with_config

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/http_client/factory.rs.html#124-133" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn create_http_client_with_config(
    config: &HttpClientConfig,
) -> Result<Client, ScraperError>
```

Expand description



Create a bare `wreq::Client` that honors the given domain config.

This is the config-driven counterpart of `HttpClient::new`: it returns the raw inner client (no retry middleware) for callers that manage requests themselves, while still applying the Chrome Client Hints headers, the resolved H2/TLS profile, request/connect timeouts, and pool tuning from `config`.

User-agent resolution: `config.user_agent` is used when set; otherwise a random agent is drawn from the fallback pool, preserving the historical rotation behavior of `create_http_client`.

## <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns `ScraperError::Config` if the underlying client fails to build.

# Struct HttpClient

Expand description



HTTP client wrapper with configurable retry behavior

Wraps `wreq::Client` and adds:

- Custom headers from config
- Status-specific retry logic
- User-agent rotation on 403
- Exponential backoff on 429 and 5xx
- Request timeout configuration
- Rate limiting
- URL validation
- TLS fingerprint rotation
- Request timeout configuration
- Rate limiting
- URL validation
- TLS fingerprint rotation

#### pub async fn <a href="#method.get" class="fn">get</a>(&self, url: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>) -\> <a href="../../domain/http_error/type.HttpResult.html" class="type" title="type webfang_core::domain::http_error::HttpResult">HttpResult</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>\>





Perform GET request with retry logic

Handles status codes as follows:

- 200-299: Returns body as String
- 403: Logs + retries once with rotated user-agent
- 429: Exponential backoff respecting Retry-After header
- 500-599: Exponential backoff with automatic retry

## Trait Implementations<a href="#trait-implementations" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/http_client/client.rs.html#460-507" class="src rightside">Source</a><a href="#impl-HttpClientPort-for-HttpClient" class="anchor">§</a>

### impl <a href="../../domain/http_port/trait.HttpClientPort.html" class="trait" title="trait webfang_core::domain::http_port::HttpClientPort">HttpClientPort</a> for <a href="struct.HttpClient.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::application::http_client::HttpClient">HttpClient</a>



Raw, single-shot [`HttpClientPort`](../../domain/http_port/trait.HttpClientPort.html "trait webfang_core::domain::http_port::HttpClientPort") implementation for [`HttpClient`](struct.HttpClient.html "struct webfang_core::application::http_client::HttpClient").







#### <a href="#why-this-path-is-deliberately-raw" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Why this path is deliberately raw

[`HttpClient`](struct.HttpClient.html "struct webfang_core::application::http_client::HttpClient") exposes two request paths with different contracts, and they are intentionally **not** unified:

- The hardened path — `HttpClient::get` / `get_inner` — returns only the response body as a `String`, after applying rate limiting, per-domain session gating, status-specific retries (429 / 5xx), user-agent rotation on 403, and WAF/CAPTCHA inspection. Non-2xx outcomes are surfaced as [`HttpError`](../../domain/http_error/enum.HttpError.html "enum webfang_core::domain::http_error::HttpError") variants.
- This port implementation returns a full [`HttpResponse`](../../domain/http_port/struct.HttpResponse.html "struct webfang_core::domain::http_port::HttpResponse") (`status` + `headers` + `body`) for a **single** GET with no retry, no user-agent rotation and no WAF inspection, reporting non-2xx as data in `status` rather than as an error. It exists for callers that depend on the domain port and manage their own request lifecycle.

Routing this impl through the hardened path would change its observable behavior — it would start retrying, rotating user agents, and turning 5xx/429 responses into [`HttpError`](../../domain/http_error/enum.HttpError.html "enum webfang_core::domain::http_error::HttpError")s instead of returning the status — so the divergence is preserved and documented here rather than collapsed (see \#444). The bare-client factories (e.g. [`create_http_client`](fn.create_http_client.html "fn webfang_core::application::http_client::create_http_client")) are raw for the same reason.

# Struct JsonlOutputStage

<a href="../../../../../src/webfang_core/application/pipeline/stages/jsonl_output.rs.html#17-20" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct JsonlOutputStage { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Output stage that writes [`ScrapedItem`](../../../../domain/pipeline_item/struct.ScrapedItem.html "struct webfang_core::domain::pipeline_item::ScrapedItem")s as JSONL (JSON Lines) to a file.

Each item is serialized as a single JSON object on its own line. The file is opened in append mode so existing content is preserved.

# Struct MultiSinkOutput

<a href="../../../../../src/webfang_core/application/pipeline/stages/multi_sink.rs.html#13-15" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct MultiSinkOutput { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Output stage that writes to all inner sinks sequentially.

If a sink fails, the error is logged and remaining sinks are still attempted. Returns `Ok(())` if at least one sink succeeds, or the first error if all fail.

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[application](../../index.html)::[pipeline](../index.html)::[stages](index.html)



# Struct CleanStage

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/application/pipeline/stages/clean.rs.html#39" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct CleanStage(pub Box<dyn ContentProcessor>);
```

Expand description



Pipeline stage that cleans raw HTML into readable text.

Delegates to a [`ContentProcessor`](../../../domain/content_processor/trait.ContentProcessor.html "trait webfang_core::domain::content_processor::ContentProcessor") strategy (e.g. [`SemanticProcessor`](../../../infrastructure/content_processing/semantic/struct.SemanticProcessor.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::content_processing::semantic::SemanticProcessor")) for the actual HTML-to-text conversion, then populates metadata (reduction percentage, SPA detection).

## <a href="#metadata-produced" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Metadata produced



| Key             | Value                                |
|-----------------|--------------------------------------|
| `original_size` | Byte length of raw_html              |
| `cleaned_size`  | Byte length of extracted text        |
| `reduction_pct` | Percentage reduction (0–100)         |
| `potential_spa` | `"true"` if cleaned text \< 50 chars |

# Struct ValidateStage

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/application/pipeline/stages/validate.rs.html#29" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct ValidateStage;
```

Expand description



Pipeline stage that validates scraped items for basic correctness.

## <a href="#validation-rules" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Validation rules

- **URL validity**: must be non-empty, parseable, with http(s) scheme
- **Status code**: must be in 200..=399
- **Content length**: raw_html must be non-empty
- **Skip patterns**: robots.txt, sitemap.xml, and similar non-content pages are silently skipped

# Struct PipelineExecutor

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/pipeline/executor.rs.html#8-10" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct PipelineExecutor { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Executes a sequence of [`PipelineStage`](../../domain/pipeline_item/trait.PipelineStage.html "trait webfang_core::domain::pipeline_item::PipelineStage")s on [`ScrapedItem`](../../domain/pipeline_item/struct.ScrapedItem.html "struct webfang_core::domain::pipeline_item::ScrapedItem")s.

Stages are processed in insertion order. The first stage to return [`StageOutcome::Skip`](../../domain/pipeline_item/enum.StageOutcome.html#variant.Skip "variant webfang_core::domain::pipeline_item::StageOutcome::Skip") or [`StageOutcome::Reject`](../../domain/pipeline_item/enum.StageOutcome.html#variant.Reject "variant webfang_core::domain::pipeline_item::StageOutcome::Reject") short-circuits the pipeline.

Run all stages on `item` in order.

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[application](../index.html)::[progress_observer](index.html)



# Struct LiveProgressObserver

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/progress_observer.rs.html#15-18" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct LiveProgressObserver { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Live observer that forwards events through an optional `UnboundedSender`.

When `tx` is `Some`, events are sent through the channel. When `tx` is `None` (non-TUI mode), events are written to stderr. When `quiet` is `true`, all methods become no-ops.

# Struct RateLimitCancelled

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/rate_limiter.rs.html#63" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct RateLimitCancelled;
```

Expand description



A rate-limit wait was cancelled before a permit was granted (#509).

Control signal, not an operational failure: the engine’s cancellation token fired while the task waited for a token-bucket permit.

#### pub async fn <a href="#method.until_ready_or_cancel" class="fn">until_ready_or_cancel</a>( &self, cancel: &CancellationToken, ) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.unit.html" class="primitive">()</a>, <a href="struct.RateLimitCancelled.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::application::rate_limiter::RateLimitCancelled">RateLimitCancelled</a>\>





Wait until a permit is available, abandoning the wait if `cancel` fires first (#509).

Dropping the pending governor future consumes no token, so a cancelled caller leaves the bucket untouched for the next task.

##### <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`RateLimitCancelled`](struct.RateLimitCancelled.html "struct webfang_core::application::rate_limiter::RateLimitCancelled") when the token fires before a permit is granted.

Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left` is `true`. where F: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html" class="trait" title="trait core::ops::function::FnOnce">FnOnce</a>(&Self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>,







Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left(&self)` returns `true`. Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right "variant either::Either::Right") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") otherwise. [Read more](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/into_either/trait.IntoEither.html#method.into_either_with)

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[application](../index.html)::[scraper_service](index.html)



# Function scrape_multiple_with_limit

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/scraper_service.rs.html#453-506" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub async fn scrape_multiple_with_limit(
    client: &dyn HttpClientPort,
    urls: &[Url],
    config: &ScraperConfig,
    downloader: Option<&dyn AssetDownloaderPort>,
) -> Result<Vec<ScrapedContent>>
```

Expand description



Scrape multiple URLs with concurrency control

Uses `buffer_unordered` to limit concurrent requests, preventing:

- File descriptor exhaustion
- HDD thrashing (for systems with mechanical drives)
- Anti-bot detection (DDoS-like patterns)

Following **config-externalize**: Concurrency is configurable via ScraperConfig. Following **async-concurrency-limit**: Uses buffer_unordered for concurrency control.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `client` - HTTP client
- `urls` - URLs to scrape
- `config` - Scraper configuration

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

- `Vec<ScrapedContent>` - All successfully scraped content

## <a href="#note" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Note

Failed URLs are logged but don’t stop the entire batch.














[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[application](../index.html)::[scraper_service](index.html)



# Function scrape_with_config

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/scraper_service.rs.html#89-111" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub async fn scrape_with_config(
    client: &dyn HttpClientPort,
    url: &Url,
    config: &ScraperConfig,
    downloader: Option<&dyn AssetDownloaderPort>,
    inspector: Option<&dyn DomInspectorPort>,
    engine: Option<&AdaptiveSelectorEngine>,
    root_correlation: &CorrelationId,
) -> Result<ScrapeOutcome>
```

Expand description



Scrape a URL with asset downloading configuration

Correlation contract (#501): the caller owns the run-root identity (`root_correlation`); this use case derives one page child from it (same `trace_id`, fresh `span_id`) so every page of the operation stays reconstructable under a single trace while each page is distinguishable.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `client` - HTTP client
- `url` - URL to scrape
- `config` - Scraper configuration with download options
- `downloader` - Optional asset downloader
- `inspector` - Optional DOM inspector for selector diagnostics (None for non-MCP paths)
- `root_correlation` - Run-root correlation identity of the enclosing operation

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

- `ScrapeOutcome` - Scraped content results + CSS selector extraction result

## <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns `ScraperError::Http` for HTTP errors, `ScraperError::Network` for connection errors.














[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[application](../index.html)::[scraper_service](index.html)



# Struct ScrapeOutcome

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/scraper_service.rs.html#53-58" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct ScrapeOutcome {
    pub results: Vec<ScrapedContent>,
    pub extract_result: ExtractResult,
}
```

Expand description



Outcome of a scrape operation, including selector extraction metadata.

Contains both the scraped content results and the [`ExtractResult`](../../domain/dom_inspector/enum.ExtractResult.html "enum webfang_core::domain::dom_inspector::ExtractResult") from CSS selector extraction, allowing callers (e.g. the MCP handler) to inspect whether the selector matched and access diagnostics.

# Constant MIN_CONTENT_CHARS

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/spa_detection.rs.html#9" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub const MIN_CONTENT_CHARS: usize = 50;
```

Expand description



Minimum character threshold for considering content “substantial”. Pages below this threshold after extraction likely require JS rendering.














[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[application](../index.html)::[spa_detection](index.html)



# Function detect_spa_content

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/spa_detection.rs.html#46-66" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn detect_spa_content(
    url: &str,
    text_content: &str,
    raw_html: &str,
) -> Option<SpaDetectionResult>
```

Expand description



Detect whether a page likely requires JavaScript rendering (SPA detection).

Analyzes extracted content to identify pages that returned minimal content after readability/fallback extraction, which is a common symptom of Single Page Applications that render client-side.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `url` - The URL that was scraped
- `text_content` - The extracted text content (used for char count threshold)
- `raw_html` - The raw HTML source (used for SPA marker detection)

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

- `Some(SpaDetectionResult)` if the page appears to be an SPA
- `None` if the content appears substantial enough

## <a href="#detection-heuristics" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Detection Heuristics

A page is flagged as potentially SPA-dependent when:

- Extracted content is below `MIN_CONTENT_CHARS` (50 chars)

# Function resolve_title

``` rust
pub fn resolve_title(extracted_title: &str, url: &Url) -> String
```

Expand description



Resolve a possibly-empty extracted title to a guaranteed-non-empty string.

- Empty/whitespace-only input → `Document: [<host>]` (or `Document: [unknown_host]`).
- Non-empty input → returned unchanged (trim-for-check only; `validate()` trims downstream).














[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[application](../index.html)::[url_filter](index.html)



# Function extract_domain

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/url_filter.rs.html#183-185" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn extract_domain(url: &str) -> Option<String>
```

Expand description



Extract domain from URL using url crate (RFC 3986 compliant)

Following **url-no-string-split**: Uses `url::Url::parse().host_str()` instead of string splitting for proper RFC 3986 compliance.

Handles:

- Credentials: `http://user:pass@domain.com` → `domain.com`
- Ports: `https://domain.com:8080/path` → `domain.com`
- IPv6: `http://[::1]:8080` → `[::1]`

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `url` - URL to extract domain from

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

Domain string or None if URL is invalid

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::application::url_filter::extract_domain;

assert_eq!(extract_domain("https://example.com/page"), Some("example.com".to_string()));
assert_eq!(extract_domain("https://blog.example.com/post"), Some("blog.example.com".to_string()));
assert_eq!(extract_domain("http://user:pass@domain.com:8080/path"), Some("domain.com".to_string()));
assert_eq!(extract_domain("http://[::1]:8080"), Some("[::1]".to_string()));
```
















[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[application](../index.html)::[url_filter](index.html)



# Function is_allowed

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/url_filter.rs.html#130-151" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn is_allowed(url: &str, config: &CrawlerConfig) -> bool
```

Expand description



Check if a URL is allowed based on the crawler configuration

Following **own-borrow-over-clone**: Accepts `&CrawlerConfig` reference.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `url` - URL to test
- `config` - Crawler configuration with include/exclude patterns

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

`true` if the URL is allowed (matches include and doesn’t match exclude)

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::{application::url_filter::is_allowed, domain::CrawlerConfig};
use url::Url;

let seed = Url::parse("https://example.com").unwrap();
let config = CrawlerConfig::builder(seed)
    // Match both root domain AND subdomains
    .include_pattern("example.com".to_string())
    .include_pattern("*.example.com/*".to_string())
    // Exclude both root domain AND subdomains
    .exclude_pattern("evil.com".to_string())
    .exclude_pattern("*.evil.com".to_string())
    .build();

assert!(is_allowed("https://example.com/page", &config));
assert!(is_allowed("https://blog.example.com/post", &config));
assert!(!is_allowed("https://evil.com/page", &config));
assert!(!is_allowed("https://blog.evil.com/admin", &config));
assert!(!is_allowed("https://other.com/page", &config));
```
















[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[application](../index.html)::[url_filter](index.html)



# Function is_excluded

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/url_filter.rs.html#89-91" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn is_excluded(url: &str, patterns: &[String]) -> bool
```

Expand description



Check if a URL is excluded by any of the exclude patterns

Following **own-borrow-over-clone**: Accepts `&[String]` not `&Vec<String>`. Following **opt-inline**: Inlined for hot path performance.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `url` - URL to test
- `patterns` - Slice of exclude patterns

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

`true` if the URL matches any exclude pattern

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::application::url_filter::is_excluded;

// To exclude both root domain AND subdomains, need both patterns
let patterns = vec![
    "evil.com".to_string(),
    "*.evil.com".to_string(),
    "malicious.com".to_string(),
    "*.malicious.com".to_string(),
];
assert!(is_excluded("https://evil.com/page", &patterns));
assert!(is_excluded("https://blog.evil.com/admin", &patterns));
assert!(!is_excluded("https://example.com/page", &patterns));
```

``` rust
pub fn is_internal_link(url: &str, seed_domain: &str) -> bool
```

Expand description



Check if a URL is internal (same domain as seed)

Following **own-borrow-over-clone**: Accepts `&str` for both parameters.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `url` - URL to check
- `seed_domain` - Domain of the seed URL

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

`true` if the URL belongs to the same domain

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples

``` rust
use webfang_core::application::url_filter::is_internal_link;

assert!(is_internal_link("https://example.com/page", "example.com"));
```

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[application](../index.html)::[url_filter](index.html)



# Function matches_pattern

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/url_filter.rs.html#52-55" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn matches_pattern(url: &str, pattern: &str) -> bool
```

Expand description



Check if a URL matches a glob-style pattern (dual-mode)

Two modes depending on whether the pattern starts with `/`:

- **Path pattern** (starts with `/`): matched against the URL path component. Example: `/pricing`, `/admin/*`, `/api/v2/*`
- **Host-only pattern** (no leading `/`): matched against the parsed hostname. Example: `example.com`, `*.example.com`, `*.example.com/*`

Following **own-borrow-over-clone**: Accepts `&str` not `&String`. Following **opt-inline**: Inlined for hot path performance. Following **security-ssrf-prevention**: Delegates to domain implementation (SSRF-safe).

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `url` - URL to test
- `pattern` - Glob-style pattern (\* for wildcard)

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

`true` if the URL matches the pattern

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::application::url_filter::matches_pattern;

assert!(matches_pattern("https://example.com/page", "*"));
assert!(matches_pattern("https://example.com/pricing", "/pricing"));
assert!(matches_pattern("https://blog.example.com/post", "*.example.com"));
assert!(!matches_pattern("https://other.com/page", "example.com"));
```

# Struct VaultSearchService

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/vault_search.rs.html#65-69" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct VaultSearchService { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Semantic search service for Obsidian vault notes.

Orchestrates domain ports to provide:

- **Search**: embed query → load indexed vectors → rank → top-N
- **Indexing**: chunk markdown → embed chunks → persist

Construct with [`VaultSearchService::new`](struct.VaultSearchService.html#method.new "associated function webfang_core::application::vault_search::VaultSearchService::new"); all dependencies are injected as `Arc<dyn Port>` for testability.

Wire the three pipeline components.





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/vault_search.rs.html#99-155" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub async fn <a href="#method.search" class="fn">search</a>( &self, query: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>, limit: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.usize.html" class="primitive">usize</a>, ) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>\<<a href="struct.VaultSearchResult.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::application::vault_search::VaultSearchResult">VaultSearchResult</a>\>, <a href="../../error/enum.ScraperError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError">ScraperError</a>\>





Search the vault index for notes matching the query.

##### <a href="#pipeline" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Pipeline

1.  Embed the query text via [`EmbeddingPort`](../../domain/embedding_port/trait.EmbeddingPort.html "trait webfang_core::domain::embedding_port::EmbeddingPort")
2.  Load all indexed chunk vectors via [`NoteRepository`](../../domain/note_repository/trait.NoteRepository.html "trait webfang_core::domain::note_repository::NoteRepository")
3.  Rank by cosine similarity (SIMD-friendly, inline implementation)
4.  Return top-`limit` results sorted by descending score

##### <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`ScraperError`](../../error/enum.ScraperError.html "enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError") if embedding or database access fails.





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/vault_search.rs.html#173-213" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub async fn <a href="#method.index_note" class="fn">index_note</a>( &self, path: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>, content: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>, content_hash: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>, mtime_secs: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.i64.html" class="primitive">i64</a>, ) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.usize.html" class="primitive">usize</a>, <a href="../../error/enum.ScraperError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError">ScraperError</a>\>





Index a single note: chunk → embed → persist.

The caller is responsible for reading the file and providing its content. This method handles chunking, embedding, and storage.

##### <a href="#pipeline-1" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Pipeline

1.  Chunk the markdown content via [`TextChunker`](../../domain/text_chunker/trait.TextChunker.html "trait webfang_core::domain::text_chunker::TextChunker")
2.  Embed all chunks via [`EmbeddingPort::embed_batch`](../../domain/embedding_port/trait.EmbeddingPort.html#method.embed_batch "method webfang_core::domain::embedding_port::EmbeddingPort::embed_batch")
3.  Register the note via [`NoteRepository::save_note`](../../domain/note_repository/trait.NoteRepository.html#tymethod.save_note "method webfang_core::domain::note_repository::NoteRepository::save_note")
4.  Persist each chunk with its embedding

##### <a href="#errors-1" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`ScraperError`](../../error/enum.ScraperError.html "enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError") if chunking, embedding, or persistence fails.





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/vault_search.rs.html#219-225" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub async fn <a href="#method.needs_reindex" class="fn">needs_reindex</a>( &self, path: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>, content_hash: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>, ) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>, <a href="../../error/enum.ScraperError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError">ScraperError</a>\>

Delegates to [`NoteRepository::note_needs_reindex`](../../domain/note_repository/trait.NoteRepository.html#tymethod.note_needs_reindex "method webfang_core::domain::note_repository::NoteRepository::note_needs_reindex") which compares the stored content hash against the provided one.

Remove a note and all its chunks from the index.





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/vault_search.rs.html#251-336" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub async fn <a href="#method.sync_vault" class="fn">sync_vault</a>( &self, vault_path: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/path/struct.Path.html" class="struct" title="struct std::path::Path">Path</a>, ) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="struct.SyncSummary.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::application::vault_search::SyncSummary">SyncSummary</a>, <a href="../../error/enum.ScraperError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError">ScraperError</a>\>





Synchronize the vault filesystem against the persistent index.

##### <a href="#pipeline-2" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Pipeline

1.  Read all `.md` notes from the vault via [`read_vault_notes`](../../infrastructure/obsidian/vault_reader/fn.read_vault_notes.html "fn webfang_core::infrastructure::obsidian::vault_reader::read_vault_notes")
2.  Load all indexed note metadata via [`NoteRepository::list_indexed_notes`](../../domain/note_repository/trait.NoteRepository.html#tymethod.list_indexed_notes "method webfang_core::domain::note_repository::NoteRepository::list_indexed_notes")
3.  Compare content hashes:
    - **New** note (not indexed) → [`index_note`](struct.VaultSearchService.html#method.index_note "method webfang_core::application::vault_search::VaultSearchService::index_note")
    - **Changed** note (hash differs) → re-index
    - **Deleted** note (indexed but gone from vault) → [`remove_note`](struct.VaultSearchService.html#method.remove_note "method webfang_core::application::vault_search::VaultSearchService::remove_note")
    - **Unchanged** → skip
4.  Return a [`SyncSummary`](struct.SyncSummary.html "struct webfang_core::application::vault_search::SyncSummary") with counts

##### <a href="#errors-2" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`ScraperError`](../../error/enum.ScraperError.html "enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError") if vault reading, database access, embedding, or persistence fails. Individual note indexing errors are logged and skipped (best-effort sync).

URL patterns to include (glob-style). Three modes:

CLI Arguments for the webfang binary.

Parsed using `clap` with derive macros.

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::Args;
use clap::Parser;

let args = Args::parse_from([
    "webfang",
    "--url", "https://example.com",
    "--output", "./output",
    "--export-format", "jsonl",
    "--resume",
]);

assert_eq!(args.crawler.url.as_deref(), Some("https://example.com"));
```

## Implementations<a href="#implementations" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/cli/args/mod.rs.html#115-136" class="src rightside">Source</a><a href="#impl-Args" class="anchor">§</a>

### impl <a href="struct.Args.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::cli::args::Args">Args</a>







<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/cli/args/mod.rs.html#127-135" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.elastic_overrides" class="fn">elastic_overrides</a>(&self) -\> <a href="../../infrastructure/autotuning/struct.ElasticOverrides.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::autotuning::ElasticOverrides">ElasticOverrides</a>





Build [`ElasticOverrides`](../../infrastructure/autotuning/struct.ElasticOverrides.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::autotuning::ElasticOverrides") (PR5) from the elastic-ingestion CLI flags.

`--ram-budget` is parsed via [`parse_ram_bytes`](../../infrastructure/autotuning/fn.parse_ram_bytes.html "fn webfang_core::infrastructure::autotuning::parse_ram_bytes") so it accepts suffixed values (`8GB`, `2048MB`, plain bytes). The result feeds [`ElasticConfig::resolve`](../../infrastructure/autotuning/struct.ElasticConfig.html#method.resolve "associated function webfang_core::infrastructure::autotuning::ElasticConfig::resolve") → Rayon pool size, byte-weighted semaphore, and SQLite path.

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/cli/args/mod.rs.html#149-235" class="src rightside">Source</a><a href="#method.from" class="anchor">§</a>

#### fn <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/convert/trait.From.html#tymethod.from" class="fn">from</a>(args: <a href="struct.Args.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::cli::args::Args">Args</a>) -\> Self





Convert CLI arguments into structured [`crate::application::crawl_options::CrawlOptions`](../../application/crawl_options/struct.CrawlOptions.html "struct webfang_core::application::crawl_options::CrawlOptions").

This is an owned, lossless conversion — every field in `Args` maps to exactly one field in `CrawlOptions`. The `url` field is parsed from `Option<String>` into `Url` (panics if invalid; CLI validation guarantees validity before this point).

# Function init_logging_dual

``` rust
pub fn init_logging_dual(
    level: &str,
    quiet: bool,
    no_color: bool,
    file_trace_layer: Option<FileTraceLayer>,
)
```

Expand description



Dual-mode logging: forces stderr, supports quiet mode and NO_COLOR.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `level` - Log level: “error”, “warn”, “info”, “debug”, “trace”
- `quiet` - If true, only warn+level output is shown
- `no_color` - If true, ANSI colors are disabled
- `file_trace_layer` - Optional file trace layer for JSONL output

### impl <a href="struct.ConfigDefaults.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::cli::config::ConfigDefaults">ConfigDefaults</a>







<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/cli/config.rs.html#45-53" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.load" class="fn">load</a>(path: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/path/struct.Path.html" class="struct" title="struct std::path::Path">Path</a>) -\> Self





Load configuration from a TOML file, falling back to defaults.

Returns defaults if the file doesn’t exist (normal — no config yet). A malformed existing file logs `error!` and falls back to defaults — the user’s entire configuration is silently lost, so this must be loud.

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[cli](../index.html)::[error](index.html)



# Enum CliExit

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/cli/error.rs.html#123-147" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum CliExit {
    Success,
    UsageError(String),
    NetworkError(String),
    IoError(String),
    ProtocolError(String),
    ConfigError(String),
    EmptyDiscovery(String),
    ScraperFailure(String),
    PartialSuccess {
        success: usize,
        failed: usize,
    },
}
```

Expand description



Exit codes following sysexits convention: 0 = success, 64 = usage error, 69 = service unavailable (network/partial), 74 = I/O error, 76 = protocol error, 78 = config error

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[cli](../index.html)::[orchestrator](index.html)



# Function prepare_progress_channel

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/cli/orchestrator.rs.html#46-56" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn prepare_progress_channel(
    quiet: bool,
) -> (Box<dyn ProgressObserver>, UnboundedReceiver<ScrapeProgress>)
```

Expand description



Create an unbounded channel and a `LiveProgressObserver` wired to it.

Returns `(observer, rx)` where:

- `observer` wraps the `tx` side and can be passed to `scrape_urls`
- `rx` is the receiving end for the TUI progress view

The caller must pass `rx` to `run_progress_view` on the main thread (crossterm TTY ownership requirement).














[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[cli](../index.html)::[orchestrator](index.html)



# Function run

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/cli/orchestrator.rs.html#66-180" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub async fn run(
    opts: CrawlOptions,
    ai_cleaner: Option<Arc<dyn SemanticCleaner>>,
    adaptive_engine: Option<Arc<AdaptiveSelectorEngine>>,
    vault_ports: VaultAiPorts,
) -> CliExit
```

Expand description



Main orchestration entry point.

Coordinates the full scraping pipeline:

1.  URL discovery + config preparation
2.  Scraping with progress
3.  Export results
4.  Report failures + exit code

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[cli](../index.html)::[preflight](index.html)



# Function apply_tui_config_args

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/cli/preflight.rs.html#235-247" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn apply_tui_config_args(args: Args, config_values: &Value) -> Args
```

Expand description



Apply config values from TUI form to Args.

This runs on Args before conversion to CrawlOptions, because the TUI Apply TUI config values to Args.

Handles all 39 fields from CollapsibleConfig. Only applies values that are present in the JSON (non-null, non-empty). Apply config values from the TUI form to `Args`.

Pure field mapping. Each logical group is applied by a dedicated helper so the orchestrator stays linear and auditably simple (issue \#516).


Apply resume mode filtering.

## <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns `CliExit::IoError` when `--resume` is active and the state store cannot be created. Without a working store the crawl would silently re-scrape every URL, defeating the purpose of resume mode.














[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[cli](../index.html)::[scrape_flow](index.html)



# Function scrape_urls

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/cli/scrape_flow.rs.html#135-213" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub async fn scrape_urls(
    urls: &[Url],
    scraper_config: &ScraperConfig,
    opts: &CrawlOptions,
    observer: &dyn ProgressObserver,
    downloader: Option<&dyn AssetDownloaderPort>,
    engine: Option<&AdaptiveSelectorEngine>,
    root_correlation: &CorrelationId,
) -> Result<(Vec<ScrapedContent>, Vec<(String, ScraperError)>), ScraperError>
```

Expand description



Scrape all URLs, reporting progress via the provided observer.

Correlation contract (#501): `root_correlation` is the run-root identity owned by the orchestrator; each page derives `.child()` from it — one shared `trace_id` for the whole run, a fresh `span_id` per page.

The observer handles quiet/channel logic internally — callers pass `&NoopObserver` for dry-run or `&LiveProgressObserver` for live output.

## <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`crate::error::ScraperError`](../../error/enum.ScraperError.html "enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError") if the configured H2/TLS profile name (`opts.network.h2_profile`) is not recognized, or if the fetch router’s HTTP client cannot be built. Both are setup failures that abort the whole batch before any URL is scraped.

Expand description



Central application configuration

Combines all configuration types into a single validated structure. Following Clean Architecture: configuration is infrastructure concern.

#### pub fn <a href="#method.new" class="fn">new</a>() -\> Self

The default crawler URL is a hardcoded constant that cannot fail to parse; `new` returns `Self`, so the error cannot be propagated.

# Struct MockClock

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/clock.rs.html#84-86" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct MockClock { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Mock clock for deterministic `Instant`-based testing.

Uses `Arc<Mutex<Instant>>` internally so the clock can be shared between the pool (via `Arc<dyn Clock>`) and the test (via `MockClock`). Advancing through the `MockClock` is visible to the pool.

## <a href="#example" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Example



``` rust
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
use webfang_core::domain::clock::{Clock, MockClock};

let clock = MockClock::new(Instant::now());
let t0 = clock.now();

// Advance time by 100ms
clock.advance(Duration::from_millis(100));
assert_eq!(clock.now(), t0 + Duration::from_millis(100));
```

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[domain](../index.html)::[clock](index.html)



# Struct MockUtcClock

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/clock.rs.html#159-161" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct MockUtcClock { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Mock UTC clock for deterministic `DateTime<Utc>`-based testing.

## <a href="#example" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Example



``` rust
use chrono::{Duration, Utc};
use webfang_core::domain::clock::{UtcClock, MockUtcClock};

let t0 = Utc::now();
let mut clock = MockUtcClock::new(t0);
assert_eq!(clock.now(), t0);

clock.advance(Duration::hours(1));
assert_eq!(clock.now(), t0 + Duration::hours(1));
```

# Trait Clock

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/clock.rs.html#19-22" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait Clock: Send + Sync {
    // Required method
    fn now(&self) -> Instant;
}
```

Expand description



Clock port for `Instant`-based timing operations.

Used by components that need monotonic time measurements: rate limiters, session pools, retry backoff.

# Trait UtcClock

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/clock.rs.html#28-31" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait UtcClock: Send + Sync {
    // Required method
    fn now(&self) -> DateTime<Utc>;
}
```

Expand description



Clock port for `DateTime<Utc>`-based timestamp operations.

Used by components that need wall-clock timestamps: credential expiry, export timestamps, audit logs.

# Struct ConcurrencyConfig

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/config.rs.html#41-46" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct ConcurrencyConfig { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Concurrency configuration with smart auto-detection.

Provides intelligent defaults based on hardware capabilities:

- **Auto-detection**: Uses `std::thread::available_parallelism()` to detect CPU cores
- **HDD-aware**: Limits concurrency on systems with limited I/O
- **Safe bounds**: Clamps values between 1 and 16

Resolve the actual concurrency value.

Uses auto-detection based on CPU cores:

- 1-2 cores: 1 (avoid overwhelming system)
- 4 cores: 3 (HDD-aware default)
- 8+ cores: min(cores - 1, 8)

# Trait ContentProcessor

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/content_processor.rs.html#22-28" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait ContentProcessor: Send + Sync {
    // Required methods
    fn process(&self, html: &str) -> String;
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
}
```

Expand description



Content processing strategy for converting HTML to usable text.

Different consumers need different cleaning behaviors:

- Semantic extraction for RAG/pipeline (preserves readability structure)
- Aggressive stripping for download pipeline (removes all noise)
- MCP tools (removes boilerplate, keeps semantic tags)

The trait is intentionally simple — implementations hold the complexity.

# Struct ApiKey

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/credentials.rs.html#51" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct ApiKey(/* private fields */);
```

Expand description



API Key wrapper using zeroize for secure memory handling

## <a href="#security" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Security

- Memory is zeroized on drop (secrecy trait)
- Debug prints `[REDACTED]` instead of actual value
- Does NOT implement Serialize/Deserialize (secrets should never be serialized)

<a href="https://docs.rs/either/1/src/either/into_either.rs.html#29" class="src rightside">Source</a><a href="#method.into_either" class="anchor">§</a>

#### fn <a href="https://docs.rs/either/1/either/into_either/trait.IntoEither.html#method.into_either" class="fn">into_either</a>(self, into_left: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>) -\> <a href="https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html" class="enum" title="enum either::Either">Either</a>\<Self, Self\>





Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left` is `true`. Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right "variant either::Either::Right") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") otherwise. [Read more](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/into_either/trait.IntoEither.html#method.into_either)





<a href="https://docs.rs/either/1/src/either/into_either.rs.html#55-57" class="src rightside">Source</a><a href="#method.into_either_with" class="anchor">§</a>

#### fn <a href="https://docs.rs/either/1/either/into_either/trait.IntoEither.html#method.into_either_with" class="fn">into_either_with</a>\<F\>(self, into_left: F) -\> <a href="https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html" class="enum" title="enum either::Either">Either</a>\<Self, Self\>



where F: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html" class="trait" title="trait core::ops::function::FnOnce">FnOnce</a>(&Self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>,







Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left(&self)` returns `true`. Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right "variant either::Either::Right") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") otherwise. [Read more](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/into_either/trait.IntoEither.html#method.into_either_with)

# Struct CredentialStore

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/credentials.rs.html#249-252" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct CredentialStore { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Collection of credentials, keyed by provider name

Only stores provider names and metadata - actual secrets are kept in memory. This type CAN be serialized (stores no actual secret values).

# Struct SecretCredential

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/credentials.rs.html#169-177" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct SecretCredential {
    pub provider: String,
    pub secret: ApiKey,
    pub expires_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
}
```

Expand description



Secret credential with optional expiry

Combines a provider name with a secret value and optional expiration time. Supports expiry checking for credentials that have limited validity.

**Security**: The secret field is NOT serialized to prevent accidental leakage.

Sensitive string wrapper with zeroize protection

## <a href="#security" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Security

- Memory is zeroized on drop
- Debug prints `[REDACTED]`
- Does NOT implement Serialize/Deserialize

<a href="https://docs.rs/either/1/src/either/into_either.rs.html#29" class="src rightside">Source</a><a href="#method.into_either" class="anchor">§</a>

#### fn <a href="https://docs.rs/either/1/either/into_either/trait.IntoEither.html#method.into_either" class="fn">into_either</a>(self, into_left: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>) -\> <a href="https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html" class="enum" title="enum either::Either">Either</a>\<Self, Self\>





Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left` is `true`. Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right "variant either::Either::Right") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") otherwise. [Read more](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/into_either/trait.IntoEither.html#method.into_either)

#### fn <a href="https://docs.rs/either/1/either/into_either/trait.IntoEither.html#method.into_either_with" class="fn">into_either_with</a>\<F\>(self, into_left: F) -\> <a href="https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html" class="enum" title="enum either::Either">Either</a>\<Self, Self\>



where F: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html" class="trait" title="trait core::ops::function::FnOnce">FnOnce</a>(&Self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>,







Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left(&self)` returns `true`. Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right "variant either::Either::Right") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") otherwise. [Read more](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/into_either/trait.IntoEither.html#method.into_either_with)

# Enum SelectorErrorKind

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/dom_inspector.rs.html#27-39" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum SelectorErrorKind {
    ZeroMatches,
    InvalidSelector(String),
    EmptyDocument,
    RepairInconclusive(Box<RepairFailureDiagnostic>),
    BlockingTaskFailed(String),
}
```

Expand description



Error kind for CSS selector diagnostics.

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[domain](../index.html)::[dom_inspector](index.html)



# Trait DomInspectorPort

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/dom_inspector.rs.html#119-135" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait DomInspectorPort: Send + Sync {
    // Required methods
    fn inspect(&self, document: &Html) -> DomStructureReport;
    fn suggest(
        &self,
        document: &Html,
        failed_selector: &str,
    ) -> Vec<SelectorSuggestion>;
}
```

Expand description



Port trait for DOM inspection — analyzes DOM structure for selector diagnostics.

This trait is **sync** (CPU-bound, not I/O). Callers may use `spawn_blocking` if the DOM is very large. Implementations walk the DOM tree to extract structural information and compute similarity scores.

## <a href="#thread-safety" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Thread safety

Implementations must be `Send + Sync` to work with Tokio’s multi-threaded runtime.



## Required Methods<a href="#required-methods" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/dom_inspector.rs.html#126" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### fn <a href="#tymethod.inspect" class="fn">inspect</a>(&self, document: &Html) -\> <a href="struct.DomStructureReport.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::domain::dom_inspector::DomStructureReport">DomStructureReport</a>





Build a structural report of the DOM.

##### <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors
