# Trait EmbeddingPort

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/embedding_port.rs.html#40-79" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait EmbeddingPort: Send + Sync {
    // Required methods
    fn embed<'a>(
        &'a self,
        text: &'a str,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Vec<f32>, SemanticError>> + Send + 'a>>;
    fn embedding_dim(&self) -> usize;

    // Provided method
    fn embed_batch<'a>(
        &'a self,
        texts: &'a [String],
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Vec<Vec<f32>>, SemanticError>> + Send + 'a>> { ... }
}
```

Expand description



Domain trait for text embedding generation.

Implementations wrap an ONNX inference pool to produce fixed-dimension embedding vectors. The default model (Granite-97M) produces 384-dimensional vectors; both supported models output 384d via Matryoshka truncation.

## <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`SemanticError`](../../error/enum.SemanticError.html "enum webfang_core::error::SemanticError") when:

- [`SemanticError::Inference`](../../error/enum.SemanticError.html#variant.Inference "variant webfang_core::error::SemanticError::Inference"): ONNX model execution failed
- [`SemanticError::Tokenize`](../../error/enum.SemanticError.html#variant.Tokenize "variant webfang_core::error::SemanticError::Tokenize"): input text tokenization failed
- [`SemanticError::ModelLoad`](../../error/enum.SemanticError.html#variant.ModelLoad "variant webfang_core::error::SemanticError::ModelLoad"): model not available



## Required Methods<a href="#required-methods" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/embedding_port.rs.html#49" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### fn <a href="#tymethod.embed" class="fn">embed</a>\<'a\>( &'a self, text: &'a <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>, ) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/pin/struct.Pin.html" class="struct" title="struct core::pin::Pin">Pin</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::boxed::Box">Box</a>\<dyn <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/future/future/trait.Future.html" class="trait" title="trait core::future::future::Future">Future</a>\<Output = <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.f32.html" class="primitive">f32</a>\>, <a href="../../error/enum.SemanticError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::SemanticError">SemanticError</a>\>\> + <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Send.html" class="trait" title="trait core::marker::Send">Send</a> + 'a\>\>





Generate an embedding vector for a single text.

Returns a fixed-dimension vector (384d for both Granite models).

##### <a href="#errors-1" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`SemanticError::Inference`](../../error/enum.SemanticError.html#variant.Inference "variant webfang_core::error::SemanticError::Inference") if the model execution fails, or [`SemanticError::Tokenize`](../../error/enum.SemanticError.html#variant.Tokenize "variant webfang_core::error::SemanticError::Tokenize") if the text cannot be tokenized.





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/embedding_port.rs.html#78" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### fn <a href="#tymethod.embedding_dim" class="fn">embedding_dim</a>(&self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.usize.html" class="primitive">usize</a>





The dimensionality of embedding vectors produced by this port.

Both supported models (Granite-97M and Granite-311M) return 384.





## Provided Methods<a href="#provided-methods" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/embedding_port.rs.html#62-73" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### fn <a href="#method.embed_batch" class="fn">embed_batch</a>\<'a\>( &'a self, texts: &'a \[<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>\], ) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/pin/struct.Pin.html" class="struct" title="struct core::pin::Pin">Pin</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::boxed::Box">Box</a>\<dyn <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/future/future/trait.Future.html" class="trait" title="trait core::future::future::Future">Future</a>\<Output = <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.f32.html" class="primitive">f32</a>\>\>, <a href="../../error/enum.SemanticError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::SemanticError">SemanticError</a>\>\> + <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Send.html" class="trait" title="trait core::marker::Send">Send</a> + 'a\>\>





Generate embedding vectors for multiple texts in a batch.

The default implementation calls [`embed`](trait.EmbeddingPort.html#tymethod.embed) sequentially. Implementations may override this to use batched ONNX inference for better throughput.

Returns one vector per input text, in the same order.

##### <a href="#errors-2" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`SemanticError`](../../error/enum.SemanticError.html "enum webfang_core::error::SemanticError") if any individual embedding fails.

Expand description



Errors that can occur during DocumentChunk validation

Domain errors define WHAT failed, not HOW to present to users. Error messages are neutral identifiers for programmatic handling. Presentation layer (CLI/TUI) maps these to user-friendly messages.

# Struct DocumentChunk

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/domain/entities/content.rs.html#216-241" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct DocumentChunk<S = Draft> {
    pub id: Uuid,
    pub url: String,
    pub title: String,
    pub content: String,
    pub metadata: HashMap<String, String>,
    pub timestamp: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub embeddings: Option<Vec<f32>>,
    pub correlation_id: Option<String>,
    /* private fields */
}
```

Expand description



A document chunk ready for export to RAG pipelines

Represents a single unit of content that can be:

- Embedded in a vector database
- Exported in various formats (JSONL, Markdown)

The embeddings field is optional because in the initial scraping phase the AI model may not be available yet. It can be populated later by a separate embedding pipeline.

Uses typestate pattern: must call `.validate()` before export.



<a href="#" class="tooltip" title="This example deliberately fails to compile">ⓘ</a>

``` rust
use webfang_core::domain::DocumentChunkUnvalidated;
use webfang_core::domain::Exporter;
use webfang_core::domain::exporter::ExporterConfig;
use webfang_core::infrastructure::export::FileExporter;
use webfang_core::ExportFormat;
use uuid::Uuid;
use std::path::PathBuf;

// DocumentChunk<Draft> cannot be compiled into the export path.
// The typestate pattern enforces .validate() before export at compile time.
let config = ExporterConfig::new(PathBuf::from("/tmp"), ExportFormat::Jsonl, "test");
let exporter = FileExporter::new(config);
let chunk = DocumentChunkUnvalidated::new(
    Uuid::new_v4(),
    "https://example.com",
    "Test Title",
    "Test content",
);

// This MUST fail: Exporter::export() expects DocumentChunk<Validated>
let _ = exporter.export(chunk);
```

where F: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html" class="trait" title="trait core::ops::function::FnOnce">FnOnce</a>(&Self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>,







Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left(&self)` returns `true`. Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right "variant either::Either::Right") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") otherwise. # Struct ScrapedContent

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/domain/entities/content.rs.html#140-167" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct ScrapedContent {
    pub title: String,
    pub content: String,
    pub url: ValidUrl,
    pub excerpt: Option<String>,
    pub author: Option<String>,
    pub date: Option<String>,
    pub html: Option<String>,
    pub assets: Vec<DownloadedAsset>,
    pub correlation_id: Option<CorrelationId>,
}
```

Expand description



Represents scraped content from a web page

This is the main output type of the scraper, containing:

- Extracted content (title, text)
- Metadata (author, date, excerpt)
- Downloaded assets (images, documents)

<a href="#structfield.correlation_id" class="anchor field">§</a>`correlation_id: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/option/enum.Option.html" class="enum" title="enum core::option::Option"><code>Option</code></a>`<`<a href="../../value_objects/struct.CorrelationId.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::domain::value_objects::CorrelationId"><code>CorrelationId</code></a>`>`



Distributed tracing correlation ID (internal — not serialized).

Populated natively on every scrape (issue \#356) and propagated in-memory to `DocumentChunk` for the JSONL export correlation. Skipped from `ScrapedContent` serialization to keep the user-facing `--format json` output clean and deterministic.

# Enum ExportFormat

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/domain/entities/export.rs.html#21-31" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum ExportFormat {
    Jsonl,
    Vector,
    Auto,
}
```

Expand description



Export format variants for RAG pipeline

Defines the supported output formats when exporting scraped content for use in retrieval-augmented generation systems.

These formats are designed for RAG/embedding pipelines, NOT for individual file output (see OutputFormat for that).



| Format | Extension | Use Case                                  |
|--------|-----------|-------------------------------------------|
| Jsonl  | .jsonl    | One JSON object per line, optimal for RAG |
| Auto   | .auto     | Auto-detect from existing files           |





## Variants<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="#variant.Jsonl" class="anchor">§</a>

### Jsonl





JSONL format (JSON Lines - one JSON object per line) Optimal for RAG pipelines and vector database ingestion





<a href="#variant.Vector" class="anchor">§</a>

### Vector





Vector format (JSON with metadata header) Supports embeddings and cosine similarity





<a href="#variant.Auto" class="anchor">§</a>

### Auto





Auto-detect format from existing export files

# Struct ExportState

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/domain/entities/export.rs.html#71-80" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct ExportState {
    pub domain: String,
    pub processed_urls: Vec<String>,
    pub last_export: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
    pub total_exported: u64,
}
```

Expand description



Metadata for the export state file

Stored at `~/.cache/webfang/state/<domain>.json` Tracks which URLs have been processed for a given domain to support incremental exports and resume capability.

# Enum ScrapeError

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/domain/entities/progress.rs.html#116-144" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum ScrapeError {
    Network(String),
    Http(u16, String),
    WafBlocked(String),
    Parse(String),
    Timeout(String),
    Connection(String),
    Other(String),
}
```

Expand description



Errors that can occur during the scraping process.

These errors are categorized by the failure mode and may include WAF/CAPTCHA blocks, network issues, or parsing failures.



## Variants<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="#variant.Network" class="anchor">§</a>

### Network(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>)

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[domain](../../index.html)::[entities](../index.html)::[progress](index.html)



# Enum ScrapeProgress

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/domain/entities/progress.rs.html#22-58" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum ScrapeProgress {
    Started {
        url: String,
    },
    StatusChanged {
        url: String,
        status: ScrapeStatus,
    },
    Completed {
        url: String,
        chars: usize,
    },
    Failed {
        url: String,
        error: ScrapeError,
    },
    Finished {
        total: usize,
        successful: usize,
        failed: usize,
    },
}
```

Expand description



Represents the progress of a scraping operation.

Variants:

- Started: Scraping operation has begun for a URL
- StatusChanged: Progress status updated (carries URL and new ScrapeStatus)
- Completed: Operation completed successfully for a URL
- Failed: Operation terminated with a non-recoverable error for a URL
- Finished: Final state after completion or failure of all URLs

# Enum ScrapeStatus

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/domain/entities/progress.rs.html#64-77" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum ScrapeStatus {
    Pending,
    Fetching,
    Extracting,
    Downloading,
    Completed,
    Failed,
}
```

Expand description



Represents the current operational status during scraping.

Status values progress through a typical web scraping pipeline.



## Variants<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="#variant.Pending" class="anchor">§</a>

### Pending





URL queued, not started





<a href="#variant.Fetching" class="anchor">§</a>

### Fetching





Currently fetching HTTP response





<a href="#variant.Extracting" class="anchor">§</a>

### Extracting





Processing with Readability algorithm





<a href="#variant.Downloading" class="anchor">§</a>

### Downloading





Downloading assets (if enabled)





<a href="#variant.Completed" class="anchor">§</a>

### Completed





Successfully scraped





<a href="#variant.Failed" class="anchor">§</a>

### Failed





Error during scrape

# Struct ErrorEntry

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/domain/entities/progress.rs.html#198-207" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct ErrorEntry {
    pub timestamp: SystemTime,
    pub url: String,
    pub error_type: ErrorType,
    pub message: String,
}
```

Expand description



Represents a single error occurrence with metadata.

Errors are timestamped and may carry contextual information to help diagnose issues during the scraping process.

# Enum CompressionType

<a href="../../src/webfang_core/domain/mod.rs.html#95-106" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum CompressionType {
    None,
    Gzip,
    Deflate,
    Brotli,
    Zstd,
}
```

Expand description



Compression types supported for sitemap parsing



## Variants<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="#variant.None" class="anchor">§</a>

### None





No compression — raw, uncompressed content.





<a href="#variant.Gzip" class="anchor">§</a>

### Gzip





gzip (RFC 1952) — common in HTTP Content-Encoding.





<a href="#variant.Deflate" class="anchor">§</a>

### Deflate





DEFLATE (RFC 1951) — raw deflate without zlib wrapper.





<a href="#variant.Brotli" class="anchor">§</a>

### Brotli





Brotli — modern high-ratio compression, used by CDNs.





<a href="#variant.Zstd" class="anchor">§</a>

### Zstd





Zstandard — modern compression balancing speed and ratio.

# Enum CrawlError

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/error/crawl_error.rs.html#57-226" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
#[non_exhaustive]pub enum CrawlError {
Network {
        message: String,
        status_code: Option<u16>,
    },
    Http {
        status: u16,
        url: String,
    },
    InvalidUrl(String),
    Parse(String),
    MaxDepthExceeded {
        current: u8,
        max: u8,
    },
    MaxPagesExceeded {
        max: usize,
    },
    UrlExcluded(String),
    InvalidContentType(String),
    Io(Error),
    Internal(String),
    SitemapNotFound(String),
    Storage(String),
    Checkpoint(String),
    SessionPool(String),
    Discovery(String),
    Download(Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>),
    WafChallenge {
        provider: String,
        kind: WafDetectionKind,
        url: String,
    },
    RetryExhausted {
        url: String,
        attempts: usize,
    },
    TransientHttp {
        status: u16,
        url: String,
    },
    RateLimited(u64),
    Timeout,
    Connection(String),
    RequestFailed(String),
    ResourceExhausted {
        resource: ResourceKind,
        limit: usize,
        actual: usize,
    },
    SitemapEmpty,
    SitemapDepthExceeded,
    SemaphoreInanition,
    Cancelled,
}
```

Expand description



Crawl errors

Following **err-thiserror-for-libraries**: Uses thiserror for library error types. Following **api-non-exhaustive**: Can add variants without breaking changes. Following **clean-architecture**: NO dependencies on reqwest/anyhow (Infra layer)



## Variants (Non-exhaustive)<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>

This enum is marked as non-exhaustive



Non-exhaustive enums could have additional variants added in future. Therefore, when matching against variants of non-exhaustive enums, an extra wildcard arm must be added to account for any future variants.







<a href="#variant.Network" class="anchor">§</a>

### Network





Network error during HTTP request

Note: Does NOT contain reqwest::Error (that’s Infra detail). Infrastructure layer converts reqwest::Error → this variant.

<a href="#variant.Cancelled" class="anchor">§</a>

### Cancelled





Task cancelled by engine shutdown (#509)

Control signal, not an operational failure: the crawl engine cancelled this task while it waited for a rate-limit permit or a resource-governor permit. Handlers must NOT count it as a crawl error.

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[domain](../index.html)::[error](index.html)



# Enum CrawlErrorCategory

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/error/crawl_error_category.rs.html#17-34" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
#[non_exhaustive]pub enum CrawlErrorCategory {
    Waf,
    Http,
    Timeout,
    Network,
    RateLimit,
    Extraction,
    Internal,
    Panic,
}
```

Expand description



Operational category for a crawl error.

Reduces the full `CrawlError` variant space to a fixed set of categories that are meaningful in dashboards and alerts.



## Variants (Non-exhaustive)<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>

This enum is marked as non-exhaustive



Non-exhaustive enums could have additional variants added in future. Therefore, when matching against variants of non-exhaustive enums, an extra wildcard arm must be added to account for any future variants.







<a href="#variant.Waf" class="anchor">§</a>

### Waf





WAF challenge detected (Cloudflare, AWS WAF, etc.)





<a href="#variant.Http" class="anchor">§</a>

### Http





HTTP status errors (4xx/5xx, transient)





<a href="#variant.Timeout" class="anchor">§</a>

### Timeout





Request timeout





<a href="#variant.Network" class="anchor">§</a>

### Network





Network-level failures (DNS, connection, download)





<a href="#variant.RateLimit" class="anchor">§</a>

### RateLimit





Rate limiting (429 / retry-after)





<a href="#variant.Extraction" class="anchor">§</a>

### Extraction





Content extraction / parsing failures





<a href="#variant.Internal" class="anchor">§</a>

### Internal





Internal / catch-all (storage, checkpoint, config, etc.)





<a href="#variant.Panic" class="anchor">§</a>

### Panic





Task panicked (JoinError)

# Enum DomainError

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/error/domain_error.rs.html#14-47" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum DomainError {
    InvalidUrl(String),
    Readability(String),
    Extraction(String),
    ExtractionFailed {
        url: String,
        reason: String,
    },
    Validation(String),
    FeatureGated(String),
    Conversion(String),
}
```

Expand description



Domain-level errors representing business rule violations.

These errors represent domain-level failures that are independent of infrastructure or application concerns. Each variant maps to a `ScraperError` variant via `From` for backward compatibility.

#### fn <a href="https://docs.rs/either/1/either/into_either/trait.IntoEither.html#method.into_either" class="fn">into_either</a>(self, into_left: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>) -\> <a href="https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html" class="enum" title="enum either::Either">Either</a>\<Self, Self\>





Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left` is `true`. Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right "variant either::Either::Right") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") otherwise. #### fn <a href="https://docs.rs/either/1/either/into_either/trait.IntoEither.html#method.into_either_with" class="fn">into_either_with</a>\<F\>(self, into_left: F) -\> <a href="https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html" class="enum" title="enum either::Either">Either</a>\<Self, Self\>



where F: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html" class="trait" title="trait core::ops::function::FnOnce">FnOnce</a>(&Self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>,







Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left(&self)` returns `true`. Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right "variant either::Either::Right") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") otherwise. [Read more](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/into_either/trait.IntoEither.html#method.into_either_with)

# Enum ExporterError

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/exporter.rs.html#15-48" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum ExporterError {
    DirectoryCreation(Error),
    WriteError(String),
    InvalidConfig(String),
    Serialization(Error),
    BatchError(String),
    UnsupportedFormat(String),
    StateStore(ScraperError),
    DimensionMismatch {
        expected: usize,
        actual: usize,
    },
}
```

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/exporter.rs.html#58-69" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct ExporterConfig {
    pub output_dir: PathBuf,
    pub format: ExportFormat,
    pub filename: String,
    pub append: bool,
    pub batch_size: Option<usize>,
}
```

Expand description



Configuration for exporter instances

Contains all settings needed to configure an exporter for a specific format and output location.

# Trait Exporter

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/exporter.rs.html#151-182" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait Exporter:
    Send
    + Sync
    + 'static {
    // Required methods
    fn export(&self, document: DocumentChunkValidated) -> ExportResult<()>;
    fn export_batch(
        &self,
        documents: &[DocumentChunkValidated],
    ) -> ExportResult<()>;
    fn config(&self) -> &ExporterConfig;

    // Provided method
    fn format(&self) -> ExportFormat { ... }
}
```

Expand description



Trait for exporting document chunks to various formats

Implementors must provide:

- Synchronous export (export method)
- Batch export (export_batch method)

The trait is designed to be:

- `Sync`: Safe to share across threads
- `'static`: No lifetime dependencies on caller

## <a href="#example" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Example



<a href="#" class="tooltip" title="This example is not tested">ⓘ</a>

``` rust
struct JsonlExporter {
    config: ExporterConfig,
}

impl Exporter for JsonlExporter {
    fn export(&self, document: DocumentChunk<Validated>) -> ExportResult<()> { ... }
    fn export_batch(&self, documents: &[DocumentChunk<Validated>]) -> ExportResult<()> { ... }
}
```

Export multiple documents in batch (must be Validated state)

This method is optimized for bulk operations and may:

- Batch I/O operations for better performance
- Use streaming writes for large datasets
- Maintain transaction semantics

##### <a href="#arguments-1" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `documents` - Slice of document chunks in Validated state to export

##### <a href="#errors-1" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns ExporterError if any document fails to export

``` rust
pub struct HttpClientConfig {
    pub accept_language: String,
    pub accept: String,
    pub referer: String,
    pub cache_control: String,
    pub max_retries: u32,
    pub backoff_base_ms: u64,
    pub backoff_max_ms: u64,
    pub enable_cookies: bool,
    pub timeout_secs: u64,
    pub connect_timeout_secs: u64,

    pub user_agent: Option<String>,

}
```

Expand description



Configuration for HTTP client behavior

Controls headers, retry behavior, and cookie handling. Use `Default` for sensible production defaults.

Rate limit: requests per minute (None for no limit)



<a href="#structfield.tls_emulation" class="anchor field">§</a>`tls_emulation: Profile`



TLS fingerprint emulation preset.

This is the **single source of truth** for the TLS/H2 fingerprint: the network stack applies it directly when building the client. Construct it from a user-supplied name with [`HttpClientConfig::profile_from_name`](struct.HttpClientConfig.html#method.profile_from_name "associated function webfang_core::domain::http_config::HttpClientConfig::profile_from_name").



<a href="#structfield.user_agent" class="anchor field">§</a>`user_agent: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/option/enum.Option.html" class="enum" title="enum core::option::Option"><code>Option</code></a>`<`<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>`>`



Custom User-Agent override



<a href="#structfield.ignore_waf" class="anchor field">§</a>`ignore_waf: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive"><code>bool</code></a>



Bypass WAF/CAPTCHA detection entirely (REQ-WAF-07).

When true, the HTTP client builds its WAF `InspectionContext` with `ignore_waf` set, short-circuiting inspection to a clean verdict so challenge markers never block a response.

### impl <a href="struct.HttpClientConfig.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::domain::http_config::HttpClientConfig">HttpClientConfig</a>







<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/http_config.rs.html#90-94" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.profile_from_name" class="fn">profile_from_name</a>(name: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<Profile, <a href="struct.UnknownProfileError.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::domain::http_config::UnknownProfileError">UnknownProfileError</a>\>





Parse an H2/TLS profile name into a \[`wreq_util::Profile`\].

This is the fallible boundary that converts a user-facing profile name (e.g. the `--h2-profile` CLI value) into the typed [`Self::tls_emulation`](struct.HttpClientConfig.html#structfield.tls_emulation "field webfang_core::domain::http_config::HttpClientConfig::tls_emulation") preset. It delegates to the domain resolver [`crate::domain::profile::profile_from_name`](../profile/fn.profile_from_name.html "fn webfang_core::domain::profile::profile_from_name"), which accepts the full \[`wreq_util::Profile`\] catalog. Unknown names are an error — there is **no** silent fallback to a default profile.

##### <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`UnknownProfileError`](struct.UnknownProfileError.html "struct webfang_core::domain::http_config::UnknownProfileError") if `name` is not a recognized profile.

# Struct UnknownProfileError

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/http_config.rs.html#105-108" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct UnknownProfileError {
    pub name: String,
}
```

Expand description



Error returned when an H2/TLS profile name is not recognized.

The user-facing [`Display`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/fmt/trait.Display.html "trait core::fmt::Display") message is in Spanish and lists the full dynamic catalog of valid options (every \[`wreq_util::Profile`\] variant), per the project’s user-facing-error convention.

# Enum HttpError

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/http_error.rs.html#22-41" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum HttpError {
    Forbidden,
    RateLimited(u64),
    ClientError(u16),
    ServerError(u16),
    Timeout,
    Connection(String),
    Request(String),
    WafChallenge(String),
    DomainBanned(String),
}
```

Expand description



HTTP-specific errors with status code information

Variants provide specific handling hints:

- `Forbidden`: 403 - retry with different UA
- `RateLimited`: 429 - respect Retry-After header
- `ClientError` / `ServerError`: other 4xx/5xx codes

Request timeout

# Trait HttpClientPort

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/http_port.rs.html#35-45" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait HttpClientPort: Send + Sync {
    // Required method
    fn get(
        &self,
        url: &str,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = HttpResult<HttpResponse>> + Send + '_>>;
}
```

Expand description



Port trait for HTTP requests — application layer depends on this, not `wreq`.

Implementors provide the actual network I/O (production) or canned responses (tests). This trait is intentionally thin — only `get` is required — so that mock implementations stay simple and fast to compile.

## <a href="#thread-safety" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Thread safety

Implementations must be `Send + Sync` to work with Tokio’s multi-threaded runtime.



## Required Methods<a href="#required-methods" class="anchor">§</a>

Production implementation of [`HttpClientPort`](trait.HttpClientPort.html "trait webfang_core::domain::http_port::HttpClientPort") backed by `wreq`.







Performs a single GET request with no retry logic. Retries and user-agent rotation live in [`super::HttpClient`](../../application/http_client/struct.HttpClient.html "struct webfang_core::application::http_client::HttpClient") — this impl is intentionally thin so that the application layer stays decoupled from retry policy.

## Implementors<a href="#implementors" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/application/http_client/client.rs.html#460-507" class="src rightside">Source</a><a href="#impl-HttpClientPort-for-HttpClient" class="anchor">§</a>

### impl <a href="trait.HttpClientPort.html" class="trait" title="trait webfang_core::domain::http_port::HttpClientPort">HttpClientPort</a> for <a href="../../application/http_client/struct.HttpClient.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::application::http_client::HttpClient">HttpClient</a>



Raw, single-shot [`HttpClientPort`](trait.HttpClientPort.html "trait webfang_core::domain::http_port::HttpClientPort") implementation for [`HttpClient`](../../application/http_client/struct.HttpClient.html "struct webfang_core::application::http_client::HttpClient").







#### <a href="#why-this-path-is-deliberately-raw" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Why this path is deliberately raw

[`HttpClient`](../../application/http_client/struct.HttpClient.html "struct webfang_core::application::http_client::HttpClient") exposes two request paths with different contracts, and they are intentionally **not** unified:

- The hardened path — `HttpClient::get` / `get_inner` — returns only the response body as a `String`, after applying rate limiting, per-domain session gating, status-specific retries (429 / 5xx), user-agent rotation on 403, and WAF/CAPTCHA inspection. Non-2xx outcomes are surfaced as [`HttpError`](../http_error/enum.HttpError.html "enum webfang_core::domain::http_error::HttpError") variants.
- This port implementation returns a full [`HttpResponse`](struct.HttpResponse.html "struct webfang_core::domain::http_port::HttpResponse") (`status` + `headers` + `body`) for a **single** GET with no retry, no user-agent rotation and no WAF inspection, reporting non-2xx as data in `status` rather than as an error. It exists for callers that depend on the domain port and manage their own request lifecycle.

Routing this impl through the hardened path would change its observable behavior — it would start retrying, rotating user agents, and turning 5xx/429 responses into [`HttpError`](../http_error/enum.HttpError.html "enum webfang_core::domain::http_error::HttpError")s instead of returning the status — so the divergence is preserved and documented here rather than collapsed (see \#444). The bare-client factories (e.g. [`create_http_client`](../../application/http_client/fn.create_http_client.html "fn webfang_core::application::http_client::create_http_client")) are raw for the same reason.

# Enum JsRenderError

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/js_renderer.rs.html#33-54" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum JsRenderError {
    Browser(String),
    Timeout {
        url: String,
        timeout_ms: u64,
    },
    Navigation(String),
    Extraction(String),
}
```

Expand description



Error type for JavaScript rendering failures.

Covers all expected failure modes for headless browser rendering:

- Browser launch/communication failures
- Page load timeouts
- Navigation errors

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[domain](../index.html)::[js_renderer](index.html)



# Trait JsRenderer

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/js_renderer.rs.html#74-92" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait JsRenderer: Send + Sync {
    // Required method
    fn render(
        &self,
        url: &Url,
    ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<String, JsRenderError>> + Send;
}
```

Expand description



Trait for JavaScript rendering of web pages.

Implementations use a headless browser to execute JavaScript and return the fully rendered HTML. This is needed for Single Page Applications (SPAs) that render content client-side.

Uses native async fn in trait (Rust 1.88+), no `async-trait` crate needed.

## <a href="#example-future-implementation" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Example (future implementation)



<a href="#" class="tooltip" title="This example is not tested">ⓘ</a>

``` rust
use webfang_core::domain::JsRenderer;
use url::Url;

// Future: HeadlessChromeRenderer implements JsRenderer
let renderer = HeadlessChromeRenderer::new().await?;
let html = renderer.render(&Url::parse("https://example.com/spa")?).await?;
```





## Required Methods<a href="#required-methods" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/js_renderer.rs.html#88-91" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### fn <a href="#tymethod.render" class="fn">render</a>( &self, url: &<a href="https://docs.rs/url/2.5.7/url/struct.Url.html" class="struct" title="struct url::Url">Url</a>, ) -\> impl <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/future/future/trait.Future.html" class="trait" title="trait core::future::future::Future">Future</a>\<Output = <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>, <a href="enum.JsRenderError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::domain::js_renderer::JsRenderError">JsRenderError</a>\>\> + <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Send.html" class="trait" title="trait core::marker::Send">Send</a>





Render a URL by executing JavaScript in a headless browser.

##### <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `url` - The URL to render

##### <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

The fully rendered HTML content as a string.

##### <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns `JsRenderError` if rendering fails for any reason.





## Dyn Compatibility<a href="#dyn-compatibility" class="anchor">§</a>



This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety", so this trait is not object safe.*

# Enum JsStrategy

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/js_strategy.rs.html#20-28" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum JsStrategy {
    Static,
    Hybrid,
    Full,
}
```

Expand description



JavaScript rendering strategy for page fetching.



## Variants<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="#variant.Static" class="anchor">§</a>

### Static





Static HTTP only (wreq). Fastest, no JS rendering.





<a href="#variant.Hybrid" class="anchor">§</a>

### Hybrid





Hybrid 3-layer: wreq → Obscura → Chromiumoxide.





<a href="#variant.Full" class="anchor">§</a>

### Full





Full JS rendering only (Chromiumoxide). Slowest, handles all SPAs.

# Trait LinkExtractor

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/link_extractor.rs.html#13-26" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait LinkExtractor {
    // Required method
    fn extract_links(
        &self,
        html: &str,
        base_url: &str,
    ) -> Result<Vec<String>, CrawlError>;
}
```

Expand description



Domain interface for link extraction

This trait defines the contract for extracting and normalizing links from HTML content. The infrastructure layer provides the implementation using external libraries like scraper.



## Required Methods<a href="#required-methods" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/link_extractor.rs.html#25" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### fn <a href="#tymethod.extract_links" class="fn">extract_links</a>( &self, html: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>, base_url: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>, ) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>\>, <a href="../error/enum.CrawlError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::domain::error::CrawlError">CrawlError</a>\>





Extract all links from HTML content

##### <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `html` - HTML content to parse
- `base_url` - Base URL for resolving relative links

##### <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

- `Ok(Vec<String>)` - List of extracted, normalized URLs
- `Err(CrawlError)` - Parse or processing error

# Struct NoteChunkVector

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/note_repository.rs.html#32-41" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct NoteChunkVector {
    pub note_path: String,
    pub content: String,
    pub chunk_index: i64,
    pub embedding: Vec<f32>,
}
```

Expand description



A stored note chunk with its embedding vector.

Returned by bulk vector queries for in-memory ranking.

``` rust
pub trait NoteRepository: Send + Sync {
    // Required methods
    fn save_note<'a>(
        &'a self,
        path: &'a str,
        content_hash: &'a str,
        mtime_secs: i64,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<i64, ScraperError>> + Send + 'a>>;
    fn save_note_chunk<'a>(
        &'a self,
        note_id: i64,
        chunk_index: i64,
        content: &'a str,
        embedding: Option<&'a [f32]>,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<(), ScraperError>> + Send + 'a>>;
    fn load_all_vectors(
        &self,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Vec<NoteChunkVector>, ScraperError>> + Send + '_>>;
    fn note_needs_reindex<'a>(
        &'a self,
        path: &'a str,
        content_hash: &'a str,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<bool, ScraperError>> + Send + 'a>>;
    fn delete_note<'a>(
        &'a self,
        path: &'a str,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<(), ScraperError>> + Send + 'a>>;
    fn list_indexed_notes(
        &self,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Vec<IndexedNoteMeta>, ScraperError>> + Send + '_>>;
}
```

Expand description



Domain trait for vault note vector persistence.

Implementations store note metadata (path, content hash, mtime) and their chunked embedding vectors. Embeddings are serialized as raw little-endian `f32` BLOBs, matching the frozen design decision \#7 used by [`super::repository::VectorRepository`](../repository/trait.VectorRepository.html "trait webfang_core::domain::repository::VectorRepository").

All database failures surface as [`ScraperError::Persistence`](../../error/enum.ScraperError.html#variant.Persistence "variant webfang_core::error::ScraperError::Persistence"), matching the error stratification pattern (frozen decision \#4).

# Function matches_pattern

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/pattern_matching/mod.rs.html#60-103" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn matches_pattern(url_str: &str, pattern: &str) -> bool
```

Expand description



Check if a URL matches a glob-style pattern (dual-mode)

Three modes depending on pattern shape:

- **Path pattern** (starts with `/`): matched against the URL path component. Examples: `/pricing`, `/admin/*`, `/api/v2/*`
- **Path glob** (starts with `*/`): matched against the URL path component. Examples: `*/pricing*`, `*/cloud*`
- **Host pattern** (no leading `/` or `*/`): matched against the parsed hostname for backward-compatible behavior. Examples: `example.com`, `*.example.com`, `*.example.com/*`

Following **own-borrow-over-clone**: Accepts `&str` not `&String`. Following **opt-inline**: Inlined for hot path performance. Following **security-ssrf-prevention**: Always parses URL first; never compares raw strings.

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::domain::pattern_matching::matches_pattern;

// Path pattern: matches URL path
assert!(matches_pattern("https://example.com/pricing", "/pricing"));
assert!(matches_pattern("https://example.com/admin/settings", "/admin/*"));
assert!(!matches_pattern("https://example.com/page", "/admin/*"));

// Host pattern: matches hostname (backward-compatible)
assert!(matches_pattern("https://blog.example.com/page", "*.example.com"));
assert!(matches_pattern("https://example.com/page", "example.com"));
assert!(!matches_pattern("https://evil.com/page", "example.com"));
```

Expand description



Outcome returned by a [`PipelineStage`](trait.PipelineStage.html "trait webfang_core::domain::pipeline_item::PipelineStage") after processing an item.

Controls whether the pipeline continues, short-circuits, or rejects an item.

Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left` is `true`. Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right "variant either::Either::Right") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") otherwise. where F: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html" class="trait" title="trait core::ops::function::FnOnce">FnOnce</a>(&Self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>,







Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left(&self)` returns `true`. Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right "variant either::Either::Right") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") otherwise. [Read more](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/into_either/trait.IntoEither.html#method.into_either_with)

# Struct ScrapedItem

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/pipeline_item.rs.html#14-33" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct ScrapedItem {
    pub url: String,
    pub raw_html: String,
    pub text_content: Option<String>,
    pub metadata: HashMap<String, String>,
    pub status_code: u16,
    pub embeddings: Option<Vec<f32>>,
}
```

Expand description



A scraped item flowing through the processing pipeline.

Represents raw or partially-processed data from a web page. Each [`PipelineStage`](trait.PipelineStage.html "trait webfang_core::domain::pipeline_item::PipelineStage") receives and optionally transforms a `ScrapedItem`.

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[domain](../index.html)::[pipeline_item](index.html)



# Trait PipelineStage

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/pipeline_item.rs.html#95-102" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait PipelineStage: Send + Sync {
    // Required methods
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
    fn process(
        &self,
        item: ScrapedItem,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = StageOutcome> + Send + '_>>;
}
```

Expand description



A single processing step in the item pipeline.

Implementors transform a [`ScrapedItem`](struct.ScrapedItem.html "struct webfang_core::domain::pipeline_item::ScrapedItem") and return a [`StageOutcome`](enum.StageOutcome.html "enum webfang_core::domain::pipeline_item::StageOutcome") indicating whether processing should continue, skip, or reject.

## <a href="#requirements" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Requirements

- `Send + Sync` — stages must be safe to share across async tasks.
- Use native `async fn` in traits (Rust 1.75+).



## Required Methods<a href="#required-methods" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/pipeline_item.rs.html#97" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### fn <a href="#tymethod.name" class="fn">name</a>(&self) -\> &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>





Human-readable name for logging/diagnostics.





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/pipeline_item.rs.html#100-101" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### fn <a href="#tymethod.process" class="fn">process</a>( &self, item: <a href="struct.ScrapedItem.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::domain::pipeline_item::ScrapedItem">ScrapedItem</a>, ) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/pin/struct.Pin.html" class="struct" title="struct core::pin::Pin">Pin</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::boxed::Box">Box</a>\<dyn <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/future/future/trait.Future.html" class="trait" title="trait core::future::future::Future">Future</a>\<Output = <a href="enum.StageOutcome.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::domain::pipeline_item::StageOutcome">StageOutcome</a>\> + <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Send.html" class="trait" title="trait core::marker::Send">Send</a> + '\_\>\>





Process an item and decide the next pipeline action.

Expand description



Port trait for downloading assets (images, documents).

Abstracts asset downloading so application services don’t depend on specific download implementations. The production adapter streams to disk with ~8KB RAM; tests inject mocks that count calls.

Expand description



Port trait for writing binary payloads (PDFs, images, archives) to disk.

Abstracts filesystem persistence so application use cases never call `std::fs` directly — Clean Architecture keeps the application layer free of filesystem specifics (issue \#442). The production adapter [`FsBinaryWriter`](../../infrastructure/crawler/binary_writer/struct.FsBinaryWriter.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::crawler::binary_writer::FsBinaryWriter") creates the parent directory tree and writes the bytes; tests inject a temp-dir or in-memory implementation.

# Trait ProgressObserver

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/ports.rs.html#120-159" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait ProgressObserver: Send + Sync {
    // Required methods
    fn on_page_started<'a>(
        &'a self,
        url: &'a str,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = ()> + Send + 'a>>;
    fn on_status_changed<'a>(
        &'a self,
        url: &'a str,
        status: ScrapeStatus,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = ()> + Send + 'a>>;
    fn on_page_completed<'a>(
        &'a self,
        url: &'a str,
        chars: usize,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = ()> + Send + 'a>>;
    fn on_page_failed<'a>(
        &'a self,
        url: &'a str,
        error: &'a ScrapeError,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = ()> + Send + 'a>>;
    fn on_robots_blocked<'a>(
        &'a self,
        url: &'a str,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = ()> + Send + 'a>>;
    fn on_finished<'a>(
        &'a self,
        total: usize,
        successful: usize,
        failed: usize,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = ()> + Send + 'a>>;
}
```

Expand description



Port trait for real-time progress reporting during scraping.

Implementations receive structured progress events as the scraper processes each URL. The trait is `Send + Sync` so observers can be shared across async tasks.

# Function profile_from_name

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/profile.rs.html#21-26" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn profile_from_name(name: &str) -> Option<Profile>
```

Expand description



Resolve a profile name to a \[`Profile`\].

Accepts the exact variant name of the \[`Profile`\] enum (e.g. `"Chrome120"`, `"SafariIos18_1_1"`). Matching is case-sensitive and covers the full catalog: the lookup is driven by \[`Profile::VARIANTS`\], so profiles added by future `wreq-util` upgrades are accepted automatically.

Returns `None` for unknown names; each caller decides its failure policy (hard error for page-fetch, warn + fallback for assets).

Defines the contract for persisting and retrieving crawl data. Implementations can use files, databases, or other storage backends.

#### fn <a href="#method.load_all" class="fn">load_all</a>(&self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>\<<a href="../entities/content/struct.ScrapedContent.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::domain::entities::content::ScrapedContent">ScrapedContent</a>\>, <a href="../error/enum.CrawlError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::domain::error::CrawlError">CrawlError</a>\>





Load all persisted content in bulk.

Returns every saved [`ScrapedContent`](../entities/content/struct.ScrapedContent.html "struct webfang_core::domain::entities::content::ScrapedContent") item. This is the bulk alternative to the `get_all_urls` → `find_by_url` loop, avoiding an N+1 query pattern for consumers that need the whole result set (e.g. the MCP export tools).

The default implementation iterates `get_all_urls` and resolves each URL via `find_by_url`. Implementations with direct storage access SHOULD override this with a single sequential scan for efficiency.

##### <a href="#returns-3" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

- `Ok(Vec<ScrapedContent>)` - All persisted content
- `Err(CrawlError)` - Query error

# Trait VectorRepository

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/repository.rs.html#37-101" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait VectorRepository: Send + Sync {
    // Required methods
    fn save_resource<'a>(
        &'a self,
        url: &'a str,
        title: &'a str,
        content_hash: &'a str,
        size_bytes: u64,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<String, ScraperError>> + Send + 'a>>;
    fn save_chunk<'a>(
        &'a self,
        id: &'a str,
        resource_url: &'a str,
        chunk_index: i64,
        content: &'a str,
        embedding: Option<&'a [f32]>,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<(), ScraperError>> + Send + 'a>>;
    fn resource_exists_by_hash<'a>(
        &'a self,
        content_hash: &'a str,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Option<String>, ScraperError>> + Send + 'a>>;
    fn get_vector<'a>(
        &'a self,
        chunk_id: &'a str,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Option<Vec<f32>>, ScraperError>> + Send + 'a>>;
}
```

Expand description



Domain trait for vector persistence (dependency inversion).

Implementations store crawl resources (with content-hash deduplication) and semantic chunks whose embeddings are serialized as raw little-endian `f32` BLOBs (frozen design decision \#7).

All database failures surface as [`ScraperError::Persistence`](../../error/enum.ScraperError.html#variant.Persistence "variant webfang_core::error::ScraperError::Persistence") (frozen decision \#4: no separate `StorageError` enum), matching the pattern established by PR1.

The methods are desugared to `Pin<Box<dyn Future<…> + Send + '_>>` so the trait is dyn-compatible (A1, spec S3.4) without the `async_trait` crate.

#### fn <a href="#tymethod.save_resource" class="fn">save_resource</a>\<'a\>( &'a self, url: &'a <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>, title: &'a <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>, content_hash: &'a <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>, size_bytes: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.u64.html" class="primitive">u64</a>, ) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/pin/struct.Pin.html" class="struct" title="struct core::pin::Pin">Pin</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::boxed::Box">Box</a>\<dyn <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/future/future/trait.Future.html" class="trait" title="trait core::future::future::Future">Future</a>\<Output = <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>, <a href="../../error/enum.ScraperError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError">ScraperError</a>\>\> + <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Send.html" class="trait" title="trait core::marker::Send">Send</a> + 'a\>\>





Save a resource with its content hash. Returns the resource URL.

If a resource with the same `content_hash` already exists, this short-circuits (dedup, frozen decision \#3) and returns the **existing** URL without inserting a duplicate row — saving the heavier chunk inserts.

##### <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`ScraperError::Persistence`](../../error/enum.ScraperError.html#variant.Persistence "variant webfang_core::error::ScraperError::Persistence") on any database failure.

Save a chunk, optionally with its embedding vector.

When `embedding` is `Some`, it is serialized to a little-endian `f32` BLOB; when `None`, the `embedding_vector` column is stored as SQL `NULL`.

##### <a href="#errors-1" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`ScraperError::Persistence`](../../error/enum.ScraperError.html#variant.Persistence "variant webfang_core::error::ScraperError::Persistence") on any database failure (e.g. a foreign-key violation if `resource_url` was never saved first).

Get the embedding vector for a chunk.

Returns `Ok(Some(vec))` if the chunk exists and has an embedding, `Ok(None)` if the chunk is missing or has a `NULL` embedding, or an error if the stored BLOB is corrupt (length not a multiple of 4).

### impl\<T: <a href="trait.VectorRepository.html" class="trait" title="trait webfang_core::domain::repository::VectorRepository">VectorRepository</a> + ?<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Sized.html" class="trait" title="trait core::marker::Sized">Sized</a>\> <a href="trait.VectorRepository.html" class="trait" title="trait webfang_core::domain::repository::VectorRepository">VectorRepository</a> for <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::sync::Arc">Arc</a>\<T\>



Blanket impl so `Arc<dyn VectorRepository + Send + Sync>` satisfies `R: VectorRepository + Send + Sync` in [`crate::application::elastic_ingestion::ElasticIngestion<R>`](../../application/elastic_ingestion/struct.ElasticIngestion.html "struct webfang_core::application::elastic_ingestion::ElasticIngestion") (spec S3.4).







Delegates each method through the `Arc` deref to the inner repository. This is the bridge that lets the Container store `Option<Arc<ElasticIngestion<Arc<dyn VectorRepository + Send + Sync>>>>` for runtime repo dispatch (SQLite when `persistence` is ON, StreamRepository when OFF).

# Type Alias DynVectorRepository

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/repository.rs.html#156" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub type DynVectorRepository = Arc<dyn VectorRepository + Send + Sync>;
```

Expand description



Erased vector repository for runtime dispatch.

Lets the Container hold either the SQLite-backed [`crate::infrastructure::persistence::sqlite::SqliteVectorRepository`](../../infrastructure/persistence/sqlite/struct.SqliteVectorRepository.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::persistence::sqlite::SqliteVectorRepository") (under the `persistence` feature) or the dependency-free `StreamRepository` JSONL sink behind a single type, enabling `Arc<dyn VectorRepository + Send + Sync>` to satisfy the `R: VectorRepository + Send + Sync` bound on [`crate::application::elastic_ingestion::ElasticIngestion`](../../application/elastic_ingestion/struct.ElasticIngestion.html "struct webfang_core::application::elastic_ingestion::ElasticIngestion").

# Trait SemanticCleaner

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/semantic_cleaner.rs.html#70-173" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait SemanticCleaner:
    Sealed
    + Send
    + Sync {
    // Required methods
    fn clean<'a>(
        &'a self,
        html: &'a str,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Vec<DocumentChunk>, SemanticError>> + Send + 'a>>;
    fn max_tokens(&self) -> usize;
    fn is_ready(&self) -> bool;
}
```

Expand description



Semantic Cleaner — AI-powered content cleaning interface

This trait defines the contract for cleaning HTML content using AI models. Implementations use ONNX models (sentence-transformers) to:

- Split content into semantic chunks
- Validate chunk sizes (token limits)
- Prepare content for embedding generation

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
let html = "<html><body><p>Hello World</p></body></html>";
let chunks = cleaner.clean(html).await?;
println!("Generated {} chunks", chunks.len());
```



## <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`SemanticError`](../../error/enum.SemanticError.html "enum webfang_core::error::SemanticError") in these cases:

- [`SemanticError::ModelLoad`](../../error/enum.SemanticError.html#variant.ModelLoad "variant webfang_core::error::SemanticError::ModelLoad"): Failed to load ONNX model from cache
- [`SemanticError::Tokenize`](../../error/enum.SemanticError.html#variant.Tokenize "variant webfang_core::error::SemanticError::Tokenize"): Tokenization failed (invalid input)
- [`SemanticError::Inference`](../../error/enum.SemanticError.html#variant.Inference "variant webfang_core::error::SemanticError::Inference"): ONNX inference failed
- [`SemanticError::ChunkTooLarge`](../../error/enum.SemanticError.html#variant.ChunkTooLarge "variant webfang_core::error::SemanticError::ChunkTooLarge"): Content exceeds model’s token limit
- [`SemanticError::Download`](../../error/enum.SemanticError.html#variant.Download "variant webfang_core::error::SemanticError::Download"): Model download failed (if auto-download enabled)

## <a href="#implementation-notes" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Implementation Notes

- Implementations MUST be thread-safe (`Send + Sync`)
- Implementations MUST cache models to avoid reloading
- Implementations MUST use memory-mapped files for large models (`mem-zero-copy`)



## Required Methods<a href="#required-methods" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/semantic_cleaner.rs.html#123-126" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### fn <a href="#tymethod.clean" class="fn">clean</a>\<'a\>( &'a self, html: &'a <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>, ) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/pin/struct.Pin.html" class="struct" title="struct core::pin::Pin">Pin</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::boxed::Box">Box</a>\<dyn <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/future/future/trait.Future.html" class="trait" title="trait core::future::future::Future">Future</a>\<Output = <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>\<<a href="../entities/content/struct.DocumentChunk.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::domain::entities::content::DocumentChunk">DocumentChunk</a>\>, <a href="../../error/enum.SemanticError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::SemanticError">SemanticError</a>\>\> + <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Send.html" class="trait" title="trait core::marker::Send">Send</a> + 'a\>\>





Clean HTML content and split into semantic chunks

This is the main entry point for semantic cleaning. It:

1.  Strips HTML tags and extracts text
2.  Splits text into semantic chunks (paragraphs, sections)
3.  Validates chunk sizes against model token limits
4.  Returns chunks ready for embedding generation

##### <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `html` - Raw HTML content to clean (borrowed, `&str` not `&String`)

##### <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

- `Ok(Vec<DocumentChunk>)` - Successfully cleaned chunks
- `Err(SemanticError)` - Cleaning failed

##### <a href="#errors-1" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`SemanticError::ChunkTooLarge`](../../error/enum.SemanticError.html#variant.ChunkTooLarge "variant webfang_core::error::SemanticError::ChunkTooLarge") if any chunk exceeds the model’s token limit (32768 tokens for IBM Granite-97M).

Returns [`SemanticError::Tokenize`](../../error/enum.SemanticError.html#variant.Tokenize "variant webfang_core::error::SemanticError::Tokenize") if the input contains invalid UTF-8 or special characters that break tokenization.

##### <a href="#examples-1" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
let html = "<article><h1>Title</h1><p>Content here...</p></article>";
let chunks = cleaner.clean(html).await?;

for chunk in &chunks {
    println!("Chunk {}: {} chars", chunk.id, chunk.content.len());
}
```



##### <a href="#performance" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Performance

- **First call**: May trigger model download (~90MB) + load (~100-500ms)
- **Subsequent calls**: Cache hit, ~10-50ms per page
- **Memory**: Uses memory-mapped files, ~90MB virtual memory (not RSS)

##### <a href="#note" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Note

Desugared to a boxed future (`Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send>>`) instead of `async fn` so the trait stays dyn-compatible (`Box<dyn SemanticCleaner>`). The single lifetime `'a` ties `&self` and `html` to the returned future, matching the `async-trait` macro’s default desugaring.





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/semantic_cleaner.rs.html#146" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### fn <a href="#tymethod.max_tokens" class="fn">max_tokens</a>(&self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.usize.html" class="primitive">usize</a>





Get the model’s maximum token limit

This is useful for validating content before processing.

##### <a href="#returns-1" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

Maximum number of tokens the model accepts per chunk. For `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, this is 512 tokens.

##### <a href="#examples-2" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
fn example(cleaner: &dyn SemanticCleaner) {
    let max_tokens = cleaner.max_tokens();
    println!("Model accepts up to {} tokens per chunk", max_tokens);
}
```







<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/semantic_cleaner.rs.html#172" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### fn <a href="#tymethod.is_ready" class="fn">is_ready</a>(&self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>





Check if the model is ready for inference

This method verifies that:

- Model file exists in cache
- Model file passes SHA256 validation
- Model can be loaded into memory

##### <a href="#returns-2" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

- `true` - Model is ready
- `false` - Model needs download or reload

##### <a href="#examples-3" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
fn example(cleaner: &dyn SemanticCleaner) {
    if cleaner.is_ready() {
        println!("Model ready for inference");
    } else {
        println!("Model needs download or reload");
    }
}
```

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[domain](../index.html)::[semantic_inspector](index.html)



# Trait SemanticInspectorPort

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/semantic_inspector.rs.html#54-64" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait SemanticInspectorPort: Send + Sync {
    // Required method
    fn find_semantic_match<'a>(
        &'a self,
        ctx: SemanticContext,
    ) -> BoxFuture<'a, Result<Option<SemanticMatch>, SelectorErrorKind>>;
}
```

Expand description



Domain trait for semantic (embedding-based) CSS selector repair.

Implementations use vector embeddings to find the best matching selector when lexical similarity (Tier 1) is insufficient. The trait is dyn-compatible via `BoxFuture` (matching `VectorRepository` in `repository.rs`).



## Required Methods<a href="#required-methods" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/semantic_inspector.rs.html#60-63" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### fn <a href="#tymethod.find_semantic_match" class="fn">find_semantic_match</a>\<'a\>( &'a self, ctx: <a href="struct.SemanticContext.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::domain::semantic_inspector::SemanticContext">SemanticContext</a>, ) -\> <a href="type.BoxFuture.html" class="type" title="type webfang_core::domain::semantic_inspector::BoxFuture">BoxFuture</a>\<'a, <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/option/enum.Option.html" class="enum" title="enum core::option::Option">Option</a>\<<a href="struct.SemanticMatch.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::domain::semantic_inspector::SemanticMatch">SemanticMatch</a>\>, <a href="../dom_inspector/enum.SelectorErrorKind.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::domain::dom_inspector::SelectorErrorKind">SelectorErrorKind</a>\>\>





Find the best semantic match for a failed selector.

Returns `Ok(Some(match))` if a candidate exceeds the confidence threshold, `Ok(None)` if no candidate is good enough, or `Err(SelectorErrorKind)` on infrastructure failure.

``` rust
pub struct SessionId(pub usize);
```

Expand description



Unique identifier for a session slot within a domain pool.

Defined in the domain layer so that `SessionPort` and its consumers never depend on infrastructure types. Infrastructure converts internally when needed.

# Trait SessionPort

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/session_port.rs.html#28-41" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait SessionPort: Send + Sync {
    // Required methods
    fn acquire(&self, domain: &str) -> Option<SessionId>;
    fn report_success(&self, domain: &str, session: SessionId);
    fn report_failure(&self, domain: &str, session: SessionId, status: u16);
}
```

Expand description



Port trait for per-domain session health management.

Implemented by [`crate::infrastructure::network::session_pool::DomainSessionPool`](../../infrastructure/network/session_pool/struct.DomainSessionPool.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::network::session_pool::DomainSessionPool") in infrastructure. The application layer uses this trait — never the concrete pool type.

``` rust
}
```

Crawler configuration with builder pattern

Following **api-builder**: Provides fluent builder API. Following **api-non-exhaustive**: Can evolve without breaking changes.

# Trait TextChunker

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/text_chunker.rs.html#17-28" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait TextChunker: Send + Sync {
    // Required method
    fn chunk_text(&self, text: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, SemanticError>;

```

Expand description



Domain trait for text segmentation into semantic chunks.

Implementations split raw text into chunks suitable for embedding. The trait is dyn-compatible (no generics, no `async`) so it can be stored as `Arc<dyn TextChunker>` in the Container.
