[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[domain](../index.html)::[url_validation](index.html)



# Function extract_domain

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/url_validation.rs.html#111-115" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn extract_domain(url: &str) -> Option<String>
```

Expand description



Extract the host (domain) from a URL, without any port component.

Uses [`url::Url::host_str`](https://docs.rs/url/2.5.7/url/struct.Url.html#method.host_str "method url::Url::host_str") for RFC 3986 compliant parsing. Unlike naive `split(':')` approaches, this correctly returns the host WITHOUT the port:

- Ports: `http://127.0.0.1:8080/page` → `127.0.0.1`
- Credentials: `http://user:pass@domain.com` → `domain.com`
- IPv6: `http://[::1]:8080` → `[::1]`

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `url` - URL to extract the host from

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

The host without port, or `None` if the URL cannot be parsed or has no host.

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::domain::url_validation::extract_domain;

assert_eq!(extract_domain("http://127.0.0.1:8080/page"), Some("127.0.0.1".to_string()));
assert_eq!(extract_domain("https://example.com/path"), Some("example.com".to_string()));
assert_eq!(extract_domain("http://[::1]:8080"), Some("[::1]".to_string()));
assert_eq!(extract_domain("not-a-url"), None);
```
















[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[domain](../index.html)::[url_validation](index.html)



# Function is_internal_link

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/url_validation.rs.html#217-222" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn is_internal_link(url: &str, seed_domain: &str) -> bool
```

Expand description



Check whether a URL is internal to a seed domain (same host or subdomain).

Both the URL host and the seed are normalized to bare hosts (port and `www.` stripped) before comparison, so URLs with an explicit port or a `www.` prefix mismatch are handled correctly. This is the single canonical implementation shared by the crawl engine and the MCP `is_internal_link` tool (#479, \#500).

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `url` - URL to classify
- `seed_domain` - Seed host or full URL to compare against

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

`true` if `url`’s host equals the seed host or is a subdomain of it.

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::domain::url_validation::is_internal_link;

assert!(is_internal_link("https://example.com/page", "example.com"));
assert!(is_internal_link("https://blog.example.com/post", "example.com"));
// The port case that broke the crawl engine (#479):
assert!(is_internal_link("http://127.0.0.1:8080/page", "127.0.0.1"));
assert!(!is_internal_link("http://other.com:8080/x", "example.com"));
// The www asymmetry that broke DOM discovery (#500):
assert!(is_internal_link("https://gnu.org/page", "www.gnu.org"));
assert!(is_internal_link("https://www.gnu.org/page", "gnu.org"));
assert!(is_internal_link("https://www.gnu.org/page", "www.gnu.org"));
```
















[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[domain](../index.html)::[url_validation](index.html)



# Function normalize_seed_host

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/url_validation.rs.html#157-170" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn normalize_seed_host(seed: &str) -> String
```

Expand description



Normalize a seed reference to a bare host string (no scheme, port, path, or `www.` prefix).

Accepts both full URLs and bare hosts:

- Full URL: `https://example.com:9090/path` → `example.com` (via [`url::Url::host_str`](https://docs.rs/url/2.5.7/url/struct.Url.html#method.host_str "method url::Url::host_str"), which drops the port).
- Bare host: `example.com/path` → `example.com` (path stripped) and `example.com:8080` → `example.com` (port stripped).

The `www.` prefix is stripped so that seed hosts are compared on the same footing as links normalized with `strip_www=true` (#500). Without this, a `www.`-prefixed seed (`www.gnu.org`) never matches its stripped links (`gnu.org`), silently dropping every internal URL on most real-world sites.

This is the canonical seed-host normalizer shared by the crawl engine and the MCP `is_internal_link` tool, so both classify links against the same bare host.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `seed` - Seed URL or bare host to normalize

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

The bare host component, without a leading `www.`.

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::domain::url_validation::normalize_seed_host;

assert_eq!(normalize_seed_host("https://example.com/path"), "example.com");
assert_eq!(normalize_seed_host("example.com"), "example.com");
assert_eq!(normalize_seed_host("example.com/path"), "example.com");
assert_eq!(normalize_seed_host("example.com:8080"), "example.com");
// www stripping (#500):
assert_eq!(normalize_seed_host("https://www.example.com/path"), "example.com");
assert_eq!(normalize_seed_host("www.example.com"), "example.com");
```
















[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[domain](../index.html)::[url_validation](index.html)



# Function normalize_url

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/url_validation.rs.html#281-307" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn normalize_url(url: &str, strip_www: bool) -> String
```

Expand description



Normalize a URL (remove fragments, strip www, remove default ports, etc.)

This is the **canonical** URL normalizer for the scraper. All URL normalization should go through this function. It lives in the domain layer so both the application deduplicators and the infrastructure crawlers share one canonical form for URL equivalence — two URLs that normalize to the same string are treated as the same document (#517).

Options:

- `strip_hash: true` — removes URL fragments (`#section`)
- `strip_www` — removes `www.` prefix when `true` (caller controls behavior)
- `remove_trailing_slash: false` — preserves trailing slashes on nested paths (`/page/` stays distinct from `/page`); a bare root is still canonicalized to `https://host` by url-normalize
- `remove_query_parameters: All` — strips query strings for dedup
- `sort_query_parameters: true` — consistent ordering

After normalization, a trailing `/index.html` or `/index.htm` path segment is collapsed to `/` (case-insensitive, idempotent) so the same document is not stored under two URLs.

Non-URLs (strings without a `://` scheme) are returned unchanged — a bare `not-a-valid-url` is never coerced into `http://not-a-valid-url`.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `url` - URL to normalize
- `strip_www` - If `true`, removes `www.` prefix (e.g. `www.example.com` → `example.com`)

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::domain::url_validation::normalize_url;

assert_eq!(
    normalize_url("https://example.com/page#section", true),
    "https://example.com/page"
);
assert_eq!(
    normalize_url("https://www.example.com/page", true),
    "https://example.com/page"
);
assert_eq!(
    normalize_url("https://www.example.com/page", false),
    "https://www.example.com/page"
);
assert_eq!(
    normalize_url("https://example.com:443/page", true),
    "https://example.com/page"
);
assert_eq!(
    normalize_url("https://example.com/index.html", true),
    "https://example.com"
);
```
















[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[domain](../index.html)::[url_validation](index.html)



# Function validate_and_parse_url

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/url_validation.rs.html#59-81" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn validate_and_parse_url(url: &str) -> Result<Url>
```

Expand description



Validate and parse a URL string using the `url` crate (RFC 3986 compliant).

This function performs strict URL validation:

- Trims whitespace automatically
- Requires http or https scheme (case-insensitive)
- Requires a valid host
- Rejects malformed URLs

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `url` - URL string to validate and parse

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

- `Ok(url::Url)` - Validated and parsed URL
- `Err(ScraperError::InvalidUrl)` - Invalid URL with error message

## <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns an error if:

- URL is empty
- URL has invalid format
- URL scheme is not http or https
- URL has no host

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::validate_and_parse_url;

// Valid URLs
let url = validate_and_parse_url("https://example.com").unwrap();
assert_eq!(url.host_str(), Some("example.com"));

let url = validate_and_parse_url("HTTP://EXAMPLE.COM").unwrap();
assert_eq!(url.scheme(), "http");

// Invalid URLs
assert!(validate_and_parse_url("").is_err());
assert!(validate_and_parse_url("ftp://example.com").is_err());
assert!(validate_and_parse_url("not-a-url").is_err());
```



## <a href="#whitespace-handling" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Whitespace Handling

Leading and trailing whitespace is automatically trimmed:



``` rust
use webfang_core::validate_and_parse_url;

let url = validate_and_parse_url("  https://example.com  ").unwrap();
assert_eq!(url.host_str(), Some("example.com"));
```

# Struct StaticUrlValidator

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/url_validator.rs.html#43" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct StaticUrlValidator;
```

Expand description



Pure, stateless implementation of `UrlValidatorTrait`.

Contains the core business rules that don’t require HTTP calls. Suitable for tests and non-network validation scenarios.

# Trait UrlValidatorTrait

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/url_validator.rs.html#23-37" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait UrlValidatorTrait: Send + Sync {
    // Required method
    fn filter_invalid_patterns(&self, url: &Url) -> ValidationResult;

    // Provided method
    fn validate_http_status(
        &self,
        _url: &Url,
    ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<ValidationResult, DomainError>> + Send { ... }
}
```

Expand description



Trait for URL validation logic.

Domain defines the contract; infrastructure provides HTTP-aware implementations while the domain itself provides a pure, stateless implementation (`StaticUrlValidator`) suitable for tests.

Uses native `impl Future` return position in trait (Rust 1.88+), no `async-trait` crate needed.


Expand description



W3C TraceContext CorrelationId value object

Provides W3C-compliant traceparent headers for distributed tracing. Generates UUID v7 for the trace_id (timestamp + random) and a random span_id for span identification.

## <a href="#w3c-traceparent-format" class="doc-anchor">§</a>W3C Traceparent Format

`00-{trace_id}-{span_id}-{trace_flags}`

- trace_id: 32-character lowercase hex (UUID v7)
- span_id: 16-character lowercase hex
- trace_flags: 01 (sampled)

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::domain::value_objects::CorrelationId;

let correlation_id = CorrelationId::new();
let traceparent = correlation_id.to_traceparent();
assert!(traceparent.starts_with("00-"));
```

Create CorrelationId from existing trace_id and span_id

Useful for propagating existing correlation IDs through the system.





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/value_objects.rs.html#84-91" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.child" class="fn">child</a>(&self) -\> Self





Create a child correlation ID: same `trace_id`, fresh `span_id`.

Used to correlate multiple operations under a single trace while giving each its own span identity — e.g. every page of a crawl shares the crawl’s `trace_id` but gets a unique `span_id`, so the whole crawl can be reconstructed by `trace_id` while each page stays distinguishable.

##### <a href="#examples-2" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::domain::value_objects::CorrelationId;

let crawl = CorrelationId::new();
let page = crawl.child();
assert_eq!(crawl.trace_id(), page.trace_id());
assert_ne!(crawl.span_id(), page.span_id());
```

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[domain](../index.html)::[value_objects](index.html)



# Struct ValidUrl

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/domain/value_objects.rs.html#157" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct ValidUrl(/* private fields */);
```

Expand description



Validated URL newtype - guarantees URL is valid at type level

This enforces that ScrapedContent always has a valid URL, preventing runtime errors from invalid URLs.

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::domain::ValidUrl;

// Create from parsed URL
let url = url::Url::parse("https://example.com").unwrap();
let valid = ValidUrl::new(url);
assert_eq!(valid.as_str(), "https://example.com/");  // URL adds trailing slash

// Or parse directly
let valid = ValidUrl::parse("https://example.com").unwrap();
assert!(valid.as_str().starts_with("https://example.com"));
```

Parse and create a ValidUrl from a string

Returns error if the string is not a valid URL.

##### <a href="#examples-1" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::domain::ValidUrl;

let url = ValidUrl::parse("https://example.com").unwrap();
assert_eq!(url.host_str(), Some("example.com"));

let invalid = ValidUrl::parse("not-a-url");
assert!(invalid.is_err());
```

[webfang_core](../index.html)::[error](index.html)



# Enum ErrorClass

<a href="../../src/webfang_core/error.rs.html#549-558" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum ErrorClass {
    TransientRetriable,
    TransientBackoff,
    PermanentFatal,
    InternalFatal,
}
```

Expand description



Operational classification of errors for observability and retry logic.

Partitions ScraperError variants by severity and recoverability.



## Variants<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="#variant.TransientRetriable" class="anchor">§</a>

### TransientRetriable





Transient errors that should be retried immediately (e.g., connection reset, 5xx)





<a href="#variant.TransientBackoff" class="anchor">§</a>

### TransientBackoff





Transient errors that require backoff before retry (e.g., rate limit, slowloris)





<a href="#variant.PermanentFatal" class="anchor">§</a>

### PermanentFatal





Permanent errors that cannot be recovered by retry (e.g., 4xx, invalid URL, WAF)





<a href="#variant.InternalFatal" class="anchor">§</a>

### InternalFatal





Internal errors that indicate a bug (e.g., integer overflow, semaphore exhaustion)

# Enum ScraperError

<a href="../../src/webfang_core/error.rs.html#16-181" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum ScraperError {
InvalidUrl(String),
    Http {
        status: u16,
        url: String,
    },
    Readability(String),
    Io(Error),
    Network(Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>),
    Middleware(String),
    Serialization(Error),
    Yaml(Error),
    UrlParse(ParseError),
    Extraction(String),
    Download(Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>),
    Config(String),
    FeatureGated(String),
    WafBlocked {
        url: String,
        provider: String,
    },
    Validation(String),
    Conversion(String),
    Export(String),
    ExtractionFailed {
        url: String,
        reason: String,
    },
    ExportBatch(String),
    GlobalTimeout,
    SlowlorisTimeout,
    PayloadTooLarge,
    SemaphoreInanition,
    Persistence(String),
    Ingestion(String),
    Semantic(SemanticError),
    H2Config(String),
    Internal(String),
    RateLimited(u64),
    CrawlLimit(String),
    SitemapNotFound(String),
}
```

Expand description



Main error type for the scraper library.

Each variant represents a specific failure mode, making it easy to:

- Handle specific errors in calling code
- Convert to/from other error types
- Provide meaningful error messages to users

### Network(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::boxed::Box">Box</a>\<dyn <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/error/trait.Error.html" class="trait" title="trait core::error::Error">Error</a> + <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Send.html" class="trait" title="trait core::marker::Send">Send</a> + <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Sync.html" class="trait" title="trait core::marker::Sync">Sync</a>\>)

<a href="#variant.WafBlocked" class="anchor">§</a>

### WafBlocked





WAF/CAPTCHA challenge detected in HTTP 200 response

The `provider` field carries the full Spanish evidence chain (`provider (patrón: …, tier: …)` per evidence, joined by `; `) when raised from a context-aware inspection verdict (REQ-WAF-08); legacy callers may still pass a bare provider name.





#### Fields



<a href="#variant.WafBlocked.field.url" class="anchor field">§</a>`url: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>

Detected WAF provider or formatted evidence chain (e.g. `"Cloudflare"`, or `"Cloudflare (patrón: cf-turnstile, tier: desafío); …"`)

### Persistence(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>)





Persistence error (SQLite storage layer — resources/chunks CRUD, pool).

Holds the underlying error rendered to a string so it uniformly covers both `rusqlite::Error` and `deadpool_sqlite` pool errors (which are different types) without forcing two `#[from]` variants.

<a href="#variant.RateLimited" class="anchor">§</a>

### RateLimited(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.u64.html" class="primitive">u64</a>)





Rate limited by the server; carries the retry-after delay in seconds.

Classifies as [`ErrorClass::TransientBackoff`](enum.ErrorClass.html#variant.TransientBackoff "variant webfang_core::error::ErrorClass::TransientBackoff") — callers should wait the indicated delay before retrying. Display is deliberately identical to `CrawlError::RateLimited` so the message survives layer conversion.





<a href="#variant.CrawlLimit" class="anchor">§</a>

### CrawlLimit(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>)





Crawl limit exceeded.

Groups all crawl-budget configuration limits — max-depth, max-pages, and sitemap-depth. All three are `PermanentFatal` configuration boundaries (see [`Self::classify`](enum.ScraperError.html#method.classify "method webfang_core::error::ScraperError::classify")); the payload carries the human-readable limit description rendered verbatim by `Display`.

Sitemap not found during auto-discovery

# Enum SemanticError

<a href="../../src/webfang_core/error.rs.html#205-308" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum SemanticError {
    ModelLoad(Error),
    Tokenize(String),
    Inference(String),
    ChunkTooLarge {
        chunk_id: String,
        tokens: usize,
        max: usize,
    },
    Download {
        repo: String,
        cause: String,
    },
    CacheValidation {
        repo: String,
        expected: String,
        actual: String,
    },
    OfflineMode {
        repo: String,
    },
    InvalidThreshold {
        value: f32,
    },
}
```

Expand description



Semantic cleaning errors (AI/ML operations)

These errors occur during AI-powered semantic cleaning operations:

- Model loading from cache
- Tokenization of input text
- ONNX inference
- Model download from HuggingFace Hub

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::error::SemanticError;
use std::io;

let io_err = io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotFound, "model file missing");
let semantic_err = SemanticError::ModelLoad(io_err);
assert!(semantic_err.to_string().contains("modelo"));
```





## Variants<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="#variant.ModelLoad" class="anchor">§</a>

### ModelLoad(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/io/error/struct.Error.html" class="struct" title="struct std::io::error::Error">Error</a>)





Failed to load ONNX model from cache

This occurs when:

- Model file doesn’t exist in cache
- Model file is corrupted
- Memory mapping failed (disk full, permissions)





<a href="#variant.Tokenize" class="anchor">§</a>

### Tokenize(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>)





Tokenization failed

This occurs when:

- Input text contains invalid UTF-8
- Text exceeds model’s maximum token limit
- Special characters break tokenizer
- Tokenizer file not found





<a href="#variant.Inference" class="anchor">§</a>

### Inference(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>)





ONNX inference failed

This occurs when:

- Model graph execution failed
- Input tensor shape mismatch
- Output tensor extraction failed
- Tensor creation failed





<a href="#variant.ChunkTooLarge" class="anchor">§</a>

### ChunkTooLarge





Content chunk exceeds model’s token limit

This occurs when a single chunk of content has more tokens than the model can handle (32768 tokens for Granite-97M).

#### <a href="#fields-1" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Fields

- `chunk_id` - Identifier of the problematic chunk
- `tokens` - Actual token count
- `max` - Maximum allowed tokens





#### Fields



<a href="#variant.ChunkTooLarge.field.chunk_id" class="anchor field">§</a>`chunk_id: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>



Identifier of the chunk (UUID or index)







<a href="#variant.ChunkTooLarge.field.tokens" class="anchor field">§</a>`tokens: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.usize.html" class="primitive"><code>usize</code></a>



Actual token count







<a href="#variant.ChunkTooLarge.field.max" class="anchor field">§</a>`max: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.usize.html" class="primitive"><code>usize</code></a>



Maximum allowed tokens for this model









<a href="#variant.Download" class="anchor">§</a>

### Download





Model download failed from HuggingFace Hub

This occurs when:

- Network error during download
- Repository doesn’t exist or is private
- Authentication required
- SHA256 validation failed after download





#### Fields



<a href="#variant.Download.field.repo" class="anchor field">§</a>`repo: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>



HuggingFace repository (e.g., “sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2”)







<a href="#variant.Download.field.cause" class="anchor field">§</a>`cause: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>



Underlying error cause









<a href="#variant.CacheValidation" class="anchor">§</a>

### CacheValidation





Cache validation failed (SHA256 mismatch)

This occurs when:

- Downloaded file is corrupted
- Cache was modified externally
- Incomplete download





#### Fields



<a href="#variant.CacheValidation.field.repo" class="anchor field">§</a>`repo: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>



HuggingFace repository







<a href="#variant.CacheValidation.field.expected" class="anchor field">§</a>`expected: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>



Expected SHA256 hash







<a href="#variant.CacheValidation.field.actual" class="anchor field">§</a>`actual: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>



Actual SHA256 hash of downloaded file









<a href="#variant.OfflineMode" class="anchor">§</a>

### OfflineMode





Offline mode: model not available in cache

This occurs when:

- Application is in offline mode
- Model is not cached
- Cannot download from HuggingFace Hub





#### Fields



<a href="#variant.OfflineMode.field.repo" class="anchor field">§</a>`repo: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>



HuggingFace repository









<a href="#variant.InvalidThreshold" class="anchor">§</a>

### InvalidThreshold





Relevance threshold out of valid range \[0.0, 1.0\]

This occurs when:

- User provides a threshold outside the valid range
- Programmatic API receives an invalid threshold value





#### Fields



<a href="#variant.InvalidThreshold.field.value" class="anchor field">§</a>`value: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.f32.html" class="primitive"><code>f32</code></a>



The invalid threshold value provided

# Function detect_ram_budget

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/autotuning.rs.html#96-105" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn detect_ram_budget() -> u64
```

Expand description



Detect the RAM budget via \[`sys_info::mem_info()`\], falling back to 2 GiB.

The `sys_info` syscall is only available under the `persistence` feature (the SQLite path). When `persistence` is OFF the lightweight core binary has no `sys_info` dependency, so detection simply returns the 2 GiB fallback — `ram_budget_from(None)` is already unit-tested.

# Function parse_ram_bytes

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/autotuning.rs.html#189-217" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn parse_ram_bytes(s: &str) -> Option<u64>
```

Expand description



Parse a RAM budget string: plain bytes, or a number with a binary suffix (`B`, `KB`/`KiB`, `MB`/`MiB`, `GB`/`GiB`, `TB`/`TiB`).

Per the hardware-autotuning spec scenario (`--ram-budget 8GB` → `8 * 1024^3`), all suffixes are treated as binary (powers of 1024).














[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../index.html)::[autotuning](index.html)



# Function ram_budget_from

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/autotuning.rs.html#75-87" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn ram_budget_from(total_kib: Option<u64>) -> u64
```

Expand description



Compute the RAM budget (bytes) from an optional total-RAM value in KiB.

- `Some(total_kib)` → `total_kib * 1024 * 0.7` (70% of total RAM, truncated).
- `None` (detection failed) → [`FALLBACK_RAM_BUDGET_BYTES`](constant.FALLBACK_RAM_BUDGET_BYTES.html "constant webfang_core::infrastructure::autotuning::FALLBACK_RAM_BUDGET_BYTES") + a `tracing::warn!`.

Exposed as a pure function (taking the detected value, not calling `sys_info` directly) so the fallback path is unit-testable without mocking the OS.

``` rust
pub struct ElasticConfig {
    pub cpu_cores: usize,
    pub ram_budget_bytes: u64,
    pub max_resource_bytes: u64,
    pub db_pool_size: usize,
    pub db_path: PathBuf,
}
```

Expand description



Resolved elastic ingestion configuration.

Combines auto-detected hardware sizing with the full pipeline parameters. `db_pool_size` is derived as `cpu_cores` with a floor of 4 (frozen decision \#6).

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../index.html)::[bridge](index.html)



# Struct CpuBridge

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/bridge.rs.html#49-52" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct CpuBridge { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Tokio→Rayon crossing for CPU-bound ingestion work (frozen design decision \#3).

Holds a dedicated [`RayonCpuPool`](../cpu_pool/struct.RayonCpuPool.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::cpu_pool::RayonCpuPool") (cloned cheaply — it wraps an `Arc`) and a [`ContentProcessor`](../../domain/content_processor/trait.ContentProcessor.html "trait webfang_core::domain::content_processor::ContentProcessor") strategy for HTML-to-text conversion, plus exposes a generic [`dispatch`](struct.CpuBridge.html#method.dispatch "method webfang_core::infrastructure::bridge::CpuBridge::dispatch") that moves any CPU-bound closure off the event loop, and a typed [`dispatch_resource`](struct.CpuBridge.html#method.dispatch_resource "method webfang_core::infrastructure::bridge::CpuBridge::dispatch_resource") that cleans `DownloadedResource` → `ProcessedResource` via the injected processor.

`CpuBridge` is `Send + Sync` (spec: “dispatch gateway MUST be Send + Sync”), so it can be shared across Tokio tasks via `Arc<CpuBridge>`.



## Implementations<a href="#implementations" class="anchor">§</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.new" class="fn">new</a>(pool: <a href="../cpu_pool/struct.RayonCpuPool.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::cpu_pool::RayonCpuPool">RayonCpuPool</a>, processor: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::sync::Arc">Arc</a>\<dyn <a href="../../domain/content_processor/trait.ContentProcessor.html" class="trait" title="trait webfang_core::domain::content_processor::ContentProcessor">ContentProcessor</a>\>) -\> Self





Wrap a dedicated [`RayonCpuPool`](../cpu_pool/struct.RayonCpuPool.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::cpu_pool::RayonCpuPool") and [`ContentProcessor`](../../domain/content_processor/trait.ContentProcessor.html "trait webfang_core::domain::content_processor::ContentProcessor") in a bridge.





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/bridge.rs.html#63-65" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.pool" class="fn">pool</a>(&self) -\> &<a href="../cpu_pool/struct.RayonCpuPool.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::cpu_pool::RayonCpuPool">RayonCpuPool</a>





Borrow the underlying CPU pool.





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/bridge.rs.html#79-112" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.dispatch" class="fn">dispatch</a>\<F, R\>(&self, work: F) -\> Receiver\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<R, <a href="../../error/enum.ScraperError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError">ScraperError</a>\>\>



where F: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html" class="trait" title="trait core::ops::function::FnOnce">FnOnce</a>() -\> R + <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Send.html" class="trait" title="trait core::marker::Send">Send</a> + 'static, R: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Send.html" class="trait" title="trait core::marker::Send">Send</a> + 'static,







Dispatch an arbitrary CPU-bound closure onto the Rayon pool and return a \[`oneshot::Receiver`\] holding `Result<R, ScraperError>`.

The work runs under `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` + `pool.install`, so the Tokio event loop stays unblocked and any nested `par_iter` routes to the sized dedicated pool. CPU panics are caught via `catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(…))` (frozen user decision \#1) and mapped to [`ScraperError::Ingestion`](../../error/enum.ScraperError.html#variant.Ingestion "variant webfang_core::error::ScraperError::Ingestion") so Rayon threads stay alive.

If the caller drops the receiver before the work finishes (Tokio task abort), `tx.send()` fails and the bridge logs a `tracing::warn!` but does NOT panic (Trap 2).





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/bridge.rs.html#125-151" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.dispatch_resource" class="fn">dispatch_resource</a>( &self, payload: <a href="../crawler/resource_downloader/struct.DownloadedResource.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::crawler::resource_downloader::DownloadedResource">DownloadedResource</a>, ) -\> Receiver\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="struct.ProcessedResource.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::bridge::ProcessedResource">ProcessedResource</a>, <a href="../../error/enum.ScraperError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError">ScraperError</a>\>\>





Typed dispatch: clean a [`DownloadedResource`](../crawler/resource_downloader/struct.DownloadedResource.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::crawler::resource_downloader::DownloadedResource") into a [`ProcessedResource`](struct.ProcessedResource.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::bridge::ProcessedResource") on the Rayon pool.

PR5 wires real `lol_html` boilerplate removal (via `clean_html_to_text`) that strips `script`/`style`/`nav`/`footer`/`aside` chrome and extracts visible text. The cleaner is infallible (`clean_html` falls back to the raw HTML on a `lol_html` parse error), so the work closure returns `ProcessedResource` directly and reuses [`dispatch`](struct.CpuBridge.html#method.dispatch "method webfang_core::infrastructure::bridge::CpuBridge::dispatch")’s single `Result` wrap. Embeddings stay `None` here — ONNX inference is async and runs in the orchestrator’s async layer (Decision 5); the bridge is sync CPU-bound text extraction only.

# Struct ProcessedChunk

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/bridge.rs.html#19-24" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct ProcessedChunk {
    pub content: String,
    pub embedding: Option<Vec<f32>>,
}
```

Expand description



One chunk of cleaned content produced by the bridge.

`embedding` is `None` until PR5 wires the ONNX inference engine (frozen: PR3 ships the CPU-bound isolation mechanism, not the model).

Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left` is `true`. Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right "variant either::Either::Right") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") otherwise. where F: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html" class="trait" title="trait core::ops::function::FnOnce">FnOnce</a>(&Self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>,







Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left(&self)` returns `true`. Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right "variant either::Either::Right") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") otherwise. [Read more](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/into_either/trait.IntoEither.html#method.into_either_with)

# Enum OutputFormat

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/config.rs.html#25-33" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum OutputFormat {
    Markdown,
    Json,
    Text,
}
```

Expand description



Output format for scraped content.

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::OutputFormat;

let format = OutputFormat::Markdown;
assert_eq!(format, OutputFormat::Markdown);
```

# Struct AutotuningConfig

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/config.rs.html#289-294" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct AutotuningConfig {
    pub cpu_cores: usize,
    pub ram_budget_bytes: u64,
}
```

Expand description



Hardware-autotuning configuration snapshot for the elastic ingestion pipeline (Issue \#51).

Serializable so it can be written to / read from a config file. Holds the two core auto-detected sizing values; the fuller [`crate::infrastructure::autotuning::ElasticConfig`](../autotuning/struct.ElasticConfig.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::autotuning::ElasticConfig") adds DB/pool parameters.

Resolution priority (frozen design decision \#12): explicit override \> `WEBFANG_*` env var \> auto-detected default.

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::AutotuningConfig;

// Explicit overrides win.
let cfg = AutotuningConfig::resolve(Some(4), Some(8 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024));
assert_eq!(cfg.cpu_cores, 4);
assert_eq!(cfg.ram_budget_bytes, 8 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024);
```

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../index.html)::[config](index.html)



# Struct ScraperConfig

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/config.rs.html#69-103" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct ScraperConfig {
    pub download_images: bool,
    pub download_documents: bool,
    pub output_dir: PathBuf,
    pub max_file_size: Option<u64>,
    pub download_timeout_secs: u64,
    pub scraper_concurrency: usize,
    pub download_concurrency: usize,
    pub max_pages: Option<usize>,
    pub selector: String,
    pub asset_h2_profile: Profile,
    pub asset_include_patterns: Vec<String>,
    pub asset_exclude_patterns: Vec<String>,
    pub asset_naming: AssetNamingStrategy,
    pub adaptive_selectors: bool,
    pub ignore_waf: bool,
}
```

Expand description



Scraper configuration for download and output behavior.

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::ScraperConfig;

// Default configuration
let config = ScraperConfig::default();

// Custom configuration with builder pattern
let config = ScraperConfig::default()
    .with_images()
    .with_documents()
    .with_output_dir("./output".into())
    .with_scraper_concurrency(5);

assert!(config.download_images);
assert!(config.download_documents);
assert_eq!(config.scraper_concurrency, 5);
```



## <a href="#concurrency-recommendations" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Concurrency Recommendations



| Storage | Concurrency | Reason                                     |
|---------|-------------|--------------------------------------------|
| HDD     | 3 (default) | Avoids disk thrashing on mechanical drives |
| SSD     | 5-8         | Faster random I/O                          |
| NVMe    | 10+         | Very high IOPS                             |

# Struct AggressiveProcessor

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/content_processing/aggressive.rs.html#20" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct AggressiveProcessor;
```

Expand description



Aggressive content processor for the download pipeline.

Removes all boilerplate (nav, header, footer, scripts, styles) via lol_html, then aggressively strips remaining HTML tags including complete block-level removal of script/style/noscript elements. Best for download pipelines where noise reduction is paramount.

# Struct McpProcessor

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/content_processing/mcp.rs.html#18" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct McpProcessor;
```

Expand description



MCP content processor for tools and API consumers.

Removes boilerplate (scripts, styles, nav, footer) via lol_html while preserving semantic HTML structure. Best for MCP tools that need structured HTML output with boilerplate stripped.

# Struct SemanticProcessor

``` rust
pub struct SemanticProcessor;
```

Expand description



Semantic content processor for the pipeline scraper.

Extracts readable content via Readability, then strips residual HTML tags and normalizes whitespace. Best for RAG and readability-focused pipelines.

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[converter](../index.html)::[html_cleaner](index.html)



# Function clean_html

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/converter/html_cleaner.rs.html#60-107" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn clean_html(html: &str) -> String
```

Expand description



Clean HTML by removing boilerplate (nav, sidebar, scripts, SVGs).

Removes:

- `script`, `style`, `noscript` (code and styles)
- `form`, `iframe`, `object`, `embed` (interactive)
- `svg`, `canvas`, `video`, `audio` (media)
- `nav`, `header`, `footer`, `aside` (page chrome)
- Elements matching CSS selectors (sidebars, search, breadcrumbs)
- Strips non-preserved attributes (keeps href, src, alt, id, class, dir, code)

Returns the cleaned HTML as a string.














[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[converter](../index.html)::[html_to_markdown](index.html)



# Function convert_to_markdown

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/converter/html_to_markdown.rs.html#26-41" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn convert_to_markdown(html: &str) -> String
```

Expand description



Convert HTML to well-structured Markdown.

Pipeline:

1.  Remove boilerplate (scripts, nav, sidebar, SVG, page chrome)
2.  Convert clean HTML → Markdown with ATX headings and fenced code blocks
3.  Fall back to plain text if conversion fails

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::infrastructure::converter::html_to_markdown::convert_to_markdown;

let html = "<h1>Title</h1><p>Content</p>";
let md = convert_to_markdown(html);
assert!(md.contains("# Title"));
```
















[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[converter](../index.html)::[obsidian](index.html)



# Function resolve_asset_paths

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/converter/obsidian.rs.html#30-63" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn resolve_asset_paths(
    content: &str,
    md_file_dir: &Path,
    assets: &[DownloadedAsset],
) -> String
```

Expand description



Rewrite Markdown image/document references to use relative paths.

Transforms `![](absolute/local/path)` -\> `![](../../relative/path)` based on the `.md` file’s location and the asset’s `local_path`.

Uses fuzzy matching to handle URL-encoded paths in Markdown references.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `content` — Markdown content with `![]()` references
- `md_file_dir` — Directory containing the output `.md` file
- `assets` — DownloadedAsset list with `local_path` and original `url`

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

Markdown with asset paths rewritten as relative














[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[converter](../index.html)::[syntax_highlight](index.html)



# Function highlight_code_blocks

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/converter/syntax_highlight.rs.html#55-76" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn highlight_code_blocks(markdown: &str) -> String
```

Expand description



Apply syntax highlighting to code blocks in Markdown

Finds all fenced code blocks (`lang ... `) and applies syntax highlighting using the base16-ocean.dark theme. Returns HTML-highlighted code blocks.

Uses `Regex::replace_all()` with closure for correct handling of:

- Multiple identical code blocks (no skip bugs)
- Single-pass processing (performance)
- No manual string mutation (correctness)

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::infrastructure::converter::syntax_highlight::highlight_code_blocks;

let md = "Text\n```rust\nfn main() {}\n```";
let highlighted = highlight_code_blocks(md);
assert!(highlighted.contains("<span"));
```



## <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns original Markdown if highlighting fails (fallback pattern).

# Function convert_wiki_links

``` rust
pub fn convert_wiki_links(content: &str, base_domain: &str) -> String
```

Expand description



Convert Markdown links to Obsidian wiki-links for same-domain URLs.

Transforms `[link text](https://same-domain.com/page)` -\> `[[page-slug|link text]]` External links (different domain) are left unchanged.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `content` — Markdown content to process
- `base_domain` — The domain of the scraped page (e.g. “example.com”)

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

Markdown with same-domain links converted to wiki-link syntax














[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[converter](../index.html)::[wikilinks](index.html)



# Function slug_from_url

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/converter/wikilinks.rs.html#40-69" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn slug_from_url(url_path: &str) -> String
```

Expand description



Extract a URL-safe slug from a URL path.

Strips query strings, fragments, trailing slashes, and file extensions. For paths with 2+ segments, combines the last 2 segments for better context (e.g., `/product/1` → `product-1` instead of just `1`). Uses `heck::ToKebabCase` for consistent kebab-case conversion.

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples

- “/” -\> “index”
- “/about” -\> “about”
- “/product/1” -\> “product-1”
- “/blog/my-post” -\> “blog-my-post”
- “/docs/api/v2” -\> “api-v2”
- “/docs/api/v2/endpoints” -\> “v2-endpoints”
- “/My%20Post%20Title” -\> “my-post-title” (URL-decoded)

# Struct RayonCpuPool

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/cpu_pool.rs.html#26-29" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct RayonCpuPool { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Dedicated, isolated Rayon thread pool for CPU-bound ingestion work.

Wraps a `rayon::ThreadPool` in an `Arc` so it can be cheaply cloned and shared across Tokio tasks (the bridge spawns a fresh blocking task per dispatch). Created via [`RayonCpuPool::new`](struct.RayonCpuPool.html#method.new "associated function webfang_core::infrastructure::cpu_pool::RayonCpuPool::new") or [`RayonCpuPool::from_config`](struct.RayonCpuPool.html#method.from_config "associated function webfang_core::infrastructure::cpu_pool::RayonCpuPool::from_config").

## <a href="#mono-core-behaviour" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Mono-core behaviour

When `cpu_cores == 1` the pool contains exactly one Rayon thread and the OS cooperatively time-slices between Tokio and Rayon (frozen user decision \#2). A thread count of `0` is floored to `1` rather than panicking.

#### pub fn <a href="#method.new" class="fn">new</a>(threads: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.usize.html" class="primitive">usize</a>) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<Self, <a href="../../error/enum.ScraperError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError">ScraperError</a>\>





Build a pool with `threads` worker threads.

The thread count is floored to at least `1` (frozen user decision \#2: mono-core cooperative scheduling) so `new(0)` yields a single-thread pool rather than panicking or erroring.

##### <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`ScraperError::Ingestion`](../../error/enum.ScraperError.html#variant.Ingestion "variant webfang_core::error::ScraperError::Ingestion") if Rayon fails to build the pool (e.g. the host refuses to spawn the requested threads).

#### pub fn <a href="#method.from_config" class="fn">from_config</a>(cfg: &<a href="../autotuning/struct.ElasticConfig.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::autotuning::ElasticConfig">ElasticConfig</a>) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<Self, <a href="../../error/enum.ScraperError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError">ScraperError</a>\>





Build a pool sized from a resolved [`ElasticConfig`](../autotuning/struct.ElasticConfig.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::autotuning::ElasticConfig")’s `cpu_cores` (frozen design: pool size = detected CPU cores, overridable via `--cpu-cores`).

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/cpu_pool.rs.html#73-78" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.install" class="fn">install</a>\<R\>(&self, f: impl <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html" class="trait" title="trait core::ops::function::FnOnce">FnOnce</a>() -\> R + <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Send.html" class="trait" title="trait core::marker::Send">Send</a>) -\> R



where R: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Send.html" class="trait" title="trait core::marker::Send">Send</a>,







Run `f` on the current thread with this pool installed as the active Rayon pool, so any nested `par_iter` / `rayon::spawn` routes to it (frozen design decision \#3).

The `Send` bounds mirror `rayon::ThreadPool::install`’s real signature (the design contract’s `impl FnOnce() -> R` is shorthand).

Apply crawl budget optimization to URL collection

Applies the 80/20 rule by:

1.  Prioritizing URLs with recent lastmod dates (if available in metadata)
2.  Filtering out parameter-heavy URLs that waste crawl budget
3.  Deduplicating similar URLs

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[crawler](../index.html)::[binary_utils](index.html)



# Function derive_filename_from_response

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/binary_utils.rs.html#78-129" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn derive_filename_from_response(
    headers: &HeaderMap,
    url: &Url,
    content_type: &str,
) -> String
```

Expand description



Derive a filename from Content-Disposition header or URL path.

Priority: Content-Disposition `filename` \> URL path basename \> fallback.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `headers` - HTTP response headers
- `url` - URL of the resource
- `content_type` - Content-Type header value

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

Derived filename

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::infrastructure::crawler::binary_utils::derive_filename_from_response;
use url::Url;

let headers = wreq::header::HeaderMap::new();
let url = Url::parse("https://example.com/docs/report.pdf").unwrap();
let result = derive_filename_from_response(&headers, &url, "application/pdf");
assert_eq!(result, "report.pdf");
```
















[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[crawler](../index.html)::[binary_utils](index.html)



# Function parse_content_disposition

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/binary_utils.rs.html#160-188" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn parse_content_disposition(value: &str) -> Option<String>
```

Expand description



Parse Content-Disposition header value to extract filename.

Supports:

- `filename="report.pdf"`
- `filename=report.pdf`
- `filename*=UTF-8''encoded-name.pdf`

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `value` - Content-Disposition header value

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

Parsed filename or None

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::infrastructure::crawler::binary_utils::parse_content_disposition;

assert_eq!(
    parse_content_disposition("attachment; filename=\"report.pdf\""),
    Some("report.pdf".to_string())
);
assert_eq!(
    parse_content_disposition("attachment; filename*=UTF-8''encoded.pdf"),
    Some("encoded.pdf".to_string())
);
```
















[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[crawler](../index.html)::[binary_utils](index.html)



# Function percent_decode

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/binary_utils.rs.html#34-51" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn percent_decode(input: &str) -> String
```

Expand description



Simple percent-decoding for filenames (handles common cases).

Decodes percent-encoded characters in filenames, e.g. `%20` → space.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `input` - String to decode

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

Decoded string

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::infrastructure::crawler::binary_utils::percent_decode;

assert_eq!(percent_decode("file%20name.pdf"), "file name.pdf");
assert_eq!(percent_decode("no-encoding"), "no-encoding");
```

# Struct FsBinaryWriter

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/binary_writer.rs.html#19" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct FsBinaryWriter;
```

Expand description



Filesystem-backed [`BinaryWriterPort`](../../../domain/ports/trait.BinaryWriterPort.html "trait webfang_core::domain::ports::BinaryWriterPort").

Creates the parent directory tree (if any) and writes the payload bytes synchronously. This is the default writer used when a scrape use case receives no injected writer (`None` fallback).

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[crawler](../index.html)::[http_client](index.html)



# Function create_rate_limited_client

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/http_client.rs.html#51-67" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn create_rate_limited_client(
    delay_ms: u64,
    tls_emulation: Profile,
) -> Result<Client>
```

Expand description



Create a rate-limited HTTP client

Delegates to the shared config-driven factory ([`create_http_client_with_config`](../../../application/http_client/fn.create_http_client_with_config.html "fn webfang_core::application::http_client::create_http_client_with_config"), the \#299 source of truth) so the crawl client carries the same Chrome Client Hints, pooled user-agent, pool tuning, compression, cookie store, and redirect policy as the scrape client — with the TLS/H2 fingerprint resolved from config instead of a hardcoded `Chrome145` (#312).

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `delay_ms` - Delay between requests in milliseconds
- `tls_emulation` - TLS/HTTP2 fingerprint preset applied to the client

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

Configured wreq Client

## <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns an error if the underlying wreq client fails to build.

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::infrastructure::crawler::create_rate_limited_client;
use wreq_util::Profile;

let client = create_rate_limited_client(500, Profile::Chrome145).unwrap();
```

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[crawler](../index.html)::[link_extractor](index.html)



# Function extract_links

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/link_extractor.rs.html#49-102" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn extract_links(
    html: &str,
    base_url: &str,
) -> Result<Vec<String>, CrawlError>
```

Expand description



Extract all crawlable links from HTML content

Following **own-borrow-over-clone**: Accepts `&str` not `&String`. Following **mem-with-capacity**: Pre-allocates Vec with estimated capacity.

Links marked `rel="nofollow"` (any token, case-insensitive) are excluded — the crawler must not follow them (#517). A `<base href>` element in the document overrides the caller’s `base_url` for resolving relative links, per the HTML spec (first `<base href>` wins; invalid or absent → fallback to `base_url`).

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `html` - HTML content to parse
- `base_url` - Base URL for resolving relative links (fallback when the document has no usable `<base href>`)

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

- `Ok(Vec<String>)` - List of extracted, normalized URLs
- `Err(CrawlError)` - Parse error

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::infrastructure::crawler::extract_links;

let html = r#"<html><body><a href="/page1">Link 1</a><a href="https://other.com/page2">Link 2</a></body></html>"#;
let links = extract_links(html, "https://example.com").unwrap();
assert!(links.contains(&"https://example.com/page1".to_string()));
assert!(links.contains(&"https://other.com/page2".to_string()));
```
















[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[crawler](../index.html)::[link_extractor](index.html)



# Function is_internal_link

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/link_extractor.rs.html#129-131" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn is_internal_link(url: &str, domain: &str) -> bool
```

Expand description



Check if a URL is internal (same domain)

Following **own-borrow-over-clone**: Accepts `&str` for both parameters. Following **opt-inline**: Inlined for hot path performance.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `url` - URL to check
- `domain` - Domain to check against

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

`true` if the URL belongs to the domain

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::infrastructure::crawler::is_internal_link;

assert!(is_internal_link("https://example.com/page", "example.com"));
assert!(is_internal_link("https://www.example.com/page", "example.com"));
assert!(!is_internal_link("https://other.com/page", "example.com"));
```

# Struct PermitGuard

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/resource_downloader.rs.html#21-24" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct PermitGuard { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



RAII guard for semaphore permits.

Ensures permits are released back to the semaphore even on panic, preventing permit starvation in the pool.

# Struct ResourceDownloader

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/resource_downloader.rs.html#103-107" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct ResourceDownloader { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Resource downloader with byte-weighted semaphore backpressure.

Implements elastic resource downloading with memory backpressure via a byte-weighted semaphore and Anti-Slowloris protection.



## Implementations<a href="#implementations" class="anchor">§</a>

#### pub async fn <a href="#method.download" class="fn">download</a>(&self, url: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.u8.html" class="primitive">u8</a>\>, <a href="../../../error/enum.ScraperError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError">ScraperError</a>\>





Downloads a resource with byte-weighted semaphore backpressure.

Permit lifecycle (spec: “Byte-Weighted Semaphore” + “Chunked Encoding Protection” + “Hard Resource Size Limit”):

- No permits are acquired until response headers arrive, so a `Content-Length` rejection never holds any permits.
- Each streamed chunk acquires its own byte-weighted permits *before* being buffered. Permits are `forget()`ten so the `PermitGuard` owns the release, guaranteeing `permits released == permits acquired` (no double-release, no permit inflation).

##### <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns `ScraperError` if:

- Global timeout exceeded (`GlobalTimeout`)
- Per-chunk timeout exceeded — Anti-Slowloris (`SlowlorisTimeout`)
- `Content-Length` or accumulated size exceeds the limit (`PayloadTooLarge`)
- Network error occurs (`Network`)
- Semaphore acquisition fails (`SemaphoreInanition`)

# Function parse_crawl_delay

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/robots_utils.rs.html#71-83" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn parse_crawl_delay(content: &str) -> Option<f64>
```

Expand description



Parse Crawl-delay from raw robots.txt content.

Searches for `Crawl-delay:` directives (case-insensitive) and returns the first valid numeric value found.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `content` - Raw robots.txt content

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

Parsed Crawl-delay in seconds, or None if not found

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::infrastructure::crawler::robots_utils::parse_crawl_delay;

assert_eq!(parse_crawl_delay("User-agent: *\nCrawl-delay: 5\n"), Some(5.0));
assert_eq!(parse_crawl_delay("User-agent: *\n"), None);
```
















[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[crawler](../index.html)::[robots_utils](index.html)



# Struct RobotsFetcher

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/robots_utils.rs.html#107-112" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct RobotsFetcher { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Fetches and caches robots.txt rules using a TLS-fingerprinted HTTP client.

The internal `wreq::Client` is built once with the caller’s TLS/HTTP2 emulation \[`Profile`\] and shared via `Arc` (#337). This keeps the robots.txt fingerprint consistent with the main page downloader instead of leaking the default fingerprint through a throwaway `wreq::get()` client.

Following **own-arc-shared**: the client is `Arc`-wrapped so the fetcher can be shared cheaply across spawned crawl tasks.



## Implementations<a href="#implementations" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/robots_utils.rs.html#114-281" class="src rightside">Source</a><a href="#impl-RobotsFetcher" class="anchor">§</a>

### impl <a href="struct.RobotsFetcher.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::crawler::robots_utils::RobotsFetcher">RobotsFetcher</a>







<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/robots_utils.rs.html#139-162" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.new" class="fn">new</a>(profile: Profile, timeout_secs: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.u64.html" class="primitive">u64</a>) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<Self, <a href="../../error/enum.InfraError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::infrastructure::error::InfraError">InfraError</a>\>





Create a new fetcher whose client uses the given TLS/HTTP2 `profile`.

The client is built once and shared via `Arc` for connection pooling. It mirrors the main downloader’s fingerprint and enables gzip/brotli plus a bounded redirect policy so the robots.txt fetch is indistinguishable from a regular page fetch (#337).

##### <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `profile` - TLS/HTTP2 fingerprint emulation preset applied to the client
- `timeout_secs` - Request timeout in seconds; the connect timeout is clamped to `min(timeout_secs, 10)`

##### <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`InfraError::Network`](../../error/enum.InfraError.html#variant.Network "variant webfang_core::infrastructure::error::InfraError::Network") if the wreq client cannot be built.

##### <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::infrastructure::crawler::robots_utils::RobotsFetcher;

let fetcher = RobotsFetcher::new(wreq_util::Profile::Chrome145, 30).unwrap();
```







<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/robots_utils.rs.html#256-264" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub async fn <a href="#method.is_allowed" class="fn">is_allowed</a>(&self, url: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>, domain: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>





Check if a URL is allowed by the site’s robots.txt.

Fetches robots.txt on first encounter (cached per domain). Uses the `robotstxt` crate’s `DefaultMatcher` for path matching. Fail-open: if robots.txt cannot be fetched, the URL is allowed.

##### <a href="#arguments-1" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `url` - The full URL to check
- `domain` - The domain key for cache lookup

##### <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

`true` if the URL is allowed by robots.txt (or if robots.txt is unavailable).

##### <a href="#examples-1" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::infrastructure::crawler::robots_utils::RobotsFetcher;

let fetcher = RobotsFetcher::new(wreq_util::Profile::Chrome145, 30).unwrap();
assert!(fetcher.is_allowed("https://example.com/page", "example.com").await);
```







<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/robots_utils.rs.html#278-280" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.get_crawl_delay" class="fn">get_crawl_delay</a>(&self, domain: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/option/enum.Option.html" class="enum" title="enum core::option::Option">Option</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.f64.html" class="primitive">f64</a>\>





Get the crawl-delay for a domain in seconds, if configured.

Returns `None` if the domain has not been fetched yet or no Crawl-delay directive was present in its robots.txt.

##### <a href="#arguments-2" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `domain` - Domain to get crawl-delay for

##### <a href="#returns-1" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

Crawl-delay in seconds, or None if not configured

Cache of robots.txt rules keyed by domain.

Using `DashMap` for lock-free concurrent reads during crawl. No TTL — robots.txt rarely changes during a single crawl session.

# Enum SitemapError

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/sitemap_parser.rs.html#47-95" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum SitemapError {
    InvalidUrl(ParseError),
    HttpError(String),
    XmlError(Error),
    IoError(Error),
    NoUrlsFound,
    InvalidStructure,
    MaxDepthExceeded,
    InvalidScheme(String),
    ResponseTooLarge(usize),
    DecompressedTooLarge(usize),
    SitemapNotFound(String),
    InvalidContentType(String),
}
```

Expand description



Sitemap parser errors

Following err-thiserror-for-libraries: typed, matchable errors

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[crawler](../index.html)::[sitemap_parser](index.html)



# Function parse_sitemap

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/sitemap_parser.rs.html#515-573" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn parse_sitemap(
    xml_content: &str,
    base_url: &Url,
) -> Result<Vec<String>, CrawlError>
```

Expand description



Parse sitemap XML content using quick-xml (streaming parser)

Standalone streaming parser for sitemap `<loc>` entries, extracted from the application layer (issue \#442): XML parsing is an infrastructure concern and lives here alongside [`SitemapParser`](struct.SitemapParser.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::crawler::sitemap_parser::SitemapParser"). Relative URLs are resolved against `base_url`.

Following **xml-no-regex**: Uses quick-xml instead of regex for XML parsing. Following **mem-stream-processing**: Streaming approach avoids loading entire DOM.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `xml_content` - XML content of the sitemap
- `base_url` - Base URL to resolve relative `<loc>` entries against

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

- `Ok(Vec<String>)` - List of URLs
- `Err(CrawlError)` - Parse error














[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[crawler](../index.html)::[sitemap_parser](index.html)



# Function resolve_url

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/sitemap_parser.rs.html#129-142" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn resolve_url(base: &Url, input: &str) -> Option<Url>
```

Expand description



Safely resolve a potentially-relative URL against a base URL.

Handles all RFC 3986 reference types: absolute, scheme-relative, absolute-path, relative-path. Returns `None` for empty inputs.

Following **err-result-over-panic**: returns Option, never panics. Following **perf-iter-over-index**: uses early returns, no loops.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `base` - The base URL for resolution context
- `input` - The URL or path to resolve

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

- `Some(Url)` - Successfully resolved URL
- `None` - Empty input or resolution failure

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use url::Url;
use webfang_core::infrastructure::crawler::sitemap_parser::resolve_url;

let base = Url::parse("https://example.com/sitemap.xml").unwrap();
let resolved = resolve_url(&base, "/page.html").unwrap();
assert_eq!(resolved.as_str(), "https://example.com/page.html");
```

Create new parser with custom config and an explicit TLS/H2 profile.

The sitemap fetch client is built once here (via the shared `create_http_client_with_config` factory) from `tls_emulation` and reused across every fetch and retry, honoring the caller’s `--h2-profile` selection instead of a hardcoded preset (#323).

# Struct PrioritizedUrl

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/url_queue.rs.html#41-46" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct PrioritizedUrl {
    pub url: DiscoveredUrl,
    pub priority: u32,
}
```

Expand description



A URL with priority for the priority queue.

Implements `Ord` so that `BinaryHeap` yields highest-priority URLs first.



## Fields<a href="#fields" class="anchor">§</a>

<a href="#structfield.url" class="anchor field">§</a>`url: `<a href="../../../domain/crawl_job/struct.DiscoveredUrl.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::domain::crawl_job::DiscoveredUrl"><code>DiscoveredUrl</code></a>

Priority score (higher = more important)

#### pub fn <a href="#method.new" class="fn">new</a>(url: <a href="../../../domain/crawl_job/struct.DiscoveredUrl.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::domain::crawl_job::DiscoveredUrl">DiscoveredUrl</a>, priority: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.u32.html" class="primitive">u32</a>) -\> Self





Create a new prioritized URL with explicit priority





<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/url_queue.rs.html#64-73" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.from_source" class="fn">from_source</a>(url: <a href="../../../domain/crawl_job/struct.DiscoveredUrl.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::domain::crawl_job::DiscoveredUrl">DiscoveredUrl</a>, source: <a href="enum.UrlSource.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::infrastructure::crawler::url_queue::UrlSource">UrlSource</a>) -\> Self





Create a prioritized URL from a source type and depth.

Priority scoring rules:

- Seed URL: 1000
- Sitemap URL: 500
- Link URL: 200
- Depth penalty: priority -= depth \* 10
- Minimum priority: 1

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[crawler](../index.html)::[url_queue](index.html)



# Struct UrlQueue

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/url_queue.rs.html#104-113" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct UrlQueue { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Thread-safe URL queue with deduplication and priority scheduling

Following **async-no-lock-across-await**: uses `tokio::sync::Mutex` with `.lock().await` for the pending-URL buffer (held across no `.await`), and a lock-free `DashSet<u64, ahash::RandomState>` for the seen set. Following **mem-with-capacity**: pre-allocates internal storage. Following **coll-binaryheap**: uses `BinaryHeap` for priority queue semantics.

Create a new URL queue

Following **mem-with-capacity**: pre-allocates internal structures and a per-process randomized hash seed (FR-3 HashDoS resistance).





<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/url_queue.rs.html#149-172" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub async fn <a href="#method.push_prioritized" class="fn">push_prioritized</a>( &self, url: <a href="../../../domain/crawl_job/struct.DiscoveredUrl.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::domain::crawl_job::DiscoveredUrl">DiscoveredUrl</a>, source: <a href="enum.UrlSource.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::infrastructure::crawler::url_queue::UrlSource">UrlSource</a>, ) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>





Push a URL to the queue with a specific source type.

The source determines the base priority:

- `UrlSource::Seed`: priority 1000
- `UrlSource::Sitemap`: priority 500
- `UrlSource::Link`: priority 200

Depth penalty is applied automatically from `url.depth`.

Returns `false` if the URL was already seen (duplicate).

##### <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `url` - URL to add
- `source` - Source type for priority scoring

##### <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

`true` if added, `false` if duplicate





<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/url_queue.rs.html#185-187" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub async fn <a href="#method.drain_all" class="fn">drain_all</a>(&self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/collections/vec_deque/struct.VecDeque.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::collections::vec_deque::VecDeque">VecDeque</a>\<<a href="../../../domain/crawl_job/struct.DiscoveredUrl.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::domain::crawl_job::DiscoveredUrl">DiscoveredUrl</a>\>





Drain all pending URLs from the internal queue into a VecDeque.

Used to transfer discovered links from the deduplicated `UrlQueue` to the main crawl loop’s `VecDeque` work queue.

URLs are drained in priority order (highest first) from the BinaryHeap.

##### <a href="#returns-3" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

VecDeque of all pending URLs (queue is emptied)





<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/url_queue.rs.html#231-234" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub async fn <a href="#method.snapshot_urls" class="fn">snapshot_urls</a>(&self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>\>





Snapshot pending URLs as strings WITHOUT consuming them.

Used by checkpoint persistence (#517): the queue must be serializable at any point so a resume can re-enqueue what was pending when the crawl stopped. The `seen` set is untouched, so re-pushing these URLs later would be rejected as duplicates — callers restoring a checkpoint must bypass the dedup set for exactly the restored URLs.

##### <a href="#returns-4" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

All URLs currently in the queue (heap order, not priority order).

# Struct UrlValidator

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/crawler/url_validator.rs.html#36-40" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct UrlValidator { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Handles URL validation and filtering

HTTP-aware implementation of `UrlValidatorTrait`. Delegates pattern filtering to the domain’s `StaticUrlValidator` and adds HTTP status validation.



## Implementations<a href="#implementations" class="anchor">§</a>

The client is built via the shared `create_http_client_with_config` factory (#299), honoring the caller’s `--h2-profile` selection instead of a hardcoded preset (#324).

# Struct ChromiumoxideDownloader

``` rust
pub struct ChromiumoxideDownloader { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



CDP downloader that spawns a headless Chrome instance per fetch.

Note: Resource gating is handled by [`super::hybrid_router::HybridRouter`](../hybrid_router/struct.HybridRouter.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::hybrid_router::HybridRouter"). This downloader does NOT own a `ResourceGovernor` — the router checks resources before invoking this layer.

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[downloader](../index.html)::[cookie_bridge](index.html)



# Struct CookieBridge

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/cookie_bridge.rs.html#18-20" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct CookieBridge { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Extracts and stores cookies from fetched pages.

After each fetch, call [`CookieBridge::ingest`](struct.CookieBridge.html#method.ingest "method webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::cookie_bridge::CookieBridge::ingest") to capture Set-Cookie cookies. The accumulated cookie jar can then be injected into CDP via [`CookieBridge::to_cdp_cookies`](struct.CookieBridge.html#method.to_cdp_cookies "method webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::cookie_bridge::CookieBridge::to_cdp_cookies") (future).
