# Enum DownloadError

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/mod.rs.html#115-158" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
#[non_exhaustive]pub enum DownloadError {
    Network(Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>),
    Http {
        status: u16,
        message: String,
    },
    WafChallenge(String),
    SpaDetected(String),
    InvalidUrl(String),
    Timeout(u64),
    Internal(String),
    ResourceExhausted(String),
    Cancelled,
}
```

Expand description



Errors that can occur during page download.

Following **api-non-exhaustive**: can add variants without breaking changes. Following **err-thiserror-lib**: uses thiserror for structured error messages.



## Variants (Non-exhaustive)<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>

This enum is marked as non-exhaustive



Non-exhaustive enums could have additional variants added in future. Therefore, when matching against variants of non-exhaustive enums, an extra wildcard arm must be added to account for any future variants.







<a href="#variant.Network" class="anchor">§</a>

### Network(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::boxed::Box">Box</a>\<dyn <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/error/trait.Error.html" class="trait" title="trait core::error::Error">Error</a> + <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Send.html" class="trait" title="trait core::marker::Send">Send</a> + <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/marker/trait.Sync.html" class="trait" title="trait core::marker::Sync">Sync</a>\>)





Network-level failure (DNS, connection, timeout).

Carries the underlying error as `#[source]` (erased) so the root-cause chain survives into `CrawlError`/`ScraperError` (D4).





<a href="#variant.Http" class="anchor">§</a>

### Http





HTTP error response (non-2xx status).





#### Fields



<a href="#variant.Http.field.status" class="anchor field">§</a>`status: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.u16.html" class="primitive"><code>u16</code></a>





<a href="#variant.Http.field.message" class="anchor field">§</a>`message: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>







<a href="#variant.WafChallenge" class="anchor">§</a>

### WafChallenge(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>)





WAF challenge detected (Cloudflare, reCAPTCHA, etc.).





<a href="#variant.SpaDetected" class="anchor">§</a>

### SpaDetected(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>)





SPA detected — page requires JavaScript rendering.





<a href="#variant.InvalidUrl" class="anchor">§</a>

### InvalidUrl(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>)





URL is invalid or has an unsupported scheme.





<a href="#variant.Timeout" class="anchor">§</a>

### Timeout(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.u64.html" class="primitive">u64</a>)





Request timed out.





<a href="#variant.Internal" class="anchor">§</a>

### Internal(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>)





Internal error (should not happen in normal operation).





<a href="#variant.ResourceExhausted" class="anchor">§</a>

### ResourceExhausted(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>)





System resources (RAM) insufficient to spawn a heavyweight downloader layer. An *expected* operational condition under memory pressure — distinct from [`Internal`](enum.DownloadError.html#variant.Internal "variant webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::DownloadError::Internal"), which means a bug.





<a href="#variant.Cancelled" class="anchor">§</a>

### Cancelled





Acquisition cancelled by the engine’s cancellation token (#509) — the caller was waiting for a resource permit when shutdown fired.

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[downloader](../index.html)::[hybrid_router](index.html)



# Struct HybridRouter

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/hybrid_router.rs.html#31-41" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct HybridRouter<L1: Downloader, L2: Downloader, L3: Downloader> { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Three-layer hybrid downloader.

Type parameters correspond to the three fetch layers:

- `L1`: static HTTP (typically [`WreqDownloader`](../wreq_downloader/struct.WreqDownloader.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::wreq_downloader::WreqDownloader"))
- `L2`: subprocess fallback (typically [`ObscuraDownloader`](../obscura_downloader/struct.ObscuraDownloader.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::obscura_downloader::ObscuraDownloader"))
- `L3`: headless browser (typically [`ChromiumoxideDownloader`](../chromiumoxide_downloader/struct.ChromiumoxideDownloader.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::chromiumoxide_downloader::ChromiumoxideDownloader"))

Expand description



Subprocess-based downloader that shells out to `obscura fetch --dump markdown`.

No cookies, no connection pool — each invocation is independent.

``` rust
pub enum ResourceError {
    RamTooHigh(u8),
    Insufficient(String),
}
```

Errors raised when system resources cannot support a new instance.

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[downloader](../index.html)::[resource_governor](index.html)



# Struct ResourceGovernor

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/resource_governor.rs.html#50-53" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct ResourceGovernor { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Gates concurrent heavyweight downloader instances based on system RAM.

Holds a \[`CancellationToken`\] (#509) so a caller blocked in [`acquire`](struct.ResourceGovernor.html#method.acquire "method webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::resource_governor::ResourceGovernor::acquire") can be woken on engine shutdown instead of hanging on the semaphore forever. [`new`](struct.ResourceGovernor.html#method.new "associated function webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::resource_governor::ResourceGovernor::new") uses a fresh token that never fires (pre-#509 behavior); the crawl engine injects its own token via [`with_cancel_token`](struct.ResourceGovernor.html#method.with_cancel_token "associated function webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::resource_governor::ResourceGovernor::with_cancel_token").



## Implementations<a href="#implementations" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/resource_governor.rs.html#55-171" class="src rightside">Source</a><a href="#impl-ResourceGovernor" class="anchor">§</a>

### impl <a href="struct.ResourceGovernor.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::resource_governor::ResourceGovernor">ResourceGovernor</a>







<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/resource_governor.rs.html#60-62" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.new" class="fn">new</a>() -\> Self





Create a governor calibrated to current system RAM.

The embedded cancellation token never fires; use [`with_cancel_token`](struct.ResourceGovernor.html#method.with_cancel_token "associated function webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::resource_governor::ResourceGovernor::with_cancel_token") to wire shutdown.





<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/resource_governor.rs.html#66-68" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.with_cancel_token" class="fn">with_cancel_token</a>(cancel: CancellationToken) -\> Self





Create a governor calibrated to current system RAM whose [`acquire`](struct.ResourceGovernor.html#method.acquire "method webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::resource_governor::ResourceGovernor::acquire") aborts when `cancel` fires (#509).





<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/resource_governor.rs.html#76-84" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.with_max_instances" class="fn">with_max_instances</a>(max_permits: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.usize.html" class="primitive">usize</a>, cancel: CancellationToken) -\> Self





Create a governor with an explicit permit budget.

Calibration seam behind [`new`](struct.ResourceGovernor.html#method.new "associated function webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::resource_governor::ResourceGovernor::new") / [`with_cancel_token`](struct.ResourceGovernor.html#method.with_cancel_token "associated function webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::resource_governor::ResourceGovernor::with_cancel_token"): lets constrained environments (containers) and tests set the budget directly instead of deriving it from system RAM.





<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/resource_governor.rs.html#91-110" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.check_resources" class="fn">check_resources</a>(&self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.usize.html" class="primitive">usize</a>, <a href="enum.ResourceError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::resource_governor::ResourceError">ResourceError</a>\>





Check whether resources are available and return a permit count, or an error if the system is under too much memory pressure.

The returned `usize` represents how many permits *could* be acquired right now (0 when denied).





<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/resource_governor.rs.html#126-138" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub async fn <a href="#method.acquire" class="fn">acquire</a>(&self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<OwnedSemaphorePermit, <a href="../enum.DownloadError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::DownloadError">DownloadError</a>\>





Acquire an owned semaphore permit, returning an error when resources are exhausted.

Returns a \[`tokio::sync::OwnedSemaphorePermit`\] (`'static`) so callers can hold it across async boundaries without tying it to the governor’s lifetime.

The wait aborts with [`DownloadError::Cancelled`](../enum.DownloadError.html#variant.Cancelled "variant webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::DownloadError::Cancelled") if the governor’s cancellation token fires while blocked (#509). Dropping the pending acquire consumes no permit, so a cancelled wait cannot leak one.

##### <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`DownloadError::Cancelled`](../enum.DownloadError.html#variant.Cancelled "variant webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::DownloadError::Cancelled") on cancellation and [`DownloadError::Internal`](../enum.DownloadError.html#variant.Internal "variant webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::DownloadError::Internal") if the semaphore was closed.

# Enum SpaReason

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/spa_detector.rs.html#26-32" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum SpaReason {
    MountPoint(String),
    InsufficientContent(usize),
}
```

Expand description



Why a page was detected as an SPA.



## Variants<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>

### MountPoint(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>)





Known SPA mount point found (e.g., `#root`, `#app`, `__NEXT_DATA__`, `__NUXT__`).





<a href="#variant.InsufficientContent" class="anchor">§</a>

### InsufficientContent(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.usize.html" class="primitive">usize</a>)





Page body is too short to contain meaningful static content. The `usize` is the content length in bytes.

# Enum SpaSignal

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/spa_detector.rs.html#15-22" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum SpaSignal {
    StaticContent,
    SpaDetected(SpaReason),
    WafBlocked,
}
```

Expand description



Signal indicating whether a page is static, an SPA, or WAF-blocked.



## Variants<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="#variant.StaticContent" class="anchor">§</a>

### StaticContent





Page has sufficient static HTML content — no JS rendering needed.





<a href="#variant.SpaDetected" class="anchor">§</a>

### SpaDetected(<a href="enum.SpaReason.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::spa_detector::SpaReason">SpaReason</a>)





Page is detected as an SPA with the given reason.





<a href="#variant.WafBlocked" class="anchor">§</a>

### WafBlocked





Page is a WAF challenge (Cloudflare, reCAPTCHA, etc.) — not a real SPA.

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[downloader](../index.html)::[spa_detector](index.html)



# Function detect_spa

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/spa_detector.rs.html#86-115" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn detect_spa(html: &str, ignore_waf: bool) -> SpaSignal
```

Expand description



Detect whether an HTML page is static content, an SPA, or a WAF challenge.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `html` - Raw HTML content of the page
- `ignore_waf` - Bypass WAF classification (REQ-WAF-07). When `true`, the inspection yields a clean verdict and the page is classified by normal spa/static logic instead of [`SpaSignal::WafBlocked`](enum.SpaSignal.html#variant.WafBlocked "variant webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::spa_detector::SpaSignal::WafBlocked").

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

A [`SpaSignal`](enum.SpaSignal.html "enum webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::spa_detector::SpaSignal") indicating the detection result.

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::spa_detector::{detect_spa, SpaSignal};

let html = "<html><body><article><h1>Hello</h1></article></body></html>";
assert_eq!(detect_spa(html, false), SpaSignal::StaticContent);

let spa = "<html><body></body></html>";
assert!(matches!(detect_spa(spa, false), SpaSignal::SpaDetected(_)));
```

Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left` is `true`. Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right "variant either::Either::Right") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") otherwise. where F: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html" class="trait" title="trait core::ops::function::FnOnce">FnOnce</a>(&Self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>,







Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left(&self)` returns `true`. Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right "variant either::Either::Right") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") otherwise. [Read more](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/into_either/trait.IntoEither.html#method.into_either_with)

# Trait Downloader

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/mod.rs.html#47-71" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait Downloader: Send + Sync {
    // Required methods
    fn fetch<'a>(
        &'a self,
        url: &'a Url,
    ) -> BoxFuture<'a, Result<FetchedPage, DownloadError>>;
    fn supports_interactions(&self) -> bool;
    fn memory_cost(&self) -> usize;
}
```

Expand description



Downloader trait for fetching pages.

Implementations must be safe to share across threads (`Send + Sync`). Each implementation owns its connection pool and request configuration.

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



<a href="#" class="tooltip" title="This example is not tested">ⓘ</a>

``` rust
use webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::wreq_downloader::WreqDownloader;
use webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::Downloader;

let downloader = WreqDownloader::new(30, 10, wreq_util::Profile::Chrome145, None).unwrap();
let page = downloader.fetch(&"https://example.com".parse().unwrap()).await.unwrap();
assert!(!page.html.is_empty());
```





## Required Methods<a href="#required-methods" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/mod.rs.html#59" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### fn <a href="#tymethod.fetch" class="fn">fetch</a>\<'a\>( &'a self, url: &'a <a href="https://docs.rs/url/2.5.7/url/struct.Url.html" class="struct" title="struct url::Url">Url</a>, ) -\> BoxFuture\<'a, <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="struct.FetchedPage.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::FetchedPage">FetchedPage</a>, <a href="enum.DownloadError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::DownloadError">DownloadError</a>\>\>





Fetch a page from the given URL.

Returns the fetched page with HTML content, HTTP status, headers, and cookies.

Desugared to \[`BoxFuture`\] (instead of native `async fn`) so the trait is dyn-compatible — `&dyn Downloader` can be passed for runtime dispatch and test mocking. Matches the `VectorRepository` precedent.

##### <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`DownloadError`](enum.DownloadError.html "enum webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::DownloadError") on network failure, timeout, or WAF detection.





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/mod.rs.html#65" class="src rightside">Source</a>

Whether this downloader supports JavaScript rendering / interactions.

Static HTTP downloaders return `false`. Headless browser implementations return `true`.





<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/mod.rs.html#70" class="src rightside">Source</a>

Estimated memory cost of this downloader instance in bytes.

Used by the scheduler to budget total memory across concurrent downloaders.

# Struct WreqDownloader

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/wreq_downloader.rs.html#42-51" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct WreqDownloader { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Downloader implementation backed by `wreq` with connection pooling.

The internal `wreq::Client` is shared via `Arc` — all requests reuse the same connection pool, avoiding the per-request client creation anti-pattern.

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



<a href="#" class="tooltip" title="This example is not tested">ⓘ</a>

``` rust
use webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::wreq_downloader::WreqDownloader;
use webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::Downloader;

let downloader = WreqDownloader::new(30, 10, wreq_util::Profile::Chrome145, None).unwrap();
let page = downloader.fetch(&"https://example.com".parse().unwrap()).await.unwrap();
assert_eq!(page.status, 200);
```

#### pub fn <a href="#method.new" class="fn">new</a>( timeout_secs: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.u64.html" class="primitive">u64</a>, connect_timeout_secs: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.u64.html" class="primitive">u64</a>, tls_emulation: Profile, user_agent: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/option/enum.Option.html" class="enum" title="enum core::option::Option">Option</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>\>, ) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<Self, <a href="../enum.DownloadError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::DownloadError">DownloadError</a>\>





Create a new WreqDownloader with the given TLS/HTTP2 emulation profile.

The client is built once and shared via `Arc` for connection pooling. Pass \[`Profile::Chrome145`\] for the historical default fingerprint.

##### <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `timeout_secs` - Request timeout in seconds
- `connect_timeout_secs` - Connection timeout in seconds
- `tls_emulation` - TLS/HTTP2 fingerprint profile applied to the client
- `user_agent` - Optional pinned User-Agent (#503). Applied at client build time via the builder’s `user_agent` API, AFTER the emulation profile, so it wins over the profile-default UA on the wire. When set, the 403 pool-rotation retry is disabled.

##### <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`DownloadError::Internal`](../enum.DownloadError.html#variant.Internal "variant webfang_core::infrastructure::downloader::DownloadError::Internal") if the wreq client cannot be built.





<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/downloader/wreq_downloader.rs.html#119-125" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.from_client" class="fn">from_client</a>( client: Client, timeout_secs: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.u64.html" class="primitive">u64</a>, \_connect_timeout_secs: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.u64.html" class="primitive">u64</a>, ) -\> Self





Create a WreqDownloader from an existing `wreq::Client`.

Useful when you need custom client configuration beyond the defaults.

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../index.html)::[error](index.html)



# Enum InfraError

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/error.rs.html#12-78" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum InfraError {
Http {
        status: u16,
        url: String,
    },
    Network(Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>),
    Middleware(String),
    WafBlocked {
        url: String,
        provider: String,
    },
    Download(Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>),
    GlobalTimeout,
    SlowlorisTimeout,
    PayloadTooLarge,
    SemaphoreInanition,
    Persistence(String),
    Ingestion(String),
    H2Config(String),
    UrlParse(ParseError),
    Io(Error),
}
```

Expand description



Infrastructure-level errors representing external system failures.

These errors represent failures in infrastructure components (HTTP, persistence, ingestion) that are independent of business logic.



## Variants<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>

``` rust
pub struct FileExporter { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



File-based exporter implementing the Exporter trait

This is the infrastructure adapter that bridges the domain’s Exporter trait with the local file system. It replaces the legacy functions in file_saver.rs.

``` rust
pub struct JsonlExporter { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



JSONL Exporter - writes one JSON object per line

Optimized for:

- Streaming writes (no in-memory buffering of entire dataset)
- Large datasets (appends to existing files)
- Integration with RAG pipelines (jq, pandas compatible)

``` rust
pub struct StateStore { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



StateStore manages persistence of export state for a specific domain

Following **proj-mod-by-feature**: Export state management is a feature Following **own-borrow-over-clone**: Accepts &str for domain

# Function cosine_similarity

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/export/vector_exporter.rs.html#56-73" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn cosine_similarity(a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> Result<f32, ExporterError>
```

Expand description



Computes cosine similarity between two vectors

Returns a value between -1.0 and 1.0, where:

- 1.0 means identical direction
- 0.0 means orthogonal
- -1.0 means opposite direction

Returns 0.0 for zero-magnitude vectors.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `a` - First vector
- `b` - Second vector

## <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns `DimensionMismatch` if vectors have different dimensions

Expand description



VectorExporter for RAG pipeline

Exports documents to JSON format with:

- Metadata header (format version, dimensions, document count)
- Documents array with optional embeddings
- Support for append mode

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[http](../index.html)::[waf_engine](index.html)



# Enum EvidenceSource

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/http/waf_engine.rs.html#74-79" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum EvidenceSource {
    Body,
    Header,
}
```

Expand description



Where a piece of WAF evidence was observed (FIX B).

Drives the 5xx body-vs-header carve-out in the verdict policy: on a 5xx response a bare vendor mention sourced from the BODY ([`EvidenceSource::Body`](enum.EvidenceSource.html#variant.Body "variant webfang_core::infrastructure::http::waf_engine::EvidenceSource::Body")) is ubiquitous diagnostic noise and does not block, whereas the same Fingerprint tier sourced from a control HEADER ([`EvidenceSource::Header`](enum.EvidenceSource.html#variant.Header "variant webfang_core::infrastructure::http::waf_engine::EvidenceSource::Header"), e.g. `cf-mitigated`) signals active mitigation and still blocks. Internal to the verdict — it is deliberately NOT part of the Spanish evidence chain.



## Variants<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="#variant.Body" class="anchor">§</a>

### Body





Evidence matched in the response body (signatures or entropy).





<a href="#variant.Header" class="anchor">§</a>

### Header





Evidence matched in a response control header.

# Enum WafTier

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/http/waf_engine.rs.html#47-52" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum WafTier {
    Challenge,
    Fingerprint,
}
```

Expand description



WAF signature tier — determines the blocking policy for a matched pattern.

Tier drives the verdict policy in [`WafInspector::inspect`](struct.WafInspector.html#method.inspect "associated function webfang_core::infrastructure::http::waf_engine::WafInspector::inspect"):

- [`WafTier::Challenge`](enum.WafTier.html#variant.Challenge "variant webfang_core::infrastructure::http::waf_engine::WafTier::Challenge") blocks at ANY HTTP status, including 200.
- [`WafTier::Fingerprint`](enum.WafTier.html#variant.Fingerprint "variant webfang_core::infrastructure::http::waf_engine::WafTier::Fingerprint") is evidence only; it blocks solely when correlated with a WAF-associated status code (403 / 429 / 503 / 520–529).



## Variants<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="#variant.Challenge" class="anchor">§</a>

### Challenge





Unambiguous challenge/captcha markers (widget tokens, challenge prose).





<a href="#variant.Fingerprint" class="anchor">§</a>

### Fingerprint





Fingerprint markers (bare vendor names, domains, cookies, control headers).

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[http](../index.html)::[waf_engine](index.html)



# Struct InspectionContext

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/http/waf_engine.rs.html#136-145" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct InspectionContext {
    pub status: Option<u16>,
    pub content_type: Option<String>,
    pub headers: HeaderMap,
    pub ignore_waf: bool,
}
```

Expand description



HTTP context for a WAF inspection (REQ-WAF-01).

[`Default`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/default/trait.Default.html "trait core::default::Default") is *degraded mode* — no HTTP context (status/content-type unknown, empty headers, `ignore_waf` false). Callers that only have the body (e.g. the MCP `detect_waf` tool) use degraded mode, where only [`WafTier::Challenge`](enum.WafTier.html#variant.Challenge "variant webfang_core::infrastructure::http::waf_engine::WafTier::Challenge") markers block and [`WafTier::Fingerprint`](enum.WafTier.html#variant.Fingerprint "variant webfang_core::infrastructure::http::waf_engine::WafTier::Fingerprint") evidence is reported as low-confidence and never blocks (REQ-WAF-05).



## Fields<a href="#fields" class="anchor">§</a>

## Implementations<a href="#implementations" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/http/waf_engine.rs.html#147-181" class="src rightside">Source</a><a href="#impl-InspectionContext" class="anchor">§</a>

### impl <a href="struct.InspectionContext.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::http::waf_engine::InspectionContext">InspectionContext</a>







<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/http/waf_engine.rs.html#159-180" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.from_lowercase_headers" class="fn">from_lowercase_headers</a>( status: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.u16.html" class="primitive">u16</a>, headers: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/collections/hash/map/struct.HashMap.html" class="struct" title="struct std::collections::hash::map::HashMap">HashMap</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>, <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>\>, ignore_waf: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>, ) -\> Self





Build a full context from an HTTP status and a lowercased-key header map, as captured by the domain `HttpResponse` and infrastructure `FetchedPage` types (REQ-WAF-01).

The `content-type` entry is lifted into [`Self::content_type`](struct.InspectionContext.html#structfield.content_type "field webfang_core::infrastructure::http::waf_engine::InspectionContext::content_type") for the REQ-WAF-02 gate, and the whole map is converted into a wreq \[`HeaderMap`\] for control-header evidence (REQ-WAF-03). Invalid header names/values are skipped — they cannot occur for headers already validated by the downloaders, but the guard keeps this infallible. `ignore_waf` short-circuits inspection to a clean verdict (REQ-WAF-07).

# Struct WafEvidence

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/http/waf_engine.rs.html#86-97" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct WafEvidence {
    pub provider: &'static str,
    pub tier: WafTier,
    pub matched_pattern: &'static str,
    pub source: EvidenceSource,
}
```

Expand description



A single piece of WAF detection evidence collected during inspection.

A verdict carries *all* collected evidences (REQ-WAF-01), enabling an evidence-chain error message (REQ-WAF-08) instead of a first-hit provider.



## Fields<a href="#fields" class="anchor">§</a>

<a href="#structfield.provider" class="anchor field">§</a>`provider: &'static `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive"><code>str</code></a>



Detected WAF provider (e.g. `"Cloudflare"`, `"DataDome"`).



<a href="#structfield.tier" class="anchor field">§</a>`tier: `<a href="enum.WafTier.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::infrastructure::http::waf_engine::WafTier"><code>WafTier</code></a>



Signature tier that matched.



<a href="#structfield.matched_pattern" class="anchor field">§</a>`matched_pattern: &'static `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive"><code>str</code></a>



The literal pattern (or rule label) that matched.



<a href="#structfield.source" class="anchor field">§</a>`source: `<a href="enum.EvidenceSource.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::infrastructure::http::waf_engine::EvidenceSource"><code>EvidenceSource</code></a>



Where the evidence was observed (body or header) — drives the 5xx body-vs-header carve-out in the verdict policy; not surfaced in the Spanish evidence chain.

## Implementations<a href="#implementations" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/http/waf_engine.rs.html#605-690" class="src rightside">Source</a><a href="#impl-WafInspector" class="anchor">§</a>

### impl <a href="struct.WafInspector.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::http::waf_engine::WafInspector">WafInspector</a>







<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/http/waf_engine.rs.html#623-671" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.inspect" class="fn">inspect</a>(body: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>, ctx: &<a href="struct.InspectionContext.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::http::waf_engine::InspectionContext">InspectionContext</a>) -\> <a href="struct.WafVerdict.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_core::infrastructure::http::waf_engine::WafVerdict">WafVerdict</a>





Inspect a response body with full HTTP context and return a verdict.

This is the single entry point for context-aware, evidence-based WAF detection (REQ-WAF-01). It collects ALL evidence — boundary-filtered body signatures (REQ-WAF-03/04), control headers (REQ-WAF-03), and entropy signals (REQ-WAF-06) — then applies the verdict policy (REQ-WAF-05):

- [`WafTier::Challenge`](enum.WafTier.html#variant.Challenge "variant webfang_core::infrastructure::http::waf_engine::WafTier::Challenge") (T1) blocks at ANY status, including 200.
- [`WafTier::Fingerprint`](enum.WafTier.html#variant.Fingerprint "variant webfang_core::infrastructure::http::waf_engine::WafTier::Fingerprint") (T2) blocks only with a correlated WAF status (403 / 429 / 503 / 520–529); in degraded mode (no status) T2 is reported low-confidence and never blocks.

`ctx.ignore_waf` yields a clean verdict immediately (REQ-WAF-02 step 1), and the content-type denylist (REQ-WAF-02) gates body scanning.

Thread-safe: the AC automaton is immutable once compiled via `Lazy`.

#### pub fn <a href="#method.clean" class="fn">clean</a>() -\> Self





A clean verdict: not blocked, no evidence.





<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/http/waf_engine.rs.html#123-125" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.evidence_chain" class="fn">evidence_chain</a>(&self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>





Spanish user-facing evidence chain for the block error (REQ-WAF-08).

Each evidence renders as `provider (patrón: <pattern>, tier: <label_es>)`, joined by `; `. Falls back to a generic label when the verdict carries no evidence. Callers that raise a block error (HTTP client, scraper service, crawler discovery, MCP) pass this string as the `provider` payload so the full chain reaches the user instead of a bare first-hit provider name.

# Enum SessionStatus

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/network/session_pool.rs.html#25-32" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum SessionStatus {
    Healthy,
    Banned,
    Retiring,
}
```

Expand description



Health status of a session for a given domain.



## Variants<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="#variant.Healthy" class="anchor">§</a>

### Healthy





Session is healthy and available for requests.





<a href="#variant.Banned" class="anchor">§</a>

### Banned





Session is temporarily banned due to consecutive failures.





<a href="#variant.Retiring" class="anchor">§</a>

### Retiring





Session is being retired after exceeding max failures.

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[observability](../index.html)::[error_logging](index.html)



# Function log_scrape_error

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/observability/error_logging.rs.html#22-38" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn log_scrape_error<E: Display + ?Sized>(
    error: &E,
    url: &str,
    stage: &str,
    correlation_id: Option<&CorrelationId>,
    context: &str,
)
```

Expand description



Log a structured error with full operational context.

Emits a `tracing::error!` event carrying the error, the URL being processed, the stage where it occurred, and the `trace_id` (when a correlation ID is available) so the error can be correlated with the rest of the operation in a trace file.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `error` - The error to log (any `Display` type).
- `url` - The URL being processed when the error occurred.
- `stage` - The stage/phase where the error occurred (e.g. `"fetch"`, `"extract"`).
- `correlation_id` - Optional correlation ID; its `trace_id` is logged when present.
- `context` - Human-readable context message.














[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[observability](../index.html)::[file_trace_layer](index.html)



# Struct FileTraceLayer

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/observability/file_trace_layer.rs.html#51-56" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct FileTraceLayer { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



A `tracing_subscriber::Layer` that writes JSONL trace files.

Each line is a JSON object with: `timestamp` (RFC3339), `level`, `target`, `span` (name, when inside a span), `trace_id`, `span_id`, `message`, and `fields` (all structured key-value pairs from the event).

When a span closes, an additional record with `"record": "span_close"` is emitted carrying a **top-level** `span_duration_ms` (wall-clock milliseconds from span creation to close), so the `analyze-trace.sh <file> slow` workflow can rank spans by duration.



## Implementations<a href="#implementations" class="anchor">§</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.new" class="fn">new</a>(path: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/path/struct.PathBuf.html" class="struct" title="struct std::path::PathBuf">PathBuf</a>) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/io/error/type.Result.html" class="type" title="type std::io::error::Result">Result</a>\<Self\>





Create a new file trace layer, opening (or creating) the file at `path`.

Parent directories are created automatically. The file is truncated on creation so each run produces a clean trace file.

##### <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns an error if the file cannot be created or opened.

# Function init_console

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/observability/mod.rs.html#35-37" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn init_console()
```

Expand description



Initialize tokio-console for runtime debugging

## <a href="#requires" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Requires

- RUSTFLAGS=“–cfg tokio_unstable” at compile time
- Feature flag `console` enabled

## <a href="#note" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Note

Only available when compiled with `console` feature. Without the feature, this function is a no-op.

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[observability](../index.html)::[logging](index.html)



# Function init_json_logging

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/observability/logging.rs.html#95-101" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn init_json_logging(
    level: &str,
    log_dir: Option<&Path>,
    app_name: &str,
) -> Result<LogGuard>
```

Expand description



Initialize JSON logging with file rotation.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `level` - Log level: “error”, “warn”, “info”, “debug”, “trace”
- `log_dir` - Optional directory for log files. If None, logs to stderr only.
- `app_name` - Application name for log file naming (default: “webfang”)

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

`Ok(LogGuard)` on success - keep this guard alive until program exit. The guard ensures all logs are flushed when dropped.

## <a href="#example" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Example



<a href="#" class="tooltip" title="This example is not tested">ⓘ</a>

``` rust
fn main() {
    let _guard = init_json_logging("info", Some("/var/log"), "myapp").unwrap();
    // ... application runs ...
    // Logs are flushed when _guard is dropped at end of main
}
```

Extended JSON logging with quiet mode and no-color support.

- `quiet` - If true, only warn+ output
- `no_color` - If true, disable ANSI colors
- `log_dir` - Optional directory for log files
- `app_name` - Application name for log file naming

# Struct LogGuard

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/observability/logging.rs.html#20-22" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct LogGuard { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Guard for JSON logging - ensures flush on drop (RAII)

Dropping this guard ensures all pending log writes are flushed to the file before the application exits.

# Function validate_obsidian_input

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/obsidian/uri.rs.html#65-74" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn validate_obsidian_input(
    vault_name: &str,
    file_path: &str,
) -> Result<(), String>
```

Expand description



Validate Obsidian URI inputs, rejecting ASCII control characters.

Shell metacharacters are neutralized by `encode_obsidian_param` (percent-encoded), so they are safe in the URI. Control characters (newline, null byte, etc.) have no legitimate place in a vault name or note path and are rejected outright as a signal of malformed or hostile input.

## <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns `Err` with a user-facing (Spanish) message if either input contains an ASCII control character.

# Function detect_vault

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/obsidian/vault_detector.rs.html#28-34" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn detect_vault(
    cli_path: Option<&Path>,
    env_var: Option<&str>,
    config_path: Option<&str>,
) -> Option<PathBuf>
```

Expand description



Detect an Obsidian vault using priority-ordered search.

## <a href="#search-order" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Search Order

1.  `cli_path` — from CLI `--vault` flag
2.  `OBSIDIAN_VAULT` environment variable
3.  `config_path` — from TOML config `vault_path` field
4.  Official Obsidian registry (`obsidian.json`)
5.  Auto-scan common locations (see `scan_for_vault()`)

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `cli_path` — Optional explicit vault path from CLI
- `env_var` — Optional environment variable name to check (default: “OBSIDIAN_VAULT”)
- `config_path` — Optional vault path from config file

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

`Option<PathBuf>` — The detected vault path, or None if not found














[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[obsidian](../index.html)::[vault_detector](index.html)



# Function detect_vault_with_root

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/obsidian/vault_detector.rs.html#47-80" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn detect_vault_with_root(
    root: Option<&Path>,
    cli_path: Option<&Path>,
    env_var: Option<&str>,
    config_path: Option<&str>,
) -> Option<PathBuf>
```

Expand description



Detect an Obsidian vault with an injectable scan root for hermetic testing.

Behaves identically to [`detect_vault`](fn.detect_vault.html "fn webfang_core::infrastructure::obsidian::vault_detector::detect_vault") except that priority-5 auto-scan uses `root` instead of the process cwd / home directory. Pass `None` for `root` to get the default production behavior.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `root` — Optional root directory for the auto-scan (replaces cwd/home)
- `cli_path` — Optional explicit vault path from CLI
- `env_var` — Optional environment variable name to check (default: “OBSIDIAN_VAULT”)
- `config_path` — Optional vault path from config file

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[obsidian](../index.html)::[vault_reader](index.html)



# Function read_vault_notes

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/obsidian/vault_reader.rs.html#62-94" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn read_vault_notes(
    vault_path: &Path,
) -> Result<Vec<VaultNote>, ScraperError>
```

Expand description



Read all Markdown notes from an Obsidian vault.

Walks the vault directory recursively, collecting every `.md` file while skipping hidden directories (names starting with `.`). Symlinks are followed (Obsidian uses them for template folders).

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `vault_path` — Root directory of the vault (should contain `.obsidian/`)

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

A vector of [`VaultNote`](struct.VaultNote.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::obsidian::vault_reader::VaultNote") for every `.md` file found. An empty vault returns `Ok(vec![])`.

## <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`ScraperError::Io`](../../../error/enum.ScraperError.html#variant.Io "variant webfang_core::error::ScraperError::Io") if the vault directory cannot be read or filesystem metadata is unavailable.

# Function save_results

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/output/file_saver.rs.html#73-88" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn save_results(
    results: &[ScrapedContent],
    output_dir: &Path,
    format: &OutputFormat,
    obsidian: &ObsidianOptions,
) -> Result<()>
```

Expand description



Save scraped results to output directory

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `results` - Scraped content to save
- `output_dir` - Base output directory
- `format` - Output format (Markdown, Text, JSON)
- `obsidian` - Obsidian options (tags, wiki-links, relative assets)

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

- `Ok(())` - Successfully saved
- `Err(ScraperError::Io)` - File system error

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `title` - Article/page title
- `url` - Original URL
- `date` - Publication date (optional, uses current date if None)
- `author` - Author name (optional)
- `excerpt` - Excerpt/summary (optional)
- `tags` - Tags for Obsidian (optional, empty slice for no tags)
- `rich_meta` - Optional rich metadata (word count, reading time, etc.)

YAML string without the surrounding `---` delimiters














[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[persistence](../index.html)::[sqlite](index.html)



# Function create_memory_pool

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/persistence/sqlite.rs.html#119-129" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn create_memory_pool() -> Result<Pool, ScraperError>
```

Expand description



Create a SQLite pool backed by `:memory:` for testing.

Uses a single connection with no WAL pragmas (in-memory databases don’t support WAL mode). The pool **must** be kept alive for the entire test lifetime — dropping the pool closes all connections and destroys the in-memory database.














[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[persistence](../index.html)::[sqlite](index.html)



# Function create_pool

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/persistence/sqlite.rs.html#92-111" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn create_pool(
    db_path: &Path,
    pool_size: usize,
) -> Result<Pool, ScraperError>
```

Expand description



Build a WAL-mode SQLite connection pool backed by \[`deadpool_sqlite`\].

`pool_size` is clamped to at least 1 (the caller — `ElasticConfig` — already applies the frozen `cpu_cores`/floor-4 sizing). The parent directory of `db_path` is created if missing. Per-connection pragmas are applied via a `post_create` hook so every connection honours the WAL-mode contract.

The pool is created lazily — the database file is only materialized on the first \[`Pool::get`\] (i.e. inside [`SqliteVectorRepository::setup_schema`](struct.SqliteVectorRepository.html#method.setup_schema "associated function webfang_core::infrastructure::persistence::sqlite::SqliteVectorRepository::setup_schema")), which is the explicit fail-fast point if the path is not writable.














[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[persistence](../index.html)::[sqlite](index.html)



# Function setup_schema

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/persistence/sqlite.rs.html#603-605" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub async fn setup_schema(pool: &Pool) -> Result<(), ScraperError>
```

Expand description



Free-function alias for [`SqliteVectorRepository::setup_schema`](struct.SqliteVectorRepository.html#method.setup_schema "associated function webfang_core::infrastructure::persistence::sqlite::SqliteVectorRepository::setup_schema") so callers that only hold a `&Pool` (without constructing the repository) can init the schema at startup.

# Struct SqliteVectorRepository

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/persistence/sqlite.rs.html#156-158" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct SqliteVectorRepository { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



SQLite-backed vector repository for the elastic ingestion pipeline.

PR1 provides explicit schema initialization only; the `VectorRepository` trait CRUD (`save_vector`, `get_vector`) and content-hash deduplication land in PR4. Per frozen design decision \#1, schema creation is **explicit** — [`SqliteVectorRepository::setup_schema`](struct.SqliteVectorRepository.html#method.setup_schema "associated function webfang_core::infrastructure::persistence::sqlite::SqliteVectorRepository::setup_schema") MUST be called at startup. There is no implicit schema creation on first connection.

#### pub fn <a href="#method.new" class="fn">new</a>(pool: Pool) -\> Self





Wrap an existing pool. The pool should already have had [`setup_schema`](fn.setup_schema.html "fn webfang_core::infrastructure::persistence::sqlite::setup_schema") run against it.





<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/persistence/sqlite.rs.html#173-176" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.from_memory" class="fn">from_memory</a>() -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<Self, <a href="../../../error/enum.ScraperError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError">ScraperError</a>\>





Create a repository backed by an in-memory SQLite database.

Intended for integration tests — no disk I/O, automatic cleanup on drop. Does **not** call [`setup_schema`](fn.setup_schema.html "fn webfang_core::infrastructure::persistence::sqlite::setup_schema"); the caller must do that explicitly if tables are needed.





<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/persistence/sqlite.rs.html#180-182" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.pool" class="fn">pool</a>(&self) -\> &Pool





Borrow the underlying pool (used by PR2+ wiring and tests).





<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/persistence/sqlite.rs.html#193-203" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub async fn <a href="#method.setup_schema" class="fn">setup_schema</a>(pool: &Pool) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.unit.html" class="primitive">()</a>, <a href="../../../error/enum.ScraperError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError">ScraperError</a>\>





Explicitly initialize the database schema (tables + indexes).

**MUST** be called once at startup (frozen design decision \#1). Acquires a pooled connection — which also materializes the database file and runs the per-connection pragmas via the `post_create` hook — making this the fail-fast point if the configured `db_path` is not writable.

The DDL is idempotent (`CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS`), so calling it on an already-initialized database is a safe no-op.

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[scraper](../index.html)::[author_extractor](index.html)



# Function extract_author

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/scraper/author_extractor.rs.html#193-214" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn extract_author(
    html: &str,
    legible_byline: Option<&str>,
) -> Option<String>
```

Expand description



Try each extraction strategy in order, returning the first successful result. Falls back to the legible byline when no strategy matches.

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `html` - Full raw HTML of the page (must include `<head>` for meta/JSON-LD)
- `legible_byline` - Byline produced by readability, used as last resort

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

- `Some(author)` - The first non-empty author found
- `None` - No strategy matched and no byline was supplied

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/scraper/dom_inspector.rs.html#46-49" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct DefaultDomInspector { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Default DOM inspector — walks the DOM tree and computes similarity scores.

Uses `scraper` for DOM traversal and `strsim::jaro_winkler` for similarity. Node-count cap prevents hangs on very large DOMs (default: 10,000).

# Struct NoOpInspector

``` rust
pub struct NoOpInspector;
```

Expand description



No-op DOM inspector — returns empty reports with zero overhead.

Null Object pattern: used when diagnostics are not needed (non-MCP paths or when an inspector is not configured in `McpState`).

Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left` is `true`. where F: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html" class="trait" title="trait core::ops::function::FnOnce">FnOnce</a>(&Self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>,







Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left(&self)` returns `true`. Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right "variant either::Either::Right") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") otherwise. [Read more](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/into_either/trait.IntoEither.html#method.into_either_with)

[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[scraper](../index.html)::[fallback](index.html)



# Function extract_text

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/scraper/fallback.rs.html#20-29" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn extract_text(html: &str) -> String
```

Expand description



Extract text without Readability (basic HTML stripping)

This is used when Readability fails to parse the HTML. It uses htmd for conversion, falling back to basic line filtering.

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::infrastructure::scraper::fallback::extract_text;

let html = "<html><body><p>Hello World</p></body></html>";
let text = extract_text(html);
assert!(text.contains("Hello World"));
```
















[webfang_core](../../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../../index.html)::[scraper](../index.html)::[readability](index.html)



# Function parse

<a href="../../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/scraper/readability.rs.html#47-59" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn parse(html: &str, url: Option<&str>) -> Result<Article>
```

Expand description



Parse HTML using Readability algorithm

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `html` - HTML content to parse
- `url` - Optional URL for relative link resolution

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

- `Ok(Article)` - Parsed article with extracted content
- `Err(ScraperError::Extraction)` - If Readability fails

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::infrastructure::scraper::readability::parse;

let html = "<html><body><article><h1>Title</h1><p>Content</p></article></body></html>";
let article = parse(html, Some("https://example.com")).unwrap();
// Title may vary depending on legible's heuristic parsing
assert!(!article.title.is_empty());
```

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../index.html)::[stream](index.html)



# Struct StreamRepository

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/stream/mod.rs.html#74-85" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct StreamRepository { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



Headless vector sink that writes [`VectorRecord`](struct.VectorRecord.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::stream::VectorRecord") lines to a JSONL stream.

Construct with [`StreamRepository::new`](struct.StreamRepository.html#method.new "associated function webfang_core::infrastructure::stream::StreamRepository::new"); `"-"` selects stdout (buffered), any other path selects a file.



## Implementations<a href="#implementations" class="anchor">§</a>

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/stream/mod.rs.html#96-98" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### pub fn <a href="#method.new" class="fn">new</a>(path: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<Self, <a href="../../error/enum.ScraperError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_core::error::ScraperError">ScraperError</a>\>





Open the JSONL sink with the system clock.

- `path == "-"` → buffered stdout.
- otherwise → a file created (truncated) at `path`.

##### <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns [`ScraperError::Io`](../../error/enum.ScraperError.html#variant.Io "variant webfang_core::error::ScraperError::Io") if the file cannot be created.

Returns [`ScraperError::Io`](../../error/enum.ScraperError.html#variant.Io "variant webfang_core::error::ScraperError::Io") if the file cannot be created.

[webfang_core](../../index.html)::[infrastructure](../index.html)::[stream](index.html)



# Struct VectorRecord

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/stream/mod.rs.html#51-68" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct VectorRecord {
    pub url: String,
    pub sha256_hex: String,
    pub title: Option<String>,
    pub chunk_text: String,
    pub embedding: Vec<f32>,
    pub metadata: Value,
    pub timestamp: String,
}
```

Expand description



A single JSONL vector record emitted by [`StreamRepository`](struct.StreamRepository.html "struct webfang_core::infrastructure::stream::StreamRepository").

Mirrors the fields surfaced by the elastic ingestion pipeline: the source URL, the content `sha256_hex` (content-hash dedup key), an optional title, the cleaned `chunk_text`, the raw `embedding` vector, arbitrary `metadata`, and an RFC3339 `timestamp`.



## Fields<a href="#fields" class="anchor">§</a>

<a href="#structfield.url" class="anchor field">§</a>`url: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>



Source URL the chunk was extracted from.



<a href="#structfield.sha256_hex" class="anchor field">§</a>`sha256_hex: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>



Content hash (SHA-256 hex) of the resource — the dedup key.



<a href="#structfield.title" class="anchor field">§</a>`title: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/option/enum.Option.html" class="enum" title="enum core::option::Option"><code>Option</code></a>`<`<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>`>`



Best-effort title (first ≤200 chars of the first chunk line), or `null`.



<a href="#structfield.chunk_text" class="anchor field">§</a>`chunk_text: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>



Cleaned chunk text.



<a href="#structfield.embedding" class="anchor field">§</a>`embedding: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec"><code>Vec</code></a>`<`<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.f32.html" class="primitive"><code>f32</code></a>`>`



Raw embedding vector (e.g. 384 floats for all-MiniLM-L6-v2). Empty only when the record would have been omitted (Q3).



<a href="#structfield.metadata" class="anchor field">§</a>`metadata: `<a href="https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html" class="enum" title="enum serde_json::value::Value"><code>Value</code></a>



Optional arbitrary metadata (reserved for future use).



<a href="#structfield.timestamp" class="anchor field">§</a>`timestamp: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>



RFC3339 timestamp of emission.

Converts `self` into a [`Left`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Left "variant either::Either::Left") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") if `into_left` is `true`. where F: <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html" class="trait" title="trait core::ops::function::FnOnce">FnOnce</a>(&Self) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.bool.html" class="primitive">bool</a>,

Converts `self` into a [`Right`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html#variant.Right "variant either::Either::Right") variant of [`Either<Self, Self>`](https://docs.rs/either/1/either/enum.Either.html "enum either::Either") otherwise. # Function get_random_user_agent_from_pool

<a href="../../../src/webfang_core/infrastructure/user_agent.rs.html#231-235" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub fn get_random_user_agent_from_pool(pool: &[String]) -> String
```

Expand description



Get a random user agent from pool

## <a href="#arguments" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `pool` - Slice of user agent strings

## <a href="#returns" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

A randomly selected user agent string

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::infrastructure::user_agent::get_random_user_agent_from_pool;

let agents = vec!["Chrome/131".to_string(), "Firefox/123".to_string()];
let ua = get_random_user_agent_from_pool(&agents);
assert!(ua == "Chrome/131" || ua == "Firefox/123");
```

##### <a href="#errors" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Errors

Returns fallback agents if:

- Cache read fails
- API download fails
- Cache is older than 1 year

# API: webfang_ai







# Crate webfang_ai

<a href="../src/webfang_ai/lib.rs.html#1-27" class="src">Source</a> 



Expand description



WebFang AI — ONNX-based semantic cleaning

Provides AI-powered content cleaning using sentence-transformers models. Depends on `webfang_core` for domain types.

The ONNX inference stack is gated behind the `ai` feature; without it the crate only re-exports the core domain types.

# Enum SemanticError

<a href="../src/webfang_core/error.rs.html#205" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum SemanticError {
    ModelLoad(Error),
    Tokenize(String),
    Inference(String),
    ChunkTooLarge {
        chunk_id: String,
        tokens: usize,
        max: usize,
    },
    Download {
        repo: String,
        cause: String,
    },
    CacheValidation {
        repo: String,
        expected: String,
        actual: String,
    },
    OfflineMode {
        repo: String,
    },
    InvalidThreshold {
        value: f32,
    },
}
```

Expand description



Semantic cleaning errors (AI/ML operations)

These errors occur during AI-powered semantic cleaning operations:

- Model loading from cache
- Tokenization of input text
- ONNX inference
- Model download from HuggingFace Hub

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_core::error::SemanticError;
use std::io;

let io_err = io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotFound, "model file missing");
let semantic_err = SemanticError::ModelLoad(io_err);
assert!(semantic_err.to_string().contains("modelo"));
```





## Variants<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="#variant.ModelLoad" class="anchor">§</a>

### ModelLoad(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/io/error/struct.Error.html" class="struct" title="struct std::io::error::Error">Error</a>)





Failed to load ONNX model from cache

This occurs when:

- Model file doesn’t exist in cache
- Model file is corrupted
- Memory mapping failed (disk full, permissions)





<a href="#variant.Tokenize" class="anchor">§</a>

### Tokenize(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>)





Tokenization failed

This occurs when:

- Input text contains invalid UTF-8
- Text exceeds model’s maximum token limit
- Special characters break tokenizer
- Tokenizer file not found





<a href="#variant.Inference" class="anchor">§</a>

### Inference(<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>)





ONNX inference failed

This occurs when:

- Model graph execution failed
- Input tensor shape mismatch
- Output tensor extraction failed
- Tensor creation failed





<a href="#variant.ChunkTooLarge" class="anchor">§</a>

### ChunkTooLarge





Content chunk exceeds model’s token limit

This occurs when a single chunk of content has more tokens than the model can handle (32768 tokens for Granite-97M).

#### <a href="#fields-1" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Fields

- `chunk_id` - Identifier of the problematic chunk
- `tokens` - Actual token count
- `max` - Maximum allowed tokens





#### Fields



<a href="#variant.ChunkTooLarge.field.chunk_id" class="anchor field">§</a>`chunk_id: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>



Identifier of the chunk (UUID or index)







<a href="#variant.ChunkTooLarge.field.tokens" class="anchor field">§</a>`tokens: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.usize.html" class="primitive"><code>usize</code></a>



Actual token count







<a href="#variant.ChunkTooLarge.field.max" class="anchor field">§</a>`max: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.usize.html" class="primitive"><code>usize</code></a>



Maximum allowed tokens for this model









<a href="#variant.Download" class="anchor">§</a>

### Download





Model download failed from HuggingFace Hub

This occurs when:

- Network error during download
- Repository doesn’t exist or is private
- Authentication required
- SHA256 validation failed after download





#### Fields



<a href="#variant.Download.field.repo" class="anchor field">§</a>`repo: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>



HuggingFace repository (e.g., “sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2”)







<a href="#variant.Download.field.cause" class="anchor field">§</a>`cause: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>



Underlying error cause









<a href="#variant.CacheValidation" class="anchor">§</a>

### CacheValidation





Cache validation failed (SHA256 mismatch)

This occurs when:

- Downloaded file is corrupted
- Cache was modified externally
- Incomplete download





#### Fields



<a href="#variant.CacheValidation.field.repo" class="anchor field">§</a>`repo: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>



HuggingFace repository







<a href="#variant.CacheValidation.field.expected" class="anchor field">§</a>`expected: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>



Expected SHA256 hash







<a href="#variant.CacheValidation.field.actual" class="anchor field">§</a>`actual: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>



Actual SHA256 hash of downloaded file









<a href="#variant.OfflineMode" class="anchor">§</a>

### OfflineMode





Offline mode: model not available in cache

This occurs when:

- Application is in offline mode
- Model is not cached
- Cannot download from HuggingFace Hub





#### Fields



<a href="#variant.OfflineMode.field.repo" class="anchor field">§</a>`repo: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String"><code>String</code></a>



HuggingFace repository









<a href="#variant.InvalidThreshold" class="anchor">§</a>

### InvalidThreshold





Relevance threshold out of valid range \[0.0, 1.0\]

This occurs when:

- User provides a threshold outside the valid range
- Programmatic API receives an invalid threshold value





#### Fields



<a href="#variant.InvalidThreshold.field.value" class="anchor field">§</a>`value: `<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.f32.html" class="primitive"><code>f32</code></a>



The invalid threshold value provided

# Enum AiModel

<a href="../../../src/webfang_ai/infrastructure_ai/cache_config.rs.html#39-45" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum AiModel {
    Granite97M,
    Granite311M,
}
```

Expand description



AI model variants supported by the inference engine

Two-tier model architecture:

- `Granite97M` (default): 97M params, 384d native, ~120MB, fast
- `Granite311M`: 311M params, 768d native (Matryoshka→384d), ~350MB, higher quality

Both produce 384-dimensional embeddings for unified storage schema.



## Variants<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="#variant.Granite97M" class="anchor">§</a>

### Granite97M





IBM Granite-97M (384d native, ~120MB, default)





<a href="#variant.Granite311M" class="anchor">§</a>

### Granite311M





IBM Granite-311M (768d native, Matryoshka-truncated to 384d, ~350MB)

# Struct ChunkId

<a href="../../../src/webfang_ai/infrastructure_ai/chunk_id.rs.html#18" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct ChunkId(pub u64);
```

Expand description



Unique identifier for a content chunk

Newtype pattern (`type-newtype-ids` rust-skill) for type safety. Prevents mixing chunk IDs with other u64 values at compile time.

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_ai::ChunkId;

let id = ChunkId(42);
assert_eq!(format!("{}", id), "chunk-42");
```

# Struct HtmlChunker

<a href="../../../src/webfang_ai/infrastructure_ai/chunker.rs.html#40-47" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub struct HtmlChunker { /* private fields */ }
```

Expand description



HTML chunker

Chunks HTML content into semantic segments using a two-pass approach:

1.  **Structural boundaries**: Split by paragraphs and HTML elements
2.  **Size-based merge/split**: Merge small chunks, split large ones

## <a href="#examples" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_ai::HtmlChunker;

let chunker = HtmlChunker::new();
let html = "<article><p>First paragraph.</p><p>Second paragraph.</p></article>";
let chunks = chunker.chunk(html)?;

println!("Generated {} chunks", chunks.len());
```

#### pub fn <a href="#method.chunk" class="fn">chunk</a>(&self, html: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>\<<a href="../../struct.DocumentChunk.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_ai::DocumentChunk">DocumentChunk</a>\>, <a href="../../enum.SemanticError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_ai::SemanticError">SemanticError</a>\>





Chunk HTML into semantic segments

##### <a href="#arguments-1" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `html` - The HTML content to chunk

##### <a href="#returns-1" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

A result containing:

- `Ok(Vec<DocumentChunk>)` - Successfully chunked content
- `Err(SemanticError)` - Chunking failed

##### <a href="#process" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Process

1.  **Strip HTML tags**: Extract plain text
2.  **Split by structural boundaries**: Paragraphs, sentences
3.  **Merge small chunks**: Combine chunks below min_chunk_size
4.  **Split large chunks**: Break chunks above max_chunk_size

##### <a href="#examples-1" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Examples



``` rust
use webfang_ai::HtmlChunker;

let chunker = HtmlChunker::new();
let html = "<article><p>Hello World</p><p>Second paragraph</p></article>";
let chunks = chunker.chunk(html)?;
```

#### pub fn <a href="#method.chunk_text" class="fn">chunk_text</a>( &self, text: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>, url: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>, title: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>, ) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/core/result/enum.Result.html" class="enum" title="enum core::result::Result">Result</a>\<<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::vec::Vec">Vec</a>\<<a href="../../struct.DocumentChunk.html" class="struct" title="struct webfang_ai::DocumentChunk">DocumentChunk</a>\>, <a href="../../enum.SemanticError.html" class="enum" title="enum webfang_ai::SemanticError">SemanticError</a>\>





Chunk text (non-HTML) into semantic segments

Similar to `chunk()` but skips HTML tag stripping.

##### <a href="#arguments-2" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Arguments

- `text` - The plain text to chunk
- `url` - Source URL for metadata
- `title` - Title for metadata

##### <a href="#returns-2" class="doc-anchor">§</a>Returns

A result containing the chunked content

[webfang_ai](../../index.html)::[infrastructure_ai](../index.html)::[content_pruner](index.html)



# Enum PruneAggressiveness

<a href="../../../src/webfang_ai/infrastructure_ai/content_pruner.rs.html#12-20" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub enum PruneAggressiveness {
    Gentle,
    Standard,
    Aggressive,
}
```

Expand description



Aggressiveness level for content pruning.

Controls how aggressively `legible` strips non-content elements.



## Variants<a href="#variants" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="#variant.Gentle" class="anchor">§</a>

### Gentle





Minimal pruning — keep most structural elements.





<a href="#variant.Standard" class="anchor">§</a>

### Standard





Standard pruning — remove nav, sidebar, ads, footer (default).





<a href="#variant.Aggressive" class="anchor">§</a>

### Aggressive





Aggressive pruning — extract only the core article text.

Content pruner backed by the `legible` crate (Mozilla Readability port).

# Trait ContentPruner

<a href="../../../src/webfang_ai/infrastructure_ai/content_pruner.rs.html#26-35" class="src">Source</a> 



``` rust
pub trait ContentPruner: Sealed {
    // Required methods
    fn prune(&self, html: &str) -> String;
    fn aggressiveness(&self) -> PruneAggressiveness;
}
```

Expand description



Sealed trait for content pruning implementations.

Only implementors within this module can implement this trait. External crates cannot add new pruning strategies.



## Required Methods<a href="#required-methods" class="anchor">§</a>





<a href="../../../src/webfang_ai/infrastructure_ai/content_pruner.rs.html#31" class="src rightside">Source</a>

#### fn <a href="#tymethod.prune" class="fn">prune</a>(&self, html: &<a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/std/primitive.str.html" class="primitive">str</a>) -\> <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.88.0/alloc/string/struct.String.html" class="struct" title="struct alloc::string::String">String</a>





Prune HTML content by extracting the readable main content.

Returns the pruned HTML string. On failure or empty input, returns the original HTML unchanged (fallback behavior).





<a href="../../../src/webfang_ai/infrastructure_ai/content_pruner.rs.html#34" class="src rightside">Source</a>
